column3: A mild, spoken cry for a slip or a small surprise, often on noticing your own mistake: 哎呀，忘了！ For a sharp hurt, 哎哟 is the cry.
column6: Āiyā, wǒ wàng le dài yàoshi!
column7: Oh no, I forgot my keys!
column9: A mild, spoken cry for a slip or a small surprise, often on noticing your own mistake: 哎呀，忘了！ For a sharp hurt, 哎喲 is the cry.

column3: The cry for a bump or sudden pain, and a soft protest too: 哎哟，不要这样啦. 哎呀 is more the dismay of a slip; 哎哟 is more bodily.
column6: Āiyō, wǒ de jiǎo hǎo tòng!
column7: Ow, my foot really hurts!
column9: The cry for a bump or sudden pain, and a soft protest too: 哎喲，不要這樣啦. 哎呀 is more the dismay of a slip; 哎喲 is more bodily.

column3: The general name; the organ goes before 癌 for a particular kind: 肺癌, 胃癌. You 得癌症 'get cancer', and a patient is a 癌症病人.
column6: Tā de bàba dé le áizhèng.
column7: His father has cancer.
column9: The general name; the organ goes before 癌 for a particular kind: 肺癌, 胃癌. You 得癌症 'get cancer', and a patient is a 癌症病人.

column3: Mostly the last part of a compound naming the organ: 肺癌, 胃癌, 肝癌, 乳癌, and 癌细胞. For the disease in general, say 癌症. It used to be read yán, exactly like 岩; the reading changed to ái in 1962 so that 癌 would not sound like 炎 'inflammation'.
column4: 他爸爸得了癌，要住院治疗。
column5: 他爸爸得了癌，要住院治療。
column6: Tā bàba dé le ái, yào zhùyuàn zhìliáo.
column7: His father has cancer and has to be hospitalized.
column9: Mostly the last part of a compound naming the organ: 肺癌, 胃癌, 肝癌, 乳癌, and 癌細胞. For the disease in general, say 癌症. It used to be read yán, exactly like 岩; the reading changed to ái in 1962 so that 癌 would not sound like 炎 'inflammation'.

column3: Mostly the end of a compound: a case in 破案 and 案件, a plan in 方案, a proposal in 提案, a file in 档案. Alone, speech says 案子.
column6: Zhè ge àn zi hái zài diàochá zhōng.
column7: This case is still under investigation.
column9: Mostly the end of a compound: a case in 破案 and 案件, a plan in 方案, a proposal in 提案, a file in 檔案. Alone, speech says 案子.

column3: The spoken word for a legal or police case; 案件 is the formal one. For a job a firm or freelancer takes on, 接案子 is the Taiwan phrase; the mainland says 项目 or 接活.
column4: 警察正在调查这个案子。
column5: 警察正在調查這個案子。
column6: Jǐngchá zhèngzài diàochá zhè ge ànzi.
column7: The police are investigating this case.
column9: The spoken word for a legal or police case; 案件 is the formal one. For a job a firm or freelancer takes on, 接案子 is the Taiwan phrase; the mainland says 項目 or 接活.

column3: Dirty in sight and in morals: 肮脏的厕所, but also 肮脏的手段 and 肮脏的钱. Stronger than 不干净, which only says 'not clean'.
column6: Zhè tiáo hé de shuǐ hěn āngzāng.
column7: The water of this river is very dirty.
column9: Dirty in sight and in morals: 骯髒的廁所, but also 骯髒的手段 and 骯髒的錢. Stronger than 不乾淨, which only says 'not clean'.

column3: Goes before the verb and tells that the doer is not seen: 暗中帮忙, 暗中观察. It can be a kind deed done quietly or a sly one, and the verb shows which.
column6: Tā ànzhōng bāng le wǒ hěn duō máng.
column7: He helped me a lot in secret.
column9: Goes before the verb and tells that the doer is not seen: 暗中幫忙, 暗中觀察. It can be a kind deed done quietly or a sly one, and the verb shows which.

column3: The word for getting through a hard stretch of time: 熬夜 'stay up late' (with a sense of strain), 熬过去 'get through it'. In the kitchen it is slow simmering: 熬汤, 熬粥.
column6: Tā áo le yī yè, jīntiān hěn lèi.
column7: He stayed up all night and is tired today.
column9: The word for getting through a hard stretch of time: 熬夜 'stay up late' (with a sense of strain), 熬過去 'get through it'. In the kitchen it is slow simmering: 熬湯, 熬粥.

column3: A verb that holds its own object, so it can be split: 罢了三天工. It is also a noun: 工人罢工, 罢工抗议. Common in news.
column6: Gōngrén juédìng míngtiān bàgōng.
column7: The workers decided to strike tomorrow.
column9: A verb that holds its own object, so it can be split: 罷了三天工. It is also a noun: 工人罷工, 罷工抗議. Common in news.

column3: Followed by the one you honor: 拜神, 拜祖先, 拜师 'take someone as your teacher'. It is also a polite opener before some verbs: 拜访 'pay a visit', 拜托 'ask a favor'.
column4: 他拜了一位老师学书法。
column5: 他拜了一位老師學書法。
column6: Tā bài le yī wèi lǎoshī xué shūfǎ.
column7: He took a teacher to study calligraphy.
column9: Followed by the one you honor: 拜神, 拜祖先, 拜師 'take someone as your teacher'. It is also a polite opener before some verbs: 拜訪 'pay a visit', 拜託 'ask a favor'.

column3: In Taiwan, the ceremony of offerings to the gods, at home or in a temple: 拜拜用的水果, 初一十五拜拜. It is also the casual 'bye-bye', said everywhere, and the situation tells the two apart.
column4: 妈妈每个月初一都要拜拜。
column5: 媽媽每個月初一都要拜拜。
column6: Māma měi ge yuè chūyī dōu yào bàibai.
column7: Mom does the offering ceremony on the first of every month.
column9: In Taiwan, the ceremony of offerings to the gods, at home or in a temple: 拜拜用的水果, 初一十五拜拜. It is also the casual 'bye-bye', said everywhere, and the situation tells the two apart.

column3: Done in person in the first days of the new year: 去亲戚家拜年, 向长辈拜年. Children usually get a 红包 from the elders they greet.
column4: 大年初一我们去外婆家拜年。
column5: 大年初一我們去外婆家拜年。
column6: Dànián chūyī wǒmen qù wàipó jiā bàinián.
column7: On New Year's Day we go to Grandma's to pay our New Year call.
column9: Done in person in the first days of the new year: 去親戚家拜年, 向長輩拜年. Children usually get a 紅包 from the elders they greet.

column3: Put before the favor you ask: 拜托你帮我一个忙. Said alone it is also impatience, 'come on': 拜托，别再说了！ It is earnest and familiar, common among friends; to a stranger, 请 or 麻烦你 is the usual request.
column6: Bàituō nǐ bāng wǒ ná yīxià shū.
column7: Please help me carry the book for a moment.
column9: Put before the favor you ask: 拜託你幫我一個忙. Said alone it is also impatience, 'come on': 拜託，別再說了！ It is earnest and familiar, common among friends; to a stranger, 請 or 麻煩你 is the usual request.

column3: Ends a sentence and plays it down, 'that's all', often after 只是 or 不过: 我只是开玩笑罢了.
column6: Wǒ zhǐshì suíbiàn shuōshuo bàle.
column7: I was only saying it casually, that's all.
column9: Ends a sentence and plays it down, 'that's all', often after 只是 or 不過: 我只是開玩笑罷了.

column3: For mixing food with a sauce or dressing by hand or spoon: 拌饭, 拌面, 拌沙拉, and 凉拌 for cold dressed dishes. In compound 搅拌 it is stirring.
column4: 他把酱油和饭拌在一起。
column5: 他把醬油和飯拌在一起。
column6: Tā bǎ jiàngyóu hé fàn bàn zài yīqǐ.
column7: He mixed the soy sauce with the rice.
column9: For mixing food with a sauce or dressing by hand or spoon: 拌飯, 拌麵, 拌沙拉, and 涼拌 for cold dressed dishes. In compound 攪拌 it is stirring.

column3: Mostly in 一般 and in the written pattern 像…一般 or 如…一般 'just like': 像梦一般. In speech, 一样 does the same job.
column4: 她的声音像音乐一般好听。
column5: 她的聲音像音樂一般好聽。
column6: Tā de shēngyīn xiàng yīnyuè yī bān hǎotīng.
column7: Her voice is as lovely as music.
column9: Mostly in 一般 and in the written pattern 像…一般 or 如…一般 'just like': 像夢一般. In speech, 一樣 does the same job.

column3: Counts pounds: 一磅牛排. As a verb it means to weigh something on a scale, and 磅秤 is a platform scale. Everyday weights are in 公斤 or 斤 instead. It was borrowed from English 'pound'.
column6: Zhè kuài niúpái yǒu yī bàng zhòng.
column7: This steak weighs a pound.
column9: Counts pounds: 一磅牛排. As a verb it means to weigh something on a scale, and 磅秤 is a platform scale. Everyday weights are in 公斤 or 斤 instead. It was borrowed from English 'pound'.

column3: Spoken, for a thick stick you can hold: 一根棒子. Avoid it for people: as slang on the mainland it is a rude word for Koreans. 棒 on its own can mean 'wonderful'. That sense may have developed from 'stick' to 'hard' to 'excellent'.
column6: Tā shǒu lǐ názhe yī gēn bàngzi.
column7: He holds a stick in his hand.
column9: Spoken, for a thick stick you can hold: 一根棒子. Avoid it for people: as slang on the mainland it is a rude word for Koreans. 棒 on its own can mean 'wonderful'. That sense may have developed from 'stick' to 'hard' to 'excellent'.

column3: A verb with the place before it: 在公司办公, 在家办公 'work from home'. It names desk and administrative work, and gives 办公室 'office' and 办公时间 'office hours'.
column6: Tā měitiān zài zhèlǐ bàngōng.
column7: He works here in this office every day.
column9: A verb with the place before it: 在公司辦公, 在家辦公 'work from home'. It names desk and administrative work, and gives 辦公室 'office' and 辦公時間 'office hours'.

column3: The stretch just before dark, after 下午. It is a time word, so it needs no 在 and often opens the sentence: 傍晚时分, 傍晚下起了雨.
column4: 傍晚我们常常去公园散步。
column5: 傍晚我們常常去公園散步。
column6: Bàngwǎn wǒmen chángcháng qù gōngyuán sànbù.
column7: Toward evening we often go for a walk in the park.
column9: The stretch just before dark, after 下午. It is a time word, so it needs no 在 and often opens the sentence: 傍晚時分, 傍晚下起了雨.

column3: Usually 在半路上 or 半路 plus an event: 半路下车 'get off midway', 半路遇到. Also for stopping something partway: 半路退出 'drop out partway'.
column4: 我在半路上遇到了老同学。
column5: 我在半路上遇到了老同學。
column6: Wǒ zài bànlù shàng yùdào le lǎo tóngxué.
column7: I met an old classmate halfway there.
column9: Usually 在半路上 or 半路 plus an event: 半路下車 'get off midway', 半路遇到. Also for stopping something partway: 半路退出 'drop out partway'.

column3: Half of a count of people or items, in news, votes and surveys: 超过半数, 半数以上. For half of one thing, such as a cake, 一半 is the word.
column4: 超过半数的人同意这个办法。
column5: 超過半數的人同意這個辦法。
column6: Chāoguò bànshù de rén tóngyì zhège bànfǎ.
column7: More than half of the people agree to this method.
column9: Half of a count of people or items, in news, votes and surveys: 超過半數, 半數以上. For half of one thing, such as a cake, 一半 is the word.

column3: The work of moving goods by hand or truck: 搬运货物, and a 搬运工 is a porter or mover. 运输 is the bigger, formal word for freight across distances.
column6: Gōngrén zhèngzài bānyùn huòwù.
column7: The workers are moving the goods.
column9: The work of moving goods by hand or truck: 搬運貨物, and a 搬運工 is a porter or mover. 運輸 is the bigger, formal word for freight across distances.

column3: A verb that holds its object, so 报了仇 works. The person you avenge comes after 为: 为父亲报仇. Mostly serious, found in stories and news; 报仇雪恨 is the full phrase.
column6: Tā xiǎng wèi péngyou bàochóu.
column7: He wants to take revenge for his friend.
column9: A verb that holds its object, so 報了仇 works. The person you avenge comes after 為: 為父親報仇. Mostly serious, found in stories and news; 報仇雪恨 is the full phrase.

column3: Both the verb and the noun: 新闻报导, 根据报导 'as reported', 被报导 'be reported'.
column4: 这件事已经被媒体报导了。
column5: 這件事已經被媒體報導了。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì yǐjīng bèi méitǐ bàodǎo le.
column7: This matter has already been reported by the media.
column9: Both the verb and the noun: 新聞報導, 根據報導 'as reported', 被報導 'be reported'.

column3: A noun, 使用暴力, 家庭暴力, and also an adjective with 很: 这部电影很暴力. The same 暴 'violent, sudden' is in 暴雨 and 暴躁. The earliest form of 暴, seen on oracle bones, put a tiger and a weapon together to mean violence.
column6: Wǒmen fǎnduì yīqiè bàolì.
column7: We oppose all violence.
column9: A noun, 使用暴力, 家庭暴力, and also an adjective with 很: 這部電影很暴力. The same 暴 'violent, sudden' is in 暴雨 and 暴躁. The earliest form of 暴, seen on oracle bones, put a tiger and a weapon together to mean violence.

column3: A polite, lighter apology, often opening a request, a refusal or bad news: 抱歉打扰你. For a real wrong done to someone, 对不起 is the stronger 'I'm sorry'.
column6: Hěn bàoqiàn, wǒ lái wǎn le.
column7: I'm very sorry, I'm late.
column9: A polite, lighter apology, often opening a request, a refusal or bad news: 抱歉打擾你. For a real wrong done to someone, 對不起 is the stronger 'I'm sorry'.

column3: The company with its reporters and editors, where you 在报社工作. The paper you read is 报纸. 社 is an organization in 出版社 and 旅行社 too.
column6: Tā zài yī jiā bàoshè dāng jìzhě.
column7: He works as a reporter at a newspaper.
column9: The company with its reporters and editors, where you 在報社工作. The paper you read is 報紙. 社 is an organization in 出版社 and 旅行社 too.

column3: About a person's temper, mostly as 脾气暴躁, quick to flare up. 急躁 is only hasty and impatient, with no anger in it.
column6: Bàba zuìjìn píqì hěn bàozào.
column7: Dad has been very short-tempered lately.
column9: About a person's temper, mostly as 脾氣暴躁, quick to flare up. 急躁 is only hasty and impatient, with no anger in it.

column3: For bombs, factories and gas leaks: 发生爆炸. It is figurative too, as in 人口爆炸 'population explosion'.
column6: Gōngchǎng zuótiān fāshēng le bàozhà.
column7: An explosion happened at the factory yesterday.
column9: For bombs, factories and gas leaks: 發生爆炸. It is figurative too, as in 人口爆炸 'population explosion'.

column3: Formal, common in news and law; what is protected is a right or an interest: 保障人权, 保障安全. Also a noun: 社会保障, 劳工的保障. In the oracle script 保 showed a person carrying a child on his back, and carrying a child grew into 'to protect'.
column4: 政府要保障人民的安全。
column5: 政府要保障人民的安全。
column6: Zhèngfǔ yào bǎozhàng rénmín de ānquán.
column7: The government must guarantee the safety of its people.
column9: Formal, common in news and law; what is protected is a right or an interest: 保障人權, 保障安全. Also a noun: 社會保障, 勞工的保障. In the oracle script 保 showed a person carrying a child on his back, and carrying a child grew into 'to protect'.

column3: Mostly in compounds: 准备, 设备, 备用 'spare', 备份 'backup'. Alone it is written, usually with a result, as in 备好 and 备齐 'get ready'.
column6: Chūmén qián yào bèi hǎo yǔsǎn.
column7: Get an umbrella ready before going out.
column9: Mostly in compounds: 準備, 設備, 備用 'spare', 備份 'backup'. Alone it is written, usually with a result, as in 備好 and 備齊 'get ready'.

column3: The back of something flat, the side you do not see first: a sheet of paper, a photo, a card. The opposite is 正面.
column4: 请把名字写在纸的背面。
column5: 請把名字寫在紙的背面。
column6: Qǐng bǎ míngzi xiě zài zhǐ de bèimiàn.
column7: Please write your name on the back of the paper.
column9: The back of something flat, the side you do not see first: a sheet of paper, a photo, a card. The opposite is 正面.

column3: Serious and written, for grief over a death or a disaster: 悲痛的心情, 表示悲痛. For ordinary sadness, speech says 难过.
column4: 听到这个消息，大家都很悲痛。
column5: 聽到這個消息，大家都很悲痛。
column6: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, dàjiā dōu hěn bēitòng.
column7: On hearing the news, everyone was deeply grieved.
column9: Serious and written, for grief over a death or a disaster: 悲痛的心情, 表示悲痛. For ordinary sadness, speech says 難過.

column3: Covers sleeveless undershirts, sports tops and vests alike: 运动背心, 防弹背心 'bulletproof vest'. The measure word is 件.
column6: Xiàtiān tā xǐhuan chuān bèixīn.
column7: In summer he likes to wear a tank top.
column9: Covers sleeveless undershirts, sports tops and vests alike: 運動背心, 防彈背心 'bulletproof vest'. The measure word is 件.

column3: A lively, written verb, mostly in compounds: 奔跑, 奔走 'run about on errands', 奔流. Before a place it means to head for it: 奔向未来.
column4: 他奔向车站，想赶上最后一班车。
column5: 他奔向車站，想趕上最後一班車。
column6: Tā bēn xiàng chēzhàn, xiǎng gǎn shàng zuìhòu yī bān chē.
column7: He ran toward the station, hoping to catch the last train.
column9: A lively, written verb, mostly in compounds: 奔跑, 奔走 'run about on errands', 奔流. Before a place it means to head for it: 奔向未來.

column3: A vivid word for running with energy, for children, animals and athletes: 在草地上奔跑. Jogging for exercise is 跑步, and 跑 alone is the plain everyday 'run'.
column6: Háizimen zài cǎodì shàng bēnpǎo.
column7: The children are running about on the grass.
column9: A vivid word for running with energy, for children, animals and athletes: 在草地上奔跑. Jogging for exercise is 跑步, and 跑 alone is the plain everyday 'run'.

column3: Follows the noun it stresses: 问题本身, 他本身就是医生. It is not 'myself', as in doing something on your own; for that, use 自己.
column6: Wèntí běnshēn bìng bù nán.
column7: The problem itself is not hard.
column9: Follows the noun it stresses: 問題本身, 他本身就是醫生. It is not 'myself', as in doing something on your own; for that, use 自己.

column3: What is homegrown rather than foreign: 本土文化, 本土品牌, 本土化 'localization'. In Taiwan it is also a word of identity, warm toward what belongs to Taiwan itself.
column4: 这是一家很有本土特色的餐厅。
column5: 這是一家很有本土特色的餐廳。
column6: Zhè shì yī jiā hěn yǒu běntǔ tèsè de cāntīng.
column7: This is a restaurant with a strong local character.
column9: What is homegrown rather than foreign: 本土文化, 本土品牌, 本土化 'localization'. In Taiwan it is also a word of identity, warm toward what belongs to Taiwan itself.

column3: Said of things that are both big and heavy and awkward to move: 笨重的行李, 笨重的机器. For weight alone, 重 is enough; for a person, 笨 alone means 'stupid'.
column6: Zhège xiāngzi yòu dà yòu bènzhòng.
column7: This box is both large and bulky.
column9: Said of things that are both big and heavy and awkward to move: 笨重的行李, 笨重的機器. For weight alone, 重 is enough; for a person, 笨 alone means 'stupid'.

column3: For eyes and mouths: 闭上眼睛, 闭嘴. For doors and windows, speech says 关; 闭 shows up in 关闭, 闭幕 'close an event' and 封闭.
column6: Qǐng bì shàng yǎnjing xiǎng yī xiǎng.
column7: Please close your eyes and think about it.
column9: For eyes and mouths: 閉上眼睛, 閉嘴. For doors and windows, speech says 關; 閉 shows up in 關閉, 閉幕 'close an event' and 封閉.

column3: Common in 方便 and 随便; in writing it also stands for 就 'then': 一听便懂. It is 'informal' in 便服 and 便饭.
column6: Tā yī tīng biàn míngbai le.
column7: He understood as soon as he heard it.
column9: Common in 方便 and 隨便; in writing it also stands for 就 'then': 一聽便懂. It is 'informal' in 便服 and 便飯.

column3: Flat in the sense of squashed, of what should be round or thick: 压扁, 扁平, 扁鼻子. A naturally flat surface is 平.
column6: Zhè ge hézi bèi yā biǎn le.
column7: This box has been squashed flat.
column9: Flat in the sense of squashed, of what should be round or thick: 壓扁, 扁平, 扁鼻子. A naturally flat surface is 平.

column3: Third in a list, after 甲 and 乙, as C comes after A and B: 丙级 'grade C', 丙方 'third party'. Hepatitis C is 丙肝 on the mainland and C肝 in Taiwan.
column6: Jiǎ, yǐ, bǐng sān ge rén dōu lái le.
column7: A, B and C, all three people came.
column9: Third in a list, after 甲 and 乙, as C comes after A and B: 丙級 'grade C', 丙方 'third party'. Hepatitis C is 丙肝 on the mainland and C肝 in Taiwan.

column3: The room a patient stays in: 住进病房, 单人病房. In Taiwan an ICU is 加护病房; on the mainland it is 重症监护室. 房 names a room by its use in 厨房 and 书房 too.
column6: Yéye zhù zài sān lóu de bìngfáng.
column7: Grandpa is in a ward on the third floor.
column9: The room a patient stays in: 住進病房, 單人病房. In Taiwan an ICU is 加護病房; on the mainland it is 重症監護室. 房 names a room by its use in 廚房 and 書房 too.

column3: How the illness is going, what doctors and families discuss: 病情稳定, 病情恶化, 病情好转. Ask 病情怎么样？ for a patient's condition.
column4: 医生向家人说明了爸爸的病情。
column5: 醫生向家人說明了爸爸的病情。
column6: Yīshēng xiàng jiārén shuōmíng le bàba de bìngqíng.
column7: The doctor explained Dad's condition to the family.
column9: How the illness is going, what doctors and families discuss: 病情穩定, 病情惡化, 病情好轉. Ask 病情怎麼樣？ for a patient's condition.

column3: The written exam, set against 口试 'oral exam' and 面试 'interview'. Hiring often goes 笔试 first, then 面试: 通过笔试.
column4: 这家公司有笔试和面试。
column5: 這家公司有筆試和面試。
column6: Zhè jiā gōngsī yǒu bǐshì hé miànshì.
column7: This company has a written test and an interview.
column9: The written exam, set against 口試 'oral exam' and 面試 'interview'. Hiring often goes 筆試 first, then 面試: 通過筆試.

column3: Goes with 流 and 擤: 流鼻涕 'have a runny nose', 擤鼻涕 'blow your nose'. Tears in speech are 眼泪, not 涕.
column6: Wǒ gǎnmào le, yīzhí liú bítì.
column7: I have a cold and my nose keeps running.
column9: Goes with 流 and 擤: 流鼻涕 'have a runny nose', 擤鼻涕 'blow your nose'. Tears in speech are 眼淚, not 涕.

column3: Mostly written, for 'meager, unkind': 薄弱 'weak', 薄利 'small profit', and 待人不薄 'treat people well'. 厚 is the opposite.
column4: 我待他不薄，他却这样对我。
column5: 我待他不薄，他卻這樣對我。
column6: Wǒ dài tā bù bó, tā què zhèyàng duì wǒ.
column7: I have treated him well, yet he treats me like this.
column9: Mostly written, for 'meager, unkind': 薄弱 'weak', 薄利 'small profit', and 待人不薄 'treat people well'. 厚 is the opposite.

column3: Typical objects: 拨电话 and 拨号 for phone numbers, 拨款 for money an authority releases. In everyday speech “to make a call” is more often 打电话; 拨 is the act of dialing the number itself.
column4: 你可以拨这个电话号码问问。
column5: 你可以撥這個電話號碼問問。
column6: Nǐ kěyǐ bō zhège diànhuà hàomǎ wènwen.
column7: You can dial this phone number and ask.
column9: Typical objects: 撥電話 and 撥號 for phone numbers, 撥款 for money an authority releases. In everyday speech “to make a call” is more often 打電話; 撥 is the act of dialing the number itself.

column3: 菠 turns up mainly in this word and in 菠萝, the pineapple: 菠萝 on the mainland, 凤梨 in Taiwan.
column6: Māma jīntiān chǎo le bōcài.
column7: Mom stir-fried spinach today.
column9: 菠 turns up mainly in this word and in 菠蘿, the pineapple: 菠蘿 on the mainland, 鳳梨 in Taiwan.

column3: For things that rise and fall over time, such as prices, moods and markets: 价格波动, 情绪波动, 股市波动. It works as a noun and as a verb (价格波动很大), and it belongs to news and finance writing.
column6: Zuìjìn càijià bōdòng hěn dà.
column7: Vegetable prices have been fluctuating a lot lately.
column9: For things that rise and fall over time, such as prices, moods and markets: 價格波動, 情緒波動, 股市波動. It works as a noun and as a verb (價格波動很大), and it belongs to news and finance writing.

column3: Mostly written or technical: fish, birds and criminals are the usual catch, as in 捕鱼, 捕捉, 逮捕, 被捕. In casual speech people say 抓 for catching an animal or a person.
column6: Yúmín chūhǎi bǔ yú.
column7: The fishermen go out to sea to catch fish.
column9: Mostly written or technical: fish, birds and criminals are the usual catch, as in 捕魚, 捕捉, 逮捕, 被捕. In casual speech people say 抓 for catching an animal or a person.

column3: Two jobs. At the end of a question it makes it rhetorical, usually after 难道: 难道你想一个人去不成? After a verb it says “won’t do”: 这样不成 “this won’t do”. It is spoken and a little old-fashioned.
column4: 难道你想一个人去不成？
column5: 難道你想一個人去不成？
column6: Nándào nǐ xiǎng yī ge rén qù bùchéng?
column7: Surely you don’t want to go all by yourself?
column9: Two jobs. At the end of a question it makes it rhetorical, usually after 難道: 難道你想一個人去不成? After a verb it says “won’t do”: 這樣不成 “this won’t do”. It is spoken and a little old-fashioned.

column3: Formal, for reports, rules and the law: 处理不当, 用词不当, 不当行为. It comes after what was done badly, or before a noun. Here 当 is read dàng, “suitable”; read dāng it is “to be” or “to act as”.
column6: Zhège cí yòng de bùdàng.
column7: This word is used improperly.
column9: Formal, for reports, rules and the law: 處理不當, 用詞不當, 不當行為. It comes after what was done badly, or before a noun. Here 當 is read dàng, “suitable”; read dāng it is “to be” or “to act as”.

column3: Before a number it means “under”, and the number itself is not reached: 不到十分钟, 不到一年, 不到一半. For “has not arrived yet”, 没到 is the usual way to say it.
column4: 从我家走到车站不到十分钟。
column5: 從我家走到車站不到十分鐘。
column6: Cóng wǒ jiā zǒu dào chēzhàn bùdào shí fēnzhōng.
column7: It takes less than ten minutes to walk from my home to the station.
column9: Before a number it means “under”, and the number itself is not reached: 不到十分鐘, 不到一年, 不到一半. For “has not arrived yet”, 沒到 is the usual way to say it.

column3: Marks an act done against your wishes, usually with 才: 不得已才这么做. 万不得已 is the stronger “only if there is truly no other way”. Here 已 is the bound “to stop; to cease; to end”, not “already”.
column4: 我是不得已才这样做的。
column5: 我是不得已才這樣做的。
column6: Wǒ shì bùdéyǐ cái zhèyàng zuò de.
column7: I only did it because I had no choice.
column9: Marks an act done against your wishes, usually with 才: 不得已才這麼做. 萬不得已 is the stronger “only if there is truly no other way”. Here 已 is the bound “to stop; to cease; to end”, not “already”.

column3: 军队 is the military as a whole; 部队 is the troops themselves, a unit or force: 部队出发, 特种部队. 在部队 means being in the service, as in 他在部队待了五年.
column6: Bùduì míngtiān jiù yào chūfā le.
column7: The unit will set out tomorrow.
column9: 軍隊 is the military as a whole; 部隊 is the troops themselves, a unit or force: 部隊出發, 特種部隊. 在部隊 means being in the service, as in 他在部隊待了五年.

column3: A formal notice put up for everyone to read, by a school, company or government: 贴布告. A 通知 goes to particular people; a 布告 is posted in public.
column6: Xuéxiào tiēchū le yī zhāng bùgào.
column7: The school put up a notice.
column9: A formal notice put up for everyone to read, by a school, company or government: 貼佈告. A 通知 goes to particular people; a 佈告 is posted in public.

column3: Where notices are pinned, in school corridors, offices and apartment lobbies: 贴在布告栏上, 看布告栏. 公告栏 is a near-identical word for the same board.
column4: 考试成绩贴在布告栏上。
column5: 考試成績貼在佈告欄上。
column6: Kǎoshì chéngjì tiē zài bùgàolán shàng.
column7: The exam results are posted on the bulletin board.
column9: Where notices are pinned, in school corridors, offices and apartment lobbies: 貼在佈告欄上, 看佈告欄. 公告欄 is a near-identical word for the same board.

column3: A gentle doubt, often answering someone: on its own, 不见得 means “I’m not so sure”. It is weaker than 一定不: 他不见得会来 leaves open that he may come.
column6: Guì de dōngxi bùjiànde hǎo.
column7: Expensive things are not necessarily good.
column9: A gentle doubt, often answering someone: on its own, 不見得 means “I’m not so sure”. It is weaker than 一定不: 他不見得會來 leaves open that he may come.

column3: A verb-object word, so an amount goes in the middle: 补了两节课. It covers a class missed and taught again, and the extra lessons a school or parents arrange to catch up or prepare for exams: 周六补课.
column4: 因为台风，学校周六要补课。
column5: 因為颱風，學校週六要補課。
column6: Yīnwèi táifēng, xuéxiào zhōuliù yào bǔkè.
column7: Because of the typhoon, the school has make-up classes on Saturday.
column9: A verb-object word, so an amount goes in the middle: 補了兩節課. It covers a class missed and taught again, and the extra lessons a school or parents arrange to catch up or prepare for exams: 週六補課.

column3: Used of surfaces (路面不平) and of a sense of injustice: 心里不平, 为他不平, 打抱不平 “step in for someone wronged”. For the unfairness itself, the word is 不公平.
column4: 他觉得老板对他不公平，心里很不平。
column5: 他覺得老闆對他不公平，心裡很不平。
column6: Tā juéde lǎobǎn duì tā bù gōngpíng, xīnlǐ hěn bùpíng.
column7: He feels the boss is unfair to him and is very resentful.
column9: Used of surfaces (路面不平) and of a sense of injustice: 心裡不平, 為他不平, 打抱不平 “step in for someone wronged”. For the unfairness itself, the word is 不公平.

column3: Takes the subject as its object: 补习英文, 补习数学, 补习费. 补习 is the usual word in Taiwan for extra paid lessons, at a 补习班 or with a tutor; the mainland often says 补课 or 上辅导班 for the same thing.
column4: 他每天晚上都去补习英文。
column5: 他每天晚上都去補習英文。
column6: Tā měitiān wǎnshang dōu qù bǔxí Yīngwén.
column7: Every evening he goes to take English lessons at a cram school.
column9: Takes the subject as its object: 補習英文, 補習數學, 補習費. 補習 is the usual word in Taiwan for extra paid lessons, at a 補習班 or with a tutor; the mainland often says 補課 or 上輔導班 for the same thing.

column3: The private school itself, which you go to after regular school hours, for exams or languages: 上补习班, 英文补习班, 数学补习班. The mainland usually says 辅导班 or 培训班 instead.
column6: Tā xiàkè hòu yào qù bǔxíbān.
column7: After class she has to go to cram school.
column9: The private school itself, which you go to after regular school hours, for exams or languages: 上補習班, 英文補習班, 數學補習班. The mainland usually says 輔導班 or 培訓班 instead.

column3: Written style, for signs, labels and advice: 儿童不宜, 不宜久坐, 不宜饮酒. The spoken way to say it is 不适合 or 最好不要.
column6: Gǎnmào de shíhou bùyí hē jiǔ.
column7: It is not advisable to drink alcohol when you have a cold.
column9: Written style, for signs, labels and advice: 兒童不宜, 不宜久坐, 不宜飲酒. The spoken way to say it is 不適合 or 最好不要.

column3: Describes a reaction you don’t control, which comes right after it: 不由得笑了, 不由得想起. It usually follows a trigger (听到…, 看到…), and 忍不住 is the more spoken near-equivalent.
column4: 听到这个消息，他不由得笑了。
column5: 聽到這個消息，他不由得笑了。
column6: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā bùyóude xiào le.
column7: On hearing the news, he couldn’t help laughing.
column9: Describes a reaction you don’t control, which comes right after it: 不由得笑了, 不由得想起. It usually follows a trigger (听到…, 看到…), and 忍不住 is the more spoken near-equivalent.

column3: Goes with 申请 (apply for) and 领 (receive): 申请补助, 领补助, 政府补助. Also a verb: 补助低收入家庭. 补贴 is a close synonym, often tied to one particular cost.
column6: Zhèngfǔ bǔzhù dī shōurù jiātíng.
column7: The government gives subsidies to low-income families.
column9: Goes with 申請 (apply for) and 領 (receive): 申請補助, 領補助, 政府補助. Also a verb: 補助低收入家庭. 補貼 is a close synonym, often tied to one particular cost.

column3: Pressing down with the foot, on a pedal too: 踩刹车, 踩油门. 踩到 is an accidental step: 踩到水坑. Online it also means to put someone down, the opposite of 赞 (like).
column4: 对不起，我踩到你的脚了。
column5: 對不起，我踩到你的腳了。
column6: Duìbuqǐ, wǒ cǎi dào nǐ de jiǎo le.
column7: Sorry, I stepped on your foot.
column9: Pressing down with the foot, on a pedal too: 踩剎車, 踩油門. 踩到 is an accidental step: 踩到水坑. Online it also means to put someone down, the opposite of 讚 (like).

column3: Alone it picks by hand: 采茶, 采花. More often it sits in formal verbs: 采取 (take measures), 采用 (adopt), 采访 (interview), 采购 (purchase).
column6: Tā qù shān shàng cǎi chá.
column7: He goes up the mountain to pick tea.
column9: Alone it picks by hand: 採茶, 採花. More often it sits in formal verbs: 採取 (take measures), 採用 (adopt), 採訪 (interview), 採購 (purchase).

column3: A news and business word, with the number after it: 公司裁员, 裁员一百人. People who lose their jobs are 被裁员 or just 被裁; 开除 is being fired for something you did, and 裁员 is job cuts.
column4: 公司因为经济不好要裁员。
column5: 公司因為經濟不好要裁員。
column6: Gōngsī yīnwèi jīngjì bù hǎo yào cáiyuán.
column7: The company is going to lay off staff because the economy is bad.
column9: A news and business word, with the number after it: 公司裁員, 裁員一百人. People who lose their jobs are 被裁員 or just 被裁; 開除 is being fired for something you did, and 裁員 is job cuts.

column6: Cán chī sāngyè, ránhòu tǔ sī.
column7: Silkworms eat mulberry leaves and then spin silk.

column3: In speech, 惨了! is “oh no, I’m in trouble”, and 很惨 or 好惨 pities someone’s state. In 惨败 and 惨剧 it is written and dramatic.
column6: Zhè cì kǎoshì tā kǎo de hěn cǎn.
column7: He did really badly in this exam.
column9: In speech, 慘了! is “oh no, I’m in trouble”, and 很慘 or 好慘 pities someone’s state. In 慘敗 and 慘劇 it is written and dramatic.

column3: Hides things: 藏钱, 藏在床底下, 藏起来. It hides people too (藏在门后, 捉迷藏); 躲 adds avoiding or dodging (躲雨, 躲着他). 收藏 is to collect (art, stamps).
column6: Tā bǎ qián cáng zài chuáng dǐxia.
column7: He hid the money under the bed.
column9: Hides things: 藏錢, 藏在床底下, 藏起來. It hides people too (藏在門後, 捉迷藏); 躲 adds avoiding or dodging (躲雨, 躲著他). 收藏 is to collect (art, stamps).

column3: Where goods are kept, from a factory warehouse to a storeroom at home: 仓库管理. 库 alone is a storage place, as in 车库 (garage), 冷库 (cold storage) and 入库 (into stock).
column6: Huòwù dōu fàng zài cāngkù lǐ.
column7: The goods are all kept in the warehouse.
column9: Where goods are kept, from a factory warehouse to a storeroom at home: 倉庫管理. 庫 alone is a storage place, as in 車庫 (garage), 冷庫 (cold storage) and 入庫 (into stock).

column3: Shame at falling short of what you should have done, not embarrassment in public (that is 不好意思). It is also the modest answer to praise: 惭愧，惭愧.
column6: Wǒ méiyǒu bāng shàng máng, zhēn cánkuì.
column7: I wasn’t able to help, and I feel ashamed.
column9: Shame at falling short of what you should have done, not embarrassment in public (that is 不好意思). It is also the modest answer to praise: 慚愧，慚愧.

column3: A verb-object word, so it splits: 操了不少心, 别操心. Often a parent over a child, and 不用你操心 tells someone it is none of their worry.
column6: Māma zǒngshì wèi háizi cāoxīn.
column7: Mom is always worrying about her children.
column9: A verb-object word, so it splits: 操了不少心, 別操心. Often a parent over a child, and 不用你操心 tells someone it is none of their worry.

column3: Goes with 制定 (draw up) and 采取 (adopt): 制定策略, 采取策略, 营销策略. 战略 is the grand long-term plan; 策略 is closer to the tactics for a particular situation.
column4: 公司需要新的销售策略。
column5: 公司需要新的銷售策略。
column6: Gōngsī xūyào xīn de xiāoshòu cèlüè.
column7: The company needs a new sales strategy.
column9: Goes with 制定 (draw up) and 採取 (adopt): 制定策略, 採取策略, 營銷策略. 戰略 is the grand long-term plan; 策略 is closer to the tactics for a particular situation.

column3: A formal word for a test: 智力测验, 性向测验. At school a quiz is 小考 in Taiwan and 小测 on the mainland.
column4: 老师明天要给我们一个测验。
column5: 老師明天要給我們一個測驗。
column6: Lǎoshī míngtiān yào gěi wǒmen yī ge cèyàn.
column7: The teacher will give us a test tomorrow.
column9: A formal word for a test: 智力測驗, 性向測驗. At school a quiz is 小考 in Taiwan and 小測 on the mainland.

column3: As “difference” it is the arithmetic and measuring word: 十和三的差, 时差 (time difference), 误差 (margin of error), 差距 (gap).
column6: Shí hé sān de chā shì qī.
column7: The difference between ten and three is seven.
column9: As “difference” it is the arithmetic and measuring word: 十和三的差, 時差 (time difference), 誤差 (margin of error), 差距 (gap).

column3: A slip in work that has to be exact, mostly with 出 or 有: 出差错, 不能有差错, 一点差错也没有. It is a mishap in something that should go right; 错误 is the general word for an error.
column4: 这件事不能出任何差错。
column5: 這件事不能出任何差錯。
column6: Zhè jiàn shì bù néng chū rènhé chācuò.
column7: There must not be any mistake in this matter.
column9: A slip in work that has to be exact, mostly with 出 or 有: 出差錯, 不能有差錯, 一點差錯也沒有. It is a mishap in something that should go right; 錯誤 is the general word for an error.

column3: Flower arranging as a hobby or class: 学插花, 插花课, 日式插花. It is built like a verb and its object (插 花), so it can split: 插了一瓶花.
column6: Zhōumò wǒ qù shàng chāhuā kè.
column7: On weekends I go to a flower arranging class.
column9: Flower arranging as a hobby or class: 學插花, 插花課, 日式插花. It is built like a verb and its object (插 花), so it can split: 插了一瓶花.

column3: Usually an organized gathering with tea and snacks, such as a welcome or school reception: 举办茶会, 欢迎茶会. Tea with a friend is just 喝茶, and the British kind is 下午茶.
column4: 学校为新生办了一个茶会。
column5: 學校為新生辦了一個茶會。
column6: Xuéxiào wèi xīnshēng bàn le yī ge cháhuì.
column7: The school held a tea party for the new students.
column9: Usually an organized gathering with tea and snacks, such as a welcome or school reception: 舉辦茶會, 歡迎茶會. Tea with a friend is just 喝茶, and the British kind is 下午茶.

column3: Alone it is mostly for a place producing a crop or resource: 产茶, 产油, 盛产水果. Most other uses are in compounds like 生产 and 产品. For a person giving birth, 生 is the everyday verb.
column4: 这个地方产茶，也产水果。
column5: 這個地方產茶，也產水果。
column6: Zhège dìfang chǎn chá, yě chǎn shuǐguǒ.
column7: This place produces tea and also fruit.
column9: Alone it is mostly for a place producing a crop or resource: 產茶, 產油, 盛產水果. Most other uses are in compounds like 生產 and 產品. For a person giving birth, 生 is the everyday verb.

column3: The space you book or prepare for an activity: 场地租借, 比赛场地, 找场地. For a place where something merely happens, 地方 is the word.
column4: 我们需要找一个大一点的场地。
column5: 我們需要找一個大一點的場地。
column6: Wǒmen xūyào zhǎo yī ge dà yīdiǎn de chǎngdì.
column7: We need to find a somewhat larger venue.
column9: The space you book or prepare for an activity: 場地租借, 比賽場地, 找場地. For a place where something merely happens, 地方 is the word.

column3: 形 ends the names of shapes: 正方形 (square), 三角形 (triangle), 圆形 (circle). Its two sides are its 长 and 宽 (length and width).
column6: Zhè zhāng zhuōzi shì chángfāngxíng de.
column7: This table is rectangular.
column9: 形 ends the names of shapes: 正方形 (square), 三角形 (triangle), 圓形 (circle). Its two sides are its 長 and 寬 (length and width).

column3: Written and a little formal; the length is in time. It asks whether something lasts: 长久之计, 不能长久, 长久以来. 长期 is for a long stretch, as in 长期合同.
column6: Zhè zhǒng guānxi bù huì chángjiǔ.
column7: This kind of relationship will not last.
column9: Written and a little formal; the length is in time. It asks whether something lasts: 長久之計, 不能長久, 長久以來. 長期 is for a long stretch, as in 長期合同.

column3: Companies as the buyer sees them, the firms behind a product: 电脑厂商, 汽车厂商. They are the ones who answer for repairs and warranties. 厂家 is the spoken near-synonym.
column4: 这家厂商提供一年免费维修。
column5: 這家廠商提供一年免費維修。
column6: Zhè jiā chǎngshāng tígōng yī nián miǎnfèi wéixiū.
column7: This maker provides one year of free repairs.
column9: Companies as the buyer sees them, the firms behind a product: 電腦廠商, 汽車廠商. They are the ones who answer for repairs and warranties. 廠家 is the spoken near-synonym.

column3: 量 after a noun gives “the amount of it”: 产量, 销量, 用量, 数量. 产量 is for factories and farms: 年产量, 提高产量, 产量下降.
column4: 今年的稻米产量比去年高。
column5: 今年的稻米產量比去年高。
column6: Jīnnián de dàomǐ chǎnliàng bǐ qùnián gāo.
column7: This year’s rice output is higher than last year’s.
column9: 量 after a noun gives “the amount of it”: 產量, 銷量, 用量, 數量. 產量 is for factories and farms: 年產量, 提高產量, 產量下降.

column3: What is passed comes right after it, nearly always a limit or a figure: 超出预算, 超出范围, 超出能力. 超过 compares quantities and people; 超出 goes past a boundary.
column4: 这次旅行的花费超出了预算。
column5: 這次旅行的花費超出了預算。
column6: Zhè cì lǚxíng de huāfèi chāochū le yùsuàn.
column7: The cost of this trip went over the budget.
column9: What is passed comes right after it, nearly always a limit or a figure: 超出預算, 超出範圍, 超出能力. 超過 compares quantities and people; 超出 goes past a boundary.

column3: About the noise, from people or from a place: 吵闹声, 孩子们吵闹, 太吵闹. For two people quarreling in words, 吵架 is the word.
column4: 教室里太吵闹，我听不清楚。
column5: 教室裡太吵鬧，我聽不清楚。
column6: Jiàoshì lǐ tài chǎonào, wǒ tīng bù qīngchu.
column7: The classroom is too noisy and I can’t hear clearly.
column9: About the noise, from people or from a place: 吵鬧聲, 孩子們吵鬧, 太吵鬧. For two people quarreling in words, 吵架 is the word.

column3: Counted with 张: 一张钞票, 数钞票, 假钞票. 钞票 is the notes themselves, 钱 is money in general, and 零钱 is small change.
column4: 他从口袋里拿出一张钞票。
column5: 他從口袋裡拿出一張鈔票。
column6: Tā cóng kǒudài lǐ náchū yī zhāng chāopiào.
column7: He took a banknote out of his pocket.
column9: Counted with 張: 一張鈔票, 數鈔票, 假鈔票. 鈔票 is the notes themselves, 錢 is money in general, and 零錢 is small change.

column3: Superman, the comic hero, and also “superhuman” of strength or will: 超人的毅力, 超人般的力量.
column4: 小男孩喜欢穿超人的衣服。
column5: 小男孩喜歡穿超人的衣服。
column6: Xiǎo nánhái xǐhuan chuān Chāorén de yīfu.
column7: The little boy likes to wear a Superman costume.
column9: Superman, the comic hero, and also “superhuman” of strength or will: 超人的毅力, 超人般的力量.

column3: Said of what is over a set weight limit, mostly luggage and loaded trucks: 行李超重, 货车超重, 超重罚款 (a fine for overloading). It is also said of a person’s weight: 我超重了.
column4: 你的行李超重了，要多付钱。
column5: 你的行李超重了，要多付錢。
column6: Nǐ de xíngli chāozhòng le, yào duō fù qián.
column7: Your baggage is overweight and you must pay extra.
column9: Said of what is over a set weight limit, mostly luggage and loaded trucks: 行李超重, 貨車超重, 超重罰款 (a fine for overloading). It is also said of a person’s weight: 我超重了.

column3: A picture inserted in a book or article: 书里的插图, 配插图. 插画 is the art of illustration, and a 插画家 is an illustrator.
column4: 这本书有很多漂亮的插图。
column5: 這本書有很多漂亮的插圖。
column6: Zhè běn shū yǒu hěn duō piàoliang de chātú.
column7: This book has a lot of pretty illustrations.
column9: A picture inserted in a book or article: 書裡的插圖, 配插圖. 插畫 is the art of illustration, and a 插畫家 is an illustrator.

column3: Pulling and tearing: 扯破, 扯后腿 “hold someone back”. Talking nonsense is 瞎扯 or 闲扯. In Taiwan, 很扯 or 太扯了 is common slang for “ridiculous, unbelievable”; on the mainland the word for it is 离谱.
column4: 这个理由太扯了，我不相信。
column5: 這個理由太扯了，我不相信。
column6: Zhège lǐyóu tài chě le, wǒ bù xiāngxìn.
column7: This reason is too ridiculous; I don’t believe it.
column9: Pulling and tearing: 扯破, 扯後腿 “hold someone back”. Talking nonsense is 瞎扯 or 閒扯. In Taiwan, 很扯 or 太扯了 is common slang for “ridiculous, unbelievable”; on the mainland the word for it is 離譜.

column3: Goes before a verb and says nothing is left: 澈底解决, 澈底改变, 澈底失败. It also works as an adjective: 很澈底, 不澈底.
column4: 我们要澈底解决这个问题。
column5: 我們要澈底解決這個問題。
column6: Wǒmen yào chèdǐ jiějué zhège wèntí.
column7: We must solve this problem once and for all.
column9: Goes before a verb and says nothing is left: 澈底解決, 澈底改變, 澈底失敗. It also works as an adjective: 很澈底, 不澈底.

column3: Three everyday uses: opening an umbrella (撑伞), holding out (撑住, 撑不下去), and being stuffed from eating (吃撑了, 撑死了 “I’m about to burst”).
column6: Xià yǔ le, tā chēng qǐ le sǎn.
column7: It was raining, and he put up his umbrella.
column9: Three everyday uses: opening an umbrella (撐傘), holding out (撐住, 撐不下去), and being stuffed from eating (吃撐了, 撐死了 “I’m about to burst”).

column3: The parts something is made of: 成分表 (ingredient list), 化学成分. -分 names the share of a substance in something: 水分, 养分, 糖分. Here 分 is read fèn, “part; ingredient; component”, not the fēn of “to divide”.
column4: 这种饼干的成分很简单。
column5: 這種餅乾的成分很簡單。
column6: Zhè zhǒng bǐnggān de chéngfèn hěn jiǎndān.
column7: The ingredients of this cookie are simple.
column9: The parts something is made of: 成分表 (ingredient list), 化學成分. -分 names the share of a substance in something: 水分, 養分, 糖分. Here 分 is read fèn, “part; ingredient; component”, not the fēn of “to divide”.

column3: 成分 is the standard form and 成份 a common variant. It names what a thing is made of, as on a food label (营养成份), and for a person it can mean class background.
column4: 牛奶里有很多营养成份。
column5: 牛奶裡有很多營養成份。
column6: Niúnǎi lǐ yǒu hěn duō yíngyǎng chéngfèn.
column7: Milk has many nutritional components.
column9: 成分 is the standard form and 成份 a common variant. It names what a thing is made of, as on a food label (營養成份), and for a person it can mean class background.

column3: Describes a person's attitude, tone or words, never an object: 态度诚恳, 诚恳地道歉, 诚恳的建议. It suggests earnest, humble honesty, so it suits apologies and requests.
column6: Tā chéngkěn de xiàng dàjiā dàoqiàn.
column7: He apologized to everyone sincerely.
column9: Describes a person's attitude, tone or words, never an object: 態度誠懇, 誠懇地道歉, 誠懇的建議. It suggests earnest, humble honesty, so it suits apologies and requests.

column3: Spoken, goes before a verb, and often carries a complaint: 成天看手机, 成天玩. 整天 says the same neutrally, and 一天到晚 is the stronger 'from morning till night'.
column6: Tā chéngtiān zhǐ zhīdào wán yóuxì.
column7: He does nothing but play games all day.
column9: Spoken, goes before a verb, and often carries a complaint: 成天看手機, 成天玩. 整天 says the same neutrally, and 一天到晚 is the stronger 'from morning till night'.

column3: A formal word for how something looks or turns out: 呈现出...的样子, 呈现新面貌. The subject is the thing that shows itself (a painting, data, a trend). 呈 alone also takes a color or shape: 呈红色, 呈圆形.
column4: 这幅画呈现出秋天的景色。
column5: 這幅畫呈現出秋天的景色。
column6: Zhè fú huà chéngxiàn chū qiūtiān de jǐngsè.
column7: This painting shows an autumn scene.
column9: A formal word for how something looks or turns out: 呈現出...的樣子, 呈現新面貌. The subject is the thing that shows itself (a painting, data, a trend). 呈 alone also takes a color or shape: 呈紅色, 呈圓形.

column3: A noun you have, show or lack: 有诚意, 表示诚意, 没有诚意. It comes up with apologies, offers and negotiations. 诚恳 is the adjective for the person's manner.
column4: 他道歉一点诚意也没有。
column5: 他道歉一點誠意也沒有。
column6: Tā dàoqiàn yī diǎn chéngyì yě méiyǒu.
column7: His apology has no sincerity at all.
column9: A noun you have, show or lack: 有誠意, 表示誠意, 沒有誠意. It comes up with apologies, offers and negotiations. 誠懇 is the adjective for the person's manner.

column3: For goods in a shop or objects in a museum, set out so people can see them: 陈列商品, 陈列室 (showroom), 陈列柜 (display case). It is a formal word; in speech people say 摆.
column4: 橱窗里陈列着新款的鞋子。
column5: 櫥窗裡陳列著新款的鞋子。
column6: Chúchuāng lǐ chénliè zhe xīnkuǎn de xiézi.
column7: New styles of shoes are displayed in the shop window.
column9: For goods in a shop or objects in a museum, set out so people can see them: 陳列商品, 陳列室 (showroom), 陳列櫃 (display case). It is a formal word; in speech people say 擺.

column3: Wings of a bird, an insect or a plane: 张开翅膀, 拍动翅膀. Chicken wings as food are 鸡翅 (or 鸡翅膀); the short 翅 only turns up inside compounds.
column6: Xiǎo niǎo zhāngkāi le chìbǎng.
column7: The little bird spread its wings.
column9: Wings of a bird, an insect or a plane: 張開翅膀, 拍動翅膀. Chicken wings as food are 雞翅 (or 雞翅膀); the short 翅 only turns up inside compounds.

column3: A bound word: it works only inside compounds, and by itself a wing is 翅膀. Meet it in 鸡翅 (chicken wings), 鱼翅 (shark's fin) and 展翅 (to spread wings).
column6: Xiǎo niǎo pāi zhe chì bǎng fēi zǒu le.
column7: The little bird flapped its wings and flew away.
column9: A bound word: it works only inside compounds, and by itself a wing is 翅膀. Meet it in 雞翅 (chicken wings), 魚翅 (shark's fin) and 展翅 (to spread wings).

column3: Said of losing out in a deal, a fight or an argument: 不想吃亏, 吃了亏, 吃亏上当. The saying 吃亏就是占便宜 says that losing out can be a gain. 吃 itself can mean to suffer a blow or defeat, which is how it is used here.
column4: 我不想吃亏，所以要问清楚。
column5: 我不想吃虧，所以要問清楚。
column6: Wǒ bù xiǎng chīkuī, suǒyǐ yào wèn qīngchu.
column7: I don't want to lose out, so I'll ask clearly.
column9: Said of losing out in a deal, a fight or an argument: 不想吃虧, 吃了虧, 吃虧上當. The saying 吃虧就是佔便宜 says that losing out can be a gain. 吃 itself can mean to suffer a blow or defeat, which is how it is used here.

column3: Goes before the verb, usually with 会 or 要, for something that is bound to happen: 迟早会知道. It often sounds like a warning: 你迟早会后悔的. 早晚 is a spoken twin.
column4: 你迟早会明白我的意思。
column5: 你遲早會明白我的意思。
column6: Nǐ chízǎo huì míngbai wǒ de yìsi.
column7: Sooner or later you will understand what I mean.
column9: Goes before the verb, usually with 會 or 要, for something that is bound to happen: 遲早會知道. It often sounds like a warning: 你遲早會後悔的. 早晚 is a spoken twin.

column3: Stronger than 喜欢 or 欣赏: you look up to a person like a hero. 崇拜偶像 (idolize a star), 个人崇拜 (personality cult). It also covers religious worship.
column6: Tā hěn chóngbài zìjǐ de gēge.
column7: He greatly admires his older brother.
column9: Stronger than 喜歡 or 欣賞: you look up to a person like a hero. 崇拜偶像 (idolize a star), 個人崇拜 (personality cult). It also covers religious worship.

column3: A written, praising word for ideals, goals, spirit or character: 崇高的理想, 崇高的精神. The set phrase 致以崇高的敬意 is a formal 'with the highest respect'. It is not used for plain physical height.
column6: Tā yǒu chónggāo de lǐxiǎng.
column7: He has lofty ideals.
column9: A written, praising word for ideals, goals, spirit or character: 崇高的理想, 崇高的精神. The set phrase 致以崇高的敬意 is a formal 'with the highest respect'. It is not used for plain physical height.

column3: You 拉开 (pull open) or 关上 a drawer; the measure word is 个, and 第一个抽屉 is the top one. 抽 is the same 'pull out' as in 抽烟 and 抽奖.
column6: Yàoshi zài shūzhuō de chōuti lǐ.
column7: The key is in the desk drawer.
column9: You 拉開 (pull open) or 關上 a drawer; the measure word is 個, and 第一個抽屜 is the top one. 抽 is the same 'pull out' as in 抽煙 and 抽獎.

column3: As a verb it is more written than spoken: 处在, 处于 (be in a situation), 相处 (get along), 处理 (deal with).
column4: 他处在很困难的情况中。
column5: 他處在很困難的情況中。
column6: Tā chǔ zài hěn kùnnán de qíngkuàng zhōng.
column7: He is in a very difficult situation.
column9: As a verb it is more written than spoken: 處在, 處於 (be in a situation), 相處 (get along), 處理 (deal with).

column3: The set verb is 发 (hand out): 发传单. Count them with 张 or 份. 单 as a sheet or list also appears in 菜单 and 账单.
column6: Lùbiān yǒu rén zài fā chuándān.
column7: Someone is handing out flyers by the road.
column9: The set verb is 發 (hand out): 發傳單. Count them with 張 or 份. 單 as a sheet or list also appears in 菜單 and 帳單.

column3: Counts a whole building (一幢楼, 一幢别墅), while 间 counts rooms or shops. 栋 does the same job.
column6: Nà zhuàng dàlóu yǒu sānshí céng.
column7: That building has thirty floors.
column9: Counts a whole building (一幢樓, 一幢別墅), while 間 counts rooms or shops. 棟 does the same job.

column3: Goes with 铺 (spread), 换 and 洗, and is counted with 条 or 张. It lies under you on the mattress; what covers you is 被子.
column4: 我每个星期换一次床单。
column5: 我每個星期換一次床單。
column6: Wǒ měi ge xīngqī huàn yī cì chuángdān.
column7: I change my sheets once a week.
column9: Goes with 鋪 (spread), 換 and 洗, and is counted with 條 or 張. It lies under you on the mattress; what covers you is 被子.

column3: A window in a wall is 窗户. 窗口 is where you queue for service (售票窗口, 挂号窗口) or a window on a screen. Figuratively it is a showcase, as in 世界的窗口.
column4: 请到三号窗口办理手续。
column5: 請到三號窗口辦理手續。
column6: Qǐng dào sān hào chuāngkǒu bànlǐ shǒuxù.
column7: Please go to window number three to do the paperwork.
column9: A window in a wall is 窗戶. 窗口 is where you queue for service (售票窗口, 掛號窗口) or a window on a screen. Figuratively it is a showcase, as in 世界的窗口.

column3: The person who passes it on takes 给: 传染给别人; the person who catches it is 被传染. 传染病 is an infectious disease. It also works for moods: 笑声会传染. 感染 is to become infected.
column4: 感冒很容易传染给别人。
column5: 感冒很容易傳染給別人。
column6: Gǎnmào hěn róngyì chuánrǎn gěi biéren.
column7: A cold is easily passed on to others.
column9: The person who passes it on takes 給: 傳染給別人; the person who catches it is 被傳染. 傳染病 is an infectious disease. It also works for moods: 笑聲會傳染. 感染 is to become infected.

column3: Sending through a machine or a system rather than by hand: 传送文件, 传送带 (conveyor belt), and in games 传送门, a teleport gate.
column6: Qǐng bǎ wénjiàn chuánsòng gěi wǒ.
column7: Please send the file to me.
column9: Sending through a machine or a system rather than by hand: 傳送文件, 傳送帶 (conveyor belt), and in games 傳送門, a teleport gate.

column3: The subject is the place or the factory: 这里出产茶叶. What a region is known for is its 特产 (local specialty), and the goods themselves are 产品.
column4: 这个地区出产很好的茶叶。
column5: 這個地區出產很好的茶葉。
column6: Zhège dìqū chūchǎn hěn hǎo de cháyè.
column7: This region produces very good tea.
column9: The subject is the place or the factory: 這裡出產茶葉. What a region is known for is its 特產 (local specialty), and the goods themselves are 產品.

column3: Doubling a one-syllable word often gives 'every': 人人, 天天, 处处. It goes before the verb, often with 都: 处处都是, 处处为别人着想.
column6: Tā chùchù wèi biéren zhuóxiǎng.
column7: He thinks of others in every way.
column9: Doubling a one-syllable word often gives 'every': 人人, 天天, 處處. It goes before the verb, often with 都: 處處都是, 處處為別人著想.

column3: In Taiwan 储存档案 is the usual way to say saving a file, where the mainland says 保存文件 or 存储. For stocking goods it is common on both sides: 储存食物.
column4: 请把这些食物储存在冰箱里。
column5: 請把這些食物儲存在冰箱裡。
column6: Qǐng bǎ zhèxiē shíwù chǔcún zài bīngxiāng lǐ.
column7: Please store this food in the refrigerator.
column9: In Taiwan 儲存檔案 is the usual way to say saving a file, where the mainland says 保存文件 or 存儲. For stocking goods it is common on both sides: 儲存食物.

column3: The border-control word: 出境 is leaving, 入境 is entering, and signs say 出入境. 出境游 is travel abroad.
column6: Chūjìng qián yào xiān jiǎnchá hùzhào.
column7: Check your passport first before leaving the country.
column9: The border-control word: 出境 is leaving, 入境 is entering, and signs say 出入境. 出境游 is travel abroad.

column3: Says what background a person comes from: family (农民家庭出身), a job (军人出身) or training (师范出身). Often 出身于..., or 出身 plus an adjective: 出身贫寒. 出生 (to be born) sounds almost the same but is a different word.
column4: 他出身于一个普通的家庭。
column5: 他出身於一個普通的家庭。
column6: Tā chūshēn yú yī ge pǔtōng de jiātíng.
column7: He comes from an ordinary family.
column9: Says what background a person comes from: family (農民家庭出身), a job (軍人出身) or training (師範出身). Often 出身於..., or 出身 plus an adjective: 出身貧寒. 出生 (to be born) sounds almost the same but is a different word.

column3: Always bad news, and spoken: an accident, a mishap, trouble. 出事了 and 出什么事了? are the everyday forms, and 没事 is the opposite, 'nothing is wrong'.
column6: Qiánmiàn de lùkǒu chūshì le.
column7: There has been an accident at the intersection ahead.
column9: Always bad news, and spoken: an accident, a mishap, trouble. 出事了 and 出什麼事了? are the everyday forms, and 沒事 is the opposite, 'nothing is wrong'.

column3: The formal word for money kept for the long term: 储蓄存款, 储蓄率, 储蓄习惯. In speech people say 存钱. In Taiwan the first character is read chú.
column4: 他每个月都会储蓄一些钱。
column5: 他每個月都會儲蓄一些錢。
column6: Tā měi ge yuè dōu huì chǔxù yīxiē qián.
column7: He saves some money every month.
column9: The formal word for money kept for the long term: 儲蓄存款, 儲蓄率, 儲蓄習慣. In speech people say 存錢. In Taiwan the first character is read chú.

column3: The count itself, which goes with 多, 少, 增加 and 减少: 次数太多. To ask 'how many times' you say 几次 or 多少次 instead.
column4: 我这个月去健身房的次数不多。
column5: 我這個月去健身房的次數不多。
column6: Wǒ zhège yuè qù jiànshēnfáng de cìshù bù duō.
column7: I haven't gone to the gym many times this month.
column9: The count itself, which goes with 多, 少, 增加 and 減少: 次數太多. To ask 'how many times' you say 幾次 or 多少次 instead.

column3: A short form of 从来没有, usually followed by a verb with 过: 从没去过. Written style has 从未. For a habit, 从不 is the word: 他从不迟到.
column4: 我从没见过这么大的雪。
column5: 我從沒見過這麼大的雪。
column6: Wǒ cóngméi jiàn guò zhème dà de xuě.
column7: I have never seen such heavy snow.
column9: A short form of 從來沒有, usually followed by a verb with 過: 從沒去過. Written style has 從未. For a habit, 從不 is the word: 他從不遲到.

column3: Putting small pieces together to get enough: 凑钱, 凑齐 (complete a set), 凑人数. Fixed phrases build on it: 凑热闹 (join the fun), 凑合 (make do), 凑巧 (as luck would have it).
column4: 我们凑钱给老师买了礼物。
column5: 我們湊錢給老師買了禮物。
column6: Wǒmen còu qián gěi lǎoshī mǎi le lǐwù.
column7: We pooled our money and bought a present for the teacher.
column9: Putting small pieces together to get enough: 湊錢, 湊齊 (complete a set), 湊人數. Fixed phrases build on it: 湊熱鬧 (join the fun), 湊合 (make do), 湊巧 (as luck would have it).

column3: The person or thing being pushed comes right after: 催他快点, 催稿 (chase a deadline), and at a restaurant 催菜 chases your order. 催促 is the formal version.
column4: 妈妈一直催我快点起床。
column5: 媽媽一直催我快點起床。
column6: Māma yīzhí cuī wǒ kuài diǎn qǐchuáng.
column7: Mom keeps urging me to get up quickly.
column9: The person or thing being pushed comes right after: 催他快點, 催稿 (chase a deadline), and at a restaurant 催菜 chases your order. 催促 is the formal version.

column3: A back-and-forth rub with the palms or fingers: 搓手 to warm up, 搓汤圆 to roll rice balls, 搓衣服 to scrub laundry by hand. 搓麻将 is slang for playing mahjong.
column4: 冬天很冷，他不停地搓手。
column5: 冬天很冷，他不停地搓手。
column6: Dōngtiān hěn lěng, tā bù tíng de cuō shǒu.
column7: It is very cold in winter, and he keeps rubbing his hands.
column9: A back-and-forth rub with the palms or fingers: 搓手 to warm up, 搓湯圓 to roll rice balls, 搓衣服 to scrub laundry by hand. 搓麻將 is slang for playing mahjong.

column3: For a chance, a train, an event or a person that went by without you meeting it: 错过机会, 错过了他. It is not 'miss' as in longing (that is 想念); in speech 没赶上 is the plainer way to say you missed a train.
column4: 我错过了最后一班火车。
column5: 我錯過了最後一班火車。
column6: Wǒ cuòguò le zuìhòu yī bān huǒchē.
column7: I missed the last train.
column9: For a chance, a train, an event or a person that went by without you meeting it: 錯過機會, 錯過了他. It is not 'miss' as in longing (that is 想念); in speech 沒趕上 is the plainer way to say you missed a train.

column3: A character with a wrong stroke or shape. A real character used in place of the right one is a 别字, and 错别字 covers both. It also means a typo: 改错字.
column4: 这篇文章里有两个错字。
column5: 這篇文章裡有兩個錯字。
column6: Zhè piān wénzhāng lǐ yǒu liǎng ge cuòzì.
column7: There are two wrongly written characters in this article.
column9: A character with a wrong stroke or shape. A real character used in place of the right one is a 別字, and 錯別字 covers both. It also means a typo: 改錯字.

column3: Before a measure word it means more than half: 大半个月, 大半天, 大半辈子 (most of a life). For 'probably', the everyday word is 多半.
column6: Tā dàbàn ge yuè dōu zài chūchāi.
column7: He is away on business for most of the month.
column9: Before a measure word it means more than half: 大半個月, 大半天, 大半輩子 (most of a life). For 'probably', the everyday word is 多半.

column3: A plain, medical-sounding word, paired with 小便, used with doctors and with babies. 拉屎 is the crude spoken one, and 上大号 the polite euphemism.
column6: Bǎobao jīntiān dàbiàn le ma?
column7: Has the baby had a bowel movement today?
column9: A plain, medical-sounding word, paired with 小便, used with doctors and with babies. 拉屎 is the crude spoken one, and 上大號 the polite euphemism.

column3: The ground seen as a whole under the sky, a poetic or news word: 大地回春, 大地震动. 土地 is land as property or soil, and 地球 is the planet.
column4: 春天来了，大地一片绿色。
column5: 春天來了，大地一片綠色。
column6: Chūntiān lái le, dàdì yī piàn lǜsè.
column7: Spring has come and the land is all green.
column9: The ground seen as a whole under the sky, a poetic or news word: 大地回春, 大地震動. 土地 is land as property or soil, and 地球 is the planet.

column3: A written word that goes before 是 or a verb: 大都是学生. It means the same as 大多, which is the more common choice in speech.
column4: 这里的学生大都住在附近。
column5: 這裡的學生大都住在附近。
column6: Zhèlǐ de xuésheng dàdōu zhù zài fùjìn.
column7: Most of the students here live nearby.
column9: A written word that goes before 是 or a verb: 大都是學生. It means the same as 大多, which is the more common choice in speech.

column3: Verb plus result: hit so that it breaks. That is why it works for a speaker, a conversation or a bone: 打断别人说话, 被打断. To bother someone, use 打扰.
column6: Qǐng bù yào dǎduàn biéren shuōhuà.
column7: Please don't interrupt other people when they speak.
column9: Verb plus result: hit so that it breaks. That is why it works for a speaker, a conversation or a bone: 打斷別人說話, 被打斷. To bother someone, use 打擾.

column3: Mostly in compounds for treating people: 对待, 招待, 接待, 款待; alone it appears in set phrases like 待人 and 待客. In speech 'wait' is 等; 待 as wait is written, as in 等待 and 期待.
column6: Tā dài rén hěn qīnqiè.
column7: He treats people very kindly.
column9: Mostly in compounds for treating people: 對待, 招待, 接待, 款待; alone it appears in set phrases like 待人 and 待客. In speech 'wait' is 等; 待 as wait is written, as in 等待 and 期待.

column3: Any long flat strip for tying or carrying: a bag strap, a ribbon, a lace. 鞋带 and 腰带 name particular ones. In speech it can also mean an audio or video tape.
column6: Zhège bāo de dàizi duàn le.
column7: The strap of this bag has broken.
column9: Any long flat strip for tying or carrying: a bag strap, a ribbon, a lace. 鞋帶 and 腰帶 name particular ones. In speech it can also mean an audio or video tape.

column3: Goes with 有 or 存在, and you 缩小 or 消除 it. Only for a gap between age groups, usually parents and children; a gap in income is 差距.
column6: Wǒ hé bàba zhījiān yǒu dàigōu.
column7: There is a generation gap between my dad and me.
column9: Goes with 有 or 存在, and you 縮小 or 消除 it. Only for a gap between age groups, usually parents and children; a gap in income is 差距.

column3: Looks ahead to a little later the same day: 待会见, 我待会再打给你. 等一会 and 一会儿 are close; for later in general, use 以后.
column4: 你先坐一下，我待会就来。
column5: 你先坐一下，我待會就來。
column6: Nǐ xiān zuò yī xià, wǒ dāihuì jiù lái.
column7: Sit down for a moment; I'll be there in a while.
column9: Looks ahead to a little later the same day: 待會見, 我待會再打給你. 等一會 and 一會兒 are close; for later in general, use 以後.

column3: The same as 待会, with an -r ending added in speech. It is often followed by 再: 待会儿再说.
column6: Wǒ dāihuìr gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà.
column7: I'll call you in a moment.
column9: The same as 待會, with an -r ending added in speech. It is often followed by 再: 待會兒再說.

column3: A verb with its object built in, so it takes 了 and 个 in between: 带了路, 带个路, 给我们带路. 带路 means going along; to tell someone the way in words, say 指路.
column4: 你对这里很熟，请你带路。
column5: 你對這裡很熟，請你帶路。
column6: Nǐ duì zhèlǐ hěn shú, qǐng nǐ dàilù.
column7: You know this place well; please lead the way.
column9: A verb with its object built in, so it takes 了 and 個 in between: 帶了路, 帶個路, 給我們帶路. 帶路 means going along; to tell someone the way in words, say 指路.

column3: Where public life happens: 大街上 (out in the street), 逛大街 (stroll and shop), 大街小巷 (streets and alleys everywhere).
column6: Dàjiē shàng dàochù dōu shì rén.
column7: The streets are full of people everywhere.
column9: Where public life happens: 大街上 (out in the street), 逛大街 (stroll and shop), 大街小巷 (streets and alleys everywhere).

column3: Goes with verbs of promoting or backing: 大力发展, 大力推广, 大力支持. It is a register of news and speeches; for pushing hard with the body, 用力 is the everyday word.
column4: 政府大力支持这项计划。
column5: 政府大力支持這項計劃。
column6: Zhèngfǔ dàlì zhīchí zhè xiàng jìhuà.
column7: The government strongly supports this plan.
column9: Goes with verbs of promoting or backing: 大力發展, 大力推廣, 大力支持. It is a register of news and speeches; for pushing hard with the body, 用力 is the everyday word.

column3: The spoken word, used with 开 or 写: 开单子, 写在单子上. More formal words are 清单 for a list and 账单 for a bill.
column4: 你把要买的东西写在单子上。
column5: 你把要買的東西寫在單子上。
column6: Nǐ bǎ yào mǎi de dōngxi xiě zài dānzi shàng.
column7: Write what you want to buy on the list.
column9: The spoken word, used with 開 or 寫: 開單子, 寫在單子上. More formal words are 清單 for a list and 帳單 for a bill.

column3: A nutrition word: 富含蛋白质, 植物蛋白. It is built on 蛋白 (egg white, the classic protein food), and 蛋白 alone can also mean protein.
column6: Dòufu hányǒu hěn duō dànbáizhì.
column7: Tofu contains a lot of protein.
column9: A nutrition word: 富含蛋白質, 植物蛋白. It is built on 蛋白 (egg white, the classic protein food), and 蛋白 alone can also mean protein.

column3: Means to treat as or take for: 把他当朋友, 当作, 当真 (take seriously). 上当 is to be taken in.
column6: Tā bǎ wǒ dàng péngyou.
column7: He treats me as a friend.
column9: Means to treat as or take for: 把他當朋友, 當作, 當真 (take seriously). 上當 is to be taken in.

column3: For a computer file, Taiwan says 档案 and the mainland says 文件; on the mainland 档案 is mainly official records, such as a personnel file. It makes 档案夹 (folder) and 档案室 (records room).
column4: 学校里有每个学生的档案。
column5: 學校裡有每個學生的檔案。
column6: Xuéxiào lǐ yǒu měi ge xuéshēng de dàng'àn.
column7: The school keeps a file on every student.
column9: For a computer file, Taiwan says 檔案 and the mainland says 文件; on the mainland 檔案 is mainly official records, such as a personnel file. It makes 檔案夾 (folder) and 檔案室 (records room).

column3: Goes with 有, 没有 and 大/小: 胆量很大. It is the daring to do something risky or to speak up; 勇气 is the broader, more admirable word for courage.
column4: 他没有胆量一个人走夜路。
column5: 他沒有膽量一個人走夜路。
column6: Tā méiyǒu dǎnliàng yī ge rén zǒu yèlù.
column7: He doesn't have the nerve to walk alone at night.
column9: Goes with 有, 沒有 and 大/小: 膽量很大. It is the daring to do something risky or to speak up; 勇氣 is the broader, more admirable word for courage.

column3: A written word for the arrival of something notable: a new country, a technology, a famous person. For an ordinary baby say 出生, and for a birthday 生日.
column4: 这种新技术诞生于二十世纪。
column5: 這種新技術誕生於二十世紀。
column6: Zhè zhǒng xīn jìshù dànshēng yú èrshí shìjì.
column7: This new technology came into being in the twentieth century.
column9: A written word for the arrival of something notable: a new country, a technology, a famous person. For an ordinary baby say 出生, and for a birthday 生日.

column3: A polite way to apologize for taking someone's time: 耽误您几分钟. It also means to hold something up or let it slip: 耽误了工作, 耽误孩子的学习.
column6: Duìbuqǐ, dānwu nǐ jǐ fēnzhōng.
column7: Sorry to take a few minutes of your time.
column9: A polite way to apologize for taking someone's time: 耽誤您幾分鐘. It also means to hold something up or let it slip: 耽誤了工作, 耽誤孩子的學習.

column3: Spoken, for everyday bad luck: 真倒楣, 倒楣鬼 (a hapless person), 倒大楣 (big trouble). Taiwan writes it 倒楣, the mainland usually 倒霉, same sound.
column4: 我今天真倒楣，又下雨又迟到。
column5: 我今天真倒楣，又下雨又遲到。
column6: Wǒ jīntiān zhēn dǎoméi, yòu xià yǔ yòu chídào.
column7: I'm so unlucky today: it rained and I was late.
column9: Spoken, for everyday bad luck: 真倒楣, 倒楣鬼 (a hapless person), 倒大楣 (big trouble). Taiwan writes it 倒楣, the mainland usually 倒霉, same sound.

column3: For things with an end date: a passport, a visa, a card, a loan, a contract. 到期日 is the due date; 过期 means it has already passed, which is also what happens to food.
column4: 我的信用卡下个月到期。
column5: 我的信用卡下個月到期。
column6: Wǒ de xìnyòngkǎ xià ge yuè dàoqī.
column7: My credit card expires next month.
column9: For things with an end date: a passport, a visa, a card, a loan, a contract. 到期日 is the due date; 過期 means it has already passed, which is also what happens to food.

column3: Spoken and emphatic, often a complaint or surprise: 大清早就起床, 大清早的. 大 only adds emphasis to 清早; the plain word is 清早.
column6: Tā dàqīngzǎo jiù chūmén le.
column7: He went out at the crack of dawn.
column9: Spoken and emphatic, often a complaint or surprise: 大清早就起床, 大清早的. 大 only adds emphasis to 清早; the plain word is 清早.

column3: Also how you address her directly: 大嫂，你好. 大 marks the eldest, as in 大哥 and 大姐; the wife of a younger brother is 弟妹.
column6: Dàsǎo zuò de cài hěn hǎochī.
column7: My brother's wife cooks very well.
column9: Also how you address her directly: 大嫂，你好. 大 marks the eldest, as in 大哥 and 大姐; the wife of a younger brother is 弟妹.

column3: The part above the knee, not the whole leg; below the knee is 小腿 (the calf). 抱大腿 ('hug a thigh') is slang for latching on to someone powerful.
column4: 爬山以后，我的大腿很酸。
column5: 爬山以後，我的大腿很酸。
column6: Páshān yǐhòu, wǒ de dàtuǐ hěn suān.
column7: After climbing the mountain, my thighs ache.
column9: The part above the knee, not the whole leg; below the knee is 小腿 (the calf). 抱大腿 ('hug a thigh') is slang for latching on to someone powerful.

column3: The gist of something said or written: 文章大意, 故事大意. You ask for it with 说说大意, and give it with 大意是…
column4: 请你说说这篇文章的大意。
column5: 請你說說這篇文章的大意。
column6: Qǐng nǐ shuōshuo zhè piān wénzhāng de dàyì.
column7: Please tell me the gist of this article.
column9: The gist of something said or written: 文章大意, 故事大意. You ask for it with 說說大意, and give it with 大意是…

column3: Written style, in news and speeches: 大有 before a two-syllable word, as in 大有希望 and 大有好处. In casual speech people say 很有 instead.
column6: Tā de Zhōngwén dàyǒu jìnbù.
column7: His Chinese has improved greatly.
column9: Written style, in news and speeches: 大有 before a two-syllable word, as in 大有希望 and 大有好處. In casual speech people say 很有 instead.

column3: A verb with its object, so it splits: 打个招呼, 打了招呼. The person goes after 跟: 跟他打招呼. It can be a wave or a nod, not only words. 打 here is the light verb that fits many objects, as in 打电话 (make a phone call).
column6: Tā zài lù shàng gēn wǒ dǎzhāohu.
column7: He greeted me on the street.
column9: A verb with its object, so it splits: 打個招呼, 打了招呼. The person goes after 跟: 跟他打招呼. It can be a wave or a nod, not only words. 打 here is the light verb that fits many objects, as in 打電話 (make a phone call).

column3: Splits like a verb with its object: 打了很多字. Speed repeats the verb: 打字打得很快. The thing typed can be the language: 打中文, 打英文.
column6: Tā dǎzì dǎ de hěn kuài.
column7: He types very fast.
column9: Splits like a verb with its object: 打了很多字. Speed repeats the verb: 打字打得很快. The thing typed can be the language: 打中文, 打英文.

column3: A verb with its object, so it splits: 得了奖, 得过奖. Add 者 for the winner (得奖者) or 作品 for the work (得奖作品). 获奖 is the more formal written word.
column6: Tā de diànyǐng déjiǎng le.
column7: His film won a prize.
column9: A verb with its object, so it splits: 得了獎, 得過獎. Add 者 for the winner (得獎者) or 作品 for the work (得獎作品). 獲獎 is the more formal written word.

column3: Rarely said alone: speech uses 凳子, and the character shows up in compounds like 板凳 (wooden bench). A seat with no back, where 椅子 has one.
column6: Tā bān le ge xiǎo dèng zi zuò xià.
column7: He brought over a small stool and sat down.
column9: Rarely said alone: speech uses 凳子, and the character shows up in compounds like 板凳 (wooden bench). A seat with no back, where 椅子 has one.

column3: The everyday word for a seat with no back; with a back it is 椅子. Counted with 个, and 小凳子 is the little stool a child sits or stands on.
column4: 孩子坐在小凳子上画画。
column5: 孩子坐在小凳子上畫畫。
column6: Háizi zuò zài xiǎo dèngzi shàng huà huà.
column7: The child is sitting on a small stool, drawing.
column9: The everyday word for a seat with no back; with a back it is 椅子. Counted with 個, and 小凳子 is the little stool a child sits or stands on.

column3: The negative potential form of 等: 等不及了 on its own, or before a verb: 等不及要见你. It can be eager excitement or plain impatience. 迫不及待 is the more formal match.
column4: 我等不及要看这部电影了。
column5: 我等不及要看這部電影了。
column6: Wǒ děngbùjí yào kàn zhè bù diànyǐng le.
column7: I can't wait to see this movie.
column9: The negative potential form of 等: 等不及了 on its own, or before a verb: 等不及要見你. It can be eager excitement or plain impatience. 迫不及待 is the more formal match.

column3: To get on someone's bad side, often without meaning to, by something said or done: 得罪人, 得罪了老板. A real crime is 犯罪, not 得罪.
column6: Wǒ bù xiǎng dézui rènhé rén.
column7: I don't want to offend anyone.
column9: To get on someone's bad side, often without meaning to, by something said or done: 得罪人, 得罪了老板. A real crime is 犯罪, not 得罪.

column3: Rarely used alone; learn it in compounds: 抵达 (in news of flights and trains), 抵抗 (resist), 抵押 (put up as security).
column6: Fēijī yǐjīng dǐ dá Táiběi le.
column7: The plane has arrived in Taipei.
column9: Rarely used alone; learn it in compounds: 抵達 (in news of flights and trains), 抵抗 (resist), 抵押 (put up as security).

column3: The verb takes the liquid: 滴水, 滴眼药水 (put in eye drops). As a measure word it counts drops: 一滴水, 一滴眼泪. 水滴 is the drop itself.
column6: Shuǐlóngtóu yīzhí zài dī shuǐ.
column7: The faucet keeps dripping.
column9: The verb takes the liquid: 滴水, 滴眼藥水 (put in eye drops). As a measure word it counts drops: 一滴水, 一滴眼淚. 水滴 is the drop itself.

column3: A pad in 坐垫 (seat cushion) and 床垫 (mattress); as a verb it puts something under to prop it up: 垫高. 垫钱 is to cover a cost first and be paid back.
column4: 我先垫钱，你回来再还我。
column5: 我先墊錢，你回來再還我。
column6: Wǒ xiān diàn qián, nǐ huílái zài huán wǒ.
column7: I'll pay first, and you can pay me back when you return.
column9: A pad in 坐墊 (seat cushion) and 床墊 (mattress); as a verb it puts something under to prop it up: 墊高. 墊錢 is to cover a cost first and be paid back.

column3: The service is long outdated, so you meet the word in history, old films and stories: 发电报 (send a telegram), 电报局 (telegraph office).
column6: Yéye niánqīng shí fā guo diànbào.
column7: Grandpa sent telegrams when he was young.
column9: The service is long outdated, so you meet the word in history, old films and stories: 發電報 (send a telegram), 電報局 (telegraph office).

column3: Goes before what it powers: 电动车, 电动牙刷, 电动门. In Taiwan 打电动 is also the everyday way to say play video games, where the mainland says 玩游戏.
column6: Tā qí diàndòng chē shàng bān.
column7: He goes to work on an electric scooter.
column9: Goes before what it powers: 電動車, 電動牙刷, 電動門. In Taiwan 打電動 is also the everyday way to say play video games, where the mainland says 玩遊戲.

column3: Plug-in household things such as refrigerators, fans and TVs; 家用电器 is the full phrase. Computers and phones are usually 电子产品 instead.
column4: 这家店卖各种家用电器。
column5: 這家店賣各種家用電器。
column6: Zhè jiā diàn mài gè zhǒng jiāyòng diànqì.
column7: This shop sells all kinds of household appliances.
column9: Plug-in household things such as refrigerators, fans and TVs; 家用電器 is the full phrase. Computers and phones are usually 電子產品 instead.

column3: The short form of 电风扇, in speech: 开电扇, 关电扇. The same 扇 is also the measure word for doors and windows.
column4: 天气太热了，我开电扇吧。
column5: 天氣太熱了，我開電扇吧。
column6: Tiānqì tài rè le, wǒ kāi diànshàn ba.
column7: It is too hot; let me turn on the fan.
column9: The short form of 電風扇, in speech: 開電扇, 關電扇. The same 扇 is also the measure word for doors and windows.

column3: The full form, counted with 台; in speech it shortens to 电扇 or 风扇. A ceiling fan is 吊扇.
column6: Jiàoshì lǐ yǒu liǎng tái diànfēngshàn.
column7: There are two electric fans in the classroom.
column9: The full form, counted with 台; in speech it shortens to 電扇 or 風扇. A ceiling fan is 吊扇.

column3: A spoken word for the cable that carries power: 拉电线 (run wires), 电线杆 (utility pole). A charging cable is 充电线, with the same 线.
column4: 这条电线太旧了，很危险。
column5: 這條電線太舊了，很危險。
column6: Zhè tiáo diànxiàn tài jiù le, hěn wēixiǎn.
column7: This wire is too old and dangerous.
column9: A spoken word for the cable that carries power: 拉電線 (run wires), 電線桿 (utility pole). A charging cable is 充電線, with the same 線.

column3: Goes straight before its noun: 电子书 (ebook), 电子邮件 (email), 电子产品 (gadgets), 电子支付 (digital payment). 电动 is the one for things powered by electricity.
column4: 我昨天买了一本电子书。
column5: 我昨天買了一本電子書。
column6: Wǒ zuótiān mǎi le yī běn diànzǐ shū.
column7: I bought an ebook yesterday.
column9: Goes straight before its noun: 電子書 (ebook), 電子郵件 (email), 電子產品 (gadgets), 電子支付 (digital payment). 電動 is the one for things powered by electricity.

column3: 吊灯 (hanging lamp), 吊扇 (ceiling fan), 吊桥 (suspension bridge) and 吊车 (crane) all hang from above. For an IV drip Taiwan says 吊点滴, the mainland 打点滴 or 输液.
column6: Kètīng lǐ diào zhe yī zhǎn dà dēng.
column7: A big lamp hangs in the living room.
column9: 吊燈 (hanging lamp), 吊扇 (ceiling fan), 吊橋 (suspension bridge) and 吊車 (crane) all hang from above. For an IV drip Taiwan says 吊點滴, the mainland 打點滴 or 輸液.

column3: Almost always with 鱼: 钓鱼, and 钓竿 for the rod. It also reaches online scams, as in 钓鱼网站 (a phishing site).
column4: 他钓了一整天，什么也没钓到。
column5: 他釣了一整天，什麼也沒釣到。
column6: Tā diào le yī zhěng tiān, shénme yě méi diào dào.
column7: He fished all day and caught nothing.
column9: Almost always with 魚: 釣魚, and 釣竿 for the rod. It also reaches online scams, as in 釣魚網站 (a phishing site).

column3: Both a verb and a noun, for wood, stone or jade: 雕刻家 (sculptor), 雕刻品 (a carved piece). Short forms are 木雕, 石雕 and 玉雕.
column4: 他在木头上雕刻了一只小鸟。
column5: 他在木頭上雕刻了一隻小鳥。
column6: Tā zài mùtou shàng diāokè le yī zhī xiǎo niǎo.
column7: He carved a little bird in the wood.
column9: Both a verb and a noun, for wood, stone or jade: 雕刻家 (sculptor), 雕刻品 (a carved piece). Short forms are 木雕, 石雕 and 玉雕.

column3: A verb with its object, so it splits: 钓到鱼, 钓了一条鱼, 钓不到鱼. The figure 'phishing' is 钓鱼邮件 (phishing email) and 钓鱼网站.
column6: Zhōumò wǒmen qù hǎibiān diàoyú.
column7: On weekends we go fishing by the sea.
column9: A verb with its object, so it splits: 釣到魚, 釣了一條魚, 釣不到魚. The figure 'phishing' is 釣魚郵件 (phishing email) and 釣魚網站.

column3: The figurative slump is the common sense, for business, a career or a mood: 陷入低潮, 低潮期. The opposite 高潮 is also the climax of a story, film or party.
column4: 公司的生意进入了低潮。
column5: 公司的生意進入了低潮。
column6: Gōngsī de shēngyi jìnrù le dīcháo.
column7: The company's business has hit a slump.
column9: The figurative slump is the common sense, for business, a career or a mood: 陷入低潮, 低潮期. The opposite 高潮 is also the climax of a story, film or party.

column3: Said of a person falling and of numbers going down: 跌倒, 下跌, 股票大跌, 价格下跌. For prices going up the word is 涨.
column6: Zuìjìn gǔpiào yīzhí zài diē.
column7: Stocks have been falling lately.
column9: Said of a person falling and of numbers going down: 跌倒, 下跌, 股票大跌, 價格下跌. For prices going up the word is 漲.

column3: Losing your footing and ending on the ground: 小心跌倒. More written, and the usual word in Taiwan; spoken mainland Chinese prefers 摔倒. 跌倒了再爬起来 means trying again after a failure.
column6: Xiǎohái pǎo de tài kuài, diēdǎo le.
column7: The child ran too fast and fell down.
column9: Losing your footing and ending on the ground: 小心跌倒. More written, and the usual word in Taiwan; spoken mainland Chinese prefers 摔倒. 跌倒了再爬起來 means trying again after a failure.

column3: Very common in health talk as 抵抗力 (the body's resistance): 增强抵抗力. 抗 alone builds anti- words, such as 抗体 (antibody) and 抗议 (protest).
column4: 多运动可以增加身体的抵抗力。
column5: 多運動可以增加身體的抵抗力。
column6: Duō yùndòng kěyǐ zēngjiā shēntǐ de dǐkàng lì.
column7: Exercise can raise the body's resistance.
column9: Very common in health talk as 抵抗力 (the body's resistance): 增強抵抗力. 抗 alone builds anti- words, such as 抗體 (antibody) and 抗議 (protest).

column3: On its own you mostly meet it as a small cube: 肉丁 (diced meat), 切成丁. It is also a common surname and the fourth of the Heavenly Stems, after 甲, 乙, 丙.
column6: Māma bǎ luóbo qiē chéng xiǎo dīng.
column7: Mom cut the radish into small cubes.
column9: On its own you mostly meet it as a small cube: 肉丁 (diced meat), 切成丁. It is also a common surname and the fourth of the Heavenly Stems, after 甲, 乙, 丙.

column3: Usually with 着: 盯着我看, 盯着手机. It also means to keep watch on a person or a task: 盯紧, 盯着他把药吃了.
column6: Tā yīzhí dīng zhe wǒ kàn.
column7: He kept staring at me.
column9: Usually with 著: 盯著我看, 盯著手機. It also means to keep watch on a person or a task: 盯緊, 盯著他把藥吃了.

column3: A somewhat formal word for ordering goods or subscribing: 订购单 (order form). For a booking use 订 alone: 订票, 订房.
column6: Wǒ dìnggòu le yī tái xīn diànnǎo.
column7: I ordered a new computer.
column9: A somewhat formal word for ordering goods or subscribing: 訂購單 (order form). For a booking use 訂 alone: 訂票, 訂房.

column3: A verb with its object, so it splits: 订了婚, 跟他订婚. The engagement is a step before 结婚 and often has its own party: 订婚宴.
column6: Tāmen dǎsuàn míngnián dìnghūn.
column7: They plan to get engaged next year.
column9: A verb with its object, so it splits: 訂了婚, 跟他訂婚. The engagement is a step before 結婚 and often has its own party: 訂婚宴.

column3: Something laid over a floor: 铺地毯, 红地毯 (red carpet, as at a premiere). 毯子 alone is a blanket, also 毛毯.
column4: 客厅里铺着一块红色的地毯。
column5: 客廳裡鋪著一塊紅色的地毯。
column6: Kètīng lǐ pū zhe yī kuài hóngsè de dìtǎn.
column7: A red carpet is laid in the living room.
column9: Something laid over a floor: 鋪地毯, 紅地毯 (red carpet, as at a premiere). 毯子 alone is a blanket, also 毛毯.

column3: A verb with its object, so it splits: 丢了脸, 丢什么脸. It is shame before other people: 让父母丢脸. Stronger than 不好意思, which is mild embarrassment.
column6: Kǎoshì zuòbì tài diūliǎn le.
column7: Cheating on an exam is so disgraceful.
column9: A verb with its object, so it splits: 丟了臉, 丟什麼臉. It is shame before other people: 讓父母丟臉. Stronger than 不好意思, which is mild embarrassment.

column3: The blunter, more spoken match for 丢脸: 真丢人, 太丢人了. 丢人现眼 is the stronger set phrase for making a fool of yourself in public.
column4: 在大家面前摔倒，真丢人。
column5: 在大家面前摔倒，真丟人。
column6: Zài dàjiā miànqián shuāidǎo, zhēn diūrén.
column7: Falling down in front of everyone was so embarrassing.
column9: The blunter, more spoken match for 丟臉: 真丟人, 太丟人了. 丟人現眼 is the stronger set phrase for making a fool of yourself in public.

column3: The measure word for a whole building: 一栋房子, 一栋大楼, 整栋. Floors are counted with 层, so one 栋 can hold many floors.
column6: Zhè dòng dàlóu yǒu èrshí céng.
column7: This building has twenty floors.
column9: The measure word for a whole building: 一棟房子, 一棟大樓, 整棟. Floors are counted with 層, so one 棟 can hold many floors.

column3: Pairs with 就: 动不动就哭, 动不动就感冒. The speaker is complaining that something happens too easily, so it is for bad habits, not good ones.
column6: Tā dòngbudòng jiù shēngqì.
column7: He gets angry at the slightest thing.
