column9: Said after a failure or setback, usually as advice: 別灰心, 不要灰心. Fixed phrase: 灰心喪氣.

column3: Overlooking by accident or carelessness: 忽略细节, 容易被忽略. Its near-synonym 忽视 is stronger and may be deliberate. 忽 also means suddenly.
column4: 我们不能忽略这个问题。
column5: 我們不能忽略這個問題。
column6: Wǒmen bù néng hūlüè zhège wèntí.
column7: We cannot overlook this problem.
column9: Overlooking by accident or carelessness: 忽略細節, 容易被忽略. Its near-synonym 忽視 is stronger and may be deliberate. 忽 also means suddenly.

column3: Common in 混合, 混乱 and 混血. In speech it also means to hang out or drift along: 混日子, 在外面混, 混熟 (to get familiar with someone).
column6: Tā zài yǎnyìquān hùn le shí nián.
column7: He has made his way in showbiz for ten years.
column9: Common in 混合, 混亂 and 混血. In speech it also means to hang out or drift along: 混日子, 在外面混, 混熟 (to get familiar with someone).

column3: A sudden faint, often from heat or shock. In Taiwan 昏倒 is the everyday word; on the mainland 晕倒 is the usual one.
column6: Tā zhòngshǔ hūndǎo le.
column7: He fainted from heatstroke.
column9: A sudden faint, often from heat or shock. In Taiwan 昏倒 is the everyday word; on the mainland 暈倒 is the usual one.

column3: The things mixed are materials or kinds: 混合两种颜色, 混合物, 混合动力 (hybrid cars), 混合双打 (mixed doubles). It is not for hanging out, which is plain 混.
column4: 把红色和黄色混合起来。
column5: 把紅色和黃色混合起來。
column6: Bǎ hóngsè hé huángsè hùnhé qǐlái.
column7: Mix the red and the yellow together.
column9: The things mixed are materials or kinds: 混合兩種顏色, 混合物, 混合動力 (hybrid cars), 混合雙打 (mixed doubles). It is not for hanging out, which is plain 混.

column3: A longer state than 昏倒, with a medical tone: 陷入昏迷, 昏迷不醒, 昏迷了三天. It is about patients and accidents.
column6: Bìngrén hūnmí le sān tiān.
column7: The patient was unconscious for three days.
column9: A longer state than 昏倒, with a medical tone: 陷入昏迷, 昏迷不醒, 昏迷了三天. It is about patients and accidents.

column3: Mostly in compounds: 车祸, 闯祸 (cause trouble), 惹祸, 祸从口出. 祸 is trouble caused by a person or a mistake, while 灾 is a natural disaster: 天灾人祸.
column6: Tā kāichē chuǎng le dà huò.
column7: He caused a disaster while driving.
column9: Mostly in compounds: 車禍, 闖禍 (cause trouble), 惹禍, 禍從口出. 禍 is trouble caused by a person or a mistake, while 災 is a natural disaster: 天災人禍.

column3: A set phrase that goes before the verb and says there is some amount without stating it. Spoken versions: 多多少少.
column4: 每个人或多或少都有压力。
column5: 每個人或多或少都有壓力。
column6: Měi ge rén huòduōhuòshǎo dōu yǒu yālì.
column7: Everyone has some stress, more or less.
column9: A set phrase that goes before the verb and says there is some amount without stating it. Spoken versions: 多多少少.

column3: Said of the bad result of someone’s own doing, and sometimes of oneself, rueful: 我活该. Spoken and can be harsh, so not for a friend who is truly hurting.
column6: Tā bù tīng quàn, huógāi!
column7: He wouldn’t listen to advice; serves him right!
column9: Said of the bad result of someone’s own doing, and sometimes of oneself, rueful: 我活該. Spoken and can be harsh, so not for a friend who is truly hurting.

column3: Goods as cargo, being shipped or stored: 货物运输, 装卸货物. A shop’s products are 商品, and 货 alone is “merchandise”: 货车, 进货.
column6: Zhèxiē huòwù míngtiān sòngdào.
column7: These goods will arrive tomorrow.
column9: Goods as cargo, being shipped or stored: 貨物運輸, 裝卸貨物. A shop’s products are 商品, and 貨 alone is “merchandise”: 貨車, 進貨.

column3: For people, markets, groups or an atmosphere; as a verb it also means to liven up: 活跃气氛. 活泼 is a lively nature (children, animals), where 活跃 is about being active.
column6: Tā zài bān shàng hěn huóyuè.
column7: He is very active in the class.
column9: For people, markets, groups or an atmosphere; as a verb it also means to liven up: 活躍氣氛. 活潑 is a lively nature (children, animals), where 活躍 is about being active.

column3: It describes activities and goods: 户外运动, 户外用品, 户外广告 (billboards). Its opposite is 室内; it is the more formal “outdoors”, where speech says 外面. 户 is one half of the gate 门. 户 also means a household, as in 户口.
column6: Wǒmen xǐhuan zài hùwài yùndòng.
column7: We like exercising outdoors.
column9: It describes activities and goods: 戶外運動, 戶外用品, 戶外廣告 (billboards). Its opposite is 室內; it is the more formal “outdoors”, where speech says 外面. 戶 is one half of the gate 門. 戶 also means a household, as in 戶口.

column3: Written and often in slogans and group names: 邻里互助, 互助小组. In speech it is 互相帮助.
column6: Línjū zhījiān yīnggāi hùzhù.
column7: Neighbors should help each other.
column9: Written and often in slogans and group names: 鄰里互助, 互助小組. In speech it is 互相幫助.

column3: Beyond gathering it counts TV episodes (第三集), names a collection (诗集, 文集), and a rural market day (赶集). 集 shows a bird 隹 and a tree 木.
column4: 这部电视剧一共有三十集。
column5: 這部電視劇一共有三十集。
column6: Zhè bù diànshìjù yīgòng yǒu sānshí jí.
column7: This TV series has thirty episodes in all.
column9: Beyond gathering it counts TV episodes (第三集), names a collection (詩集, 文集), and a rural market day (趕集). 集 shows a bird 隹 and a tree 木.

column3: The woman is the one who 嫁; the man takes a wife with 娶. Forms: 嫁给, 嫁人, 出嫁 and 嫁女儿 for a parent marrying off a daughter. 嫁 is built on 家 “home” and meant to go to one’s new home, to become married.
column6: Tā jià gěi le yī ge yīshēng.
column7: She married a doctor.
column9: The woman is the one who 嫁; the man takes a wife with 娶. Forms: 嫁給, 嫁人, 出嫁 and 嫁女兒 for a parent marrying off a daughter. 嫁 is built on 家 “home” and meant to go to one’s new home, to become married.

column3: Short for 家用电器. 大家电 are the big ones (refrigerator, washing machine) and 小家电 the small ones (rice cooker, kettle). A store is a 家电店.
column6: Zhè jiā shāngdiàn mài gèzhǒng jiādiàn.
column7: This store sells all kinds of household appliances.
column9: Short for 家用電器. 大家電 are the big ones (refrigerator, washing machine) and 小家電 the small ones (rice cooker, kettle). A store is a 家電店.

column3: Counted with 支. 射箭 is archery, 箭头 an arrowhead or an arrow sign, and 火箭 a rocket. 一箭双雕 is “two birds with one stone”.
column6: Tā yī jiàn shèzhòng le bǎxīn.
column7: He hit the bullseye with one arrow.
column9: Counted with 支. 射箭 is archery, 箭頭 an arrowhead or an arrow sign, and 火箭 a rocket. 一箭雙鵰 is “two birds with one stone”.

column3: Picking out from many. Speech prefers 挑 (挑选); 拣 lives on in 挑拣 and 拣选. Not 捡, which is picking up what lies on the ground.
column4: 把好的拣出来，坏的扔掉。
column5: 把好的揀出來，壞的扔掉。
column6: Bǎ hǎo de jiǎn chū lái, huài de rēng diào.
column7: Pick out the good ones and throw away the bad.
column9: Picking out from many. Speech prefers 挑 (挑選); 揀 lives on in 挑揀 and 揀選. Not 撿, which is picking up what lies on the ground.

column3: Often finding something by luck: 捡到钱, 捡便宜 (get a bargain). For choosing among several, see 拣.
column4: 我在路上捡到一个钱包。
column5: 我在路上撿到一個錢包。
column6: Wǒ zài lù shàng jiǎn dào yī ge qiánbāo.
column7: I found a wallet on the road.
column9: Often finding something by luck: 撿到錢, 撿便宜 (get a bargain). For choosing among several, see 揀.

column3: Works for a shape, a sound and the senses: 笔尖 is a pen tip, 尖叫 a scream, and 耳朵很尖 means sharp hearing. As a noun it is the tip or point of something.
column6: Lǎoshǔ de zuǐba shì jiān de.
column7: A mouse's snout is pointed.
column9: Works for a shape, a sound and the senses: 筆尖 is a pen tip, 尖叫 a scream, and 耳朵很尖 means sharp hearing. As a noun it is the tip or point of something.

column3: Adds a second job or role to the main one, before a verb or noun: 兼职 is a side or part-time job, 老师兼司机 a teacher who also drives. 兼顾 is to look after both at once.
column6: Tā jiān le liǎng fèn gōngzuò.
column7: He holds two jobs at once.
column9: Adds a second job or role to the main one, before a verb or noun: 兼職 is a side or part-time job, 老師兼司機 a teacher who also drives. 兼顧 is to look after both at once.

column3: Pan-frying in a little oil, so 煎蛋, 煎鱼, 煎饺, 煎牛排; deep-frying is 炸. It also means simmering herbal medicine in water: 煎药.
column6: Māma jiān le liǎng ge dàn.
column7: Mom fried two eggs.
column9: Pan-frying in a little oil, so 煎蛋, 煎魚, 煎餃, 煎牛排; deep-frying is 炸. It also means simmering herbal medicine in water: 煎藥.

column3: The thing handed to a winner: 得到奖品, 领奖品, 比赛的奖品. Prize money is 奖金, and 奖 alone is the award itself.
column4: 比赛的奖品是一台电脑。
column5: 比賽的獎品是一台電腦。
column6: Bǐsài de jiǎngpǐn shì yī tái diànnǎo.
column7: The prize of the contest is a computer.
column9: The thing handed to a winner: 得到獎品, 領獎品, 比賽的獎品. Prize money is 獎金, and 獎 alone is the award itself.

column3: Mostly heard as a time marker for a country's early years: 建国初期, 建国以来 "since the founding". It also turns up in street and school names, such as 建国路.
column6: Zhège guójiā gāng jiànguó bù jiǔ.
column7: This country was founded not long ago.
column9: Mostly heard as a time marker for a country's early years: 建國初期, 建國以來 "since the founding". It also turns up in street and school names, such as 建國路.

column3: Pointed rather than keen-edged: sharp objects, a shrill sound (尖锐的声音), sharp criticism, a conflict come to a head (矛盾尖锐). A knife that cuts well is 锋利.
column6: Tā de shēngyīn yòu gāo yòu jiānruì.
column7: Her voice is high and shrill.
column9: Pointed rather than keen-edged: sharp objects, a shrill sound (尖銳的聲音), sharp criticism, a conflict come to a head (矛盾尖銳). A knife that cuts well is 鋒利.

column3: Close watch kept by police or an authority, usually on someone suspected: 警察监视嫌疑人, 被监视. For the camera itself, Taiwan says 监视器 and the mainland 监控 or 摄像头.
column6: Jǐngchá zài jiānshì tā de xíngdòng.
column7: The police are watching his movements.
column9: Close watch kept by police or an authority, usually on someone suspected: 警察監視嫌疑人, 被監視. For the camera itself, Taiwan says 監視器 and the mainland 監控 or 攝像頭.

column3: The prison as a building or institution: 关进监狱, 监狱生活, and 越狱 is a jailbreak. Serving a sentence is 坐牢, which is what people say in speech.
column4: 他因为偷东西进了监狱。
column5: 他因為偷東西進了監獄。
column6: Tā yīnwèi tōu dōngxi jìn le jiānyù.
column7: He went to prison for stealing.
column9: The prison as a building or institution: 關進監獄, 監獄生活, and 越獄 is a jailbreak. Serving a sentence is 坐牢, which is what people say in speech.

column3: For official or compulsory payments: 缴费, 缴税. At a shop you 付钱 instead; 缴 is what you owe an institution.
column6: Míngtiān yào jiǎo xuéfèi.
column7: The tuition is due tomorrow.
column9: For official or compulsory payments: 繳費, 繳稅. At a shop you 付錢 instead; 繳 is what you owe an institution.

column3: Pouring liquid over something: 浇花, 浇水, 浇熄. Figuratively 浇冷水 is to pour cold water on someone's enthusiasm or plans.
column6: Tā měi tiān zǎoshang jiāo huā.
column7: She waters the flowers every morning.
column9: Pouring liquid over something: 澆花, 澆水, 澆熄. Figuratively 澆冷水 is to pour cold water on someone's enthusiasm or plans.

column3: Loud, often prolonged yelling: 大声叫喊, 拼命叫喊. To call someone over, use 喊 or 叫: 喊他过来.
column6: Tā zài chuāngkǒu dàshēng jiàohǎn.
column7: He shouted loudly from the window.
column9: Loud, often prolonged yelling: 大聲叫喊, 拼命叫喊. To call someone over, use 喊 or 叫: 喊他過來.

column3: The church as an organization or congregation: 去教会, 基督教会. The building itself is 教堂.
column4: 她每个星期天都去教会。
column5: 她每個星期天都去教會。
column6: Tā měi ge xīngqītiān dōu qù jiàohuì.
column7: She goes to church every Sunday.
column9: The church as an organization or congregation: 去教會, 基督教會. The building itself is 教堂.

column3: A corner inside a space, or a remote spot: 房间的角落, 世界的每个角落. For a street corner say 街角.
column6: Tā zuò zài jiàoshì de jiǎoluò.
column7: He sits in the corner of the classroom.
column9: A corner inside a space, or a remote spot: 房間的角落, 世界的每個角落. For a street corner say 街角.

column3: Where city people go for fresh air: 到郊外走走, 郊外踏青, 在郊外野餐. It is the countryside you travel out to, not where you live; the suburbs where people live are 郊区.
column4: 星期天我们去郊外野餐。
column5: 星期天我們去郊外野餐。
column6: Xīngqītiān wǒmen qù jiāowài yěcān.
column7: On Sunday we go on a picnic in the countryside.
column9: Where city people go for fresh air: 到郊外走走, 郊外踏青, 在郊外野餐. It is the countryside you travel out to, not where you live; the suburbs where people live are 郊區.

column3: In Taiwan 做家事 is the usual way to say doing housework, where the mainland says 做家务. 家事 also means family matters, as in 家事法庭 "family court".
column6: Wǒ hé zhàngfu yīqǐ zuò jiāshì.
column7: My husband and I do the chores together.
column9: In Taiwan 做家事 is the usual way to say doing housework, where the mainland says 做家務. 家事 also means family matters, as in 家事法庭 "family court".

column3: Formal and found in compounds: 驾车, 驾驶, 驾照 "driver's license", 酒驾 "drunk driving". In everyday speech people say 开车.
column6: Tā jià chē qù le Táizhōng.
column7: He drove to Taichung.
column9: Formal and found in compounds: 駕車, 駕駛, 駕照 "driver's license", 酒駕 "drunk driving". In everyday speech people say 開車.

column3: The formal, general word for illness as a category: 慢性疾病, 预防疾病. For being sick yourself, speech uses 病: 我病了.
column4: 运动可以预防很多疾病。
column5: 運動可以預防很多疾病。
column6: Yùndòng kěyǐ yùfáng hěn duō jíbìng.
column7: Exercise can prevent many illnesses.
column9: The formal, general word for illness as a category: 慢性疾病, 預防疾病. For being sick yourself, speech uses 病: 我病了.

column3: Resentment of what another person has, whether success, looks or a relationship: 嫉妒别人, 嫉妒心. 羡慕 is the milder, admiring "I wish I had that".
column6: Tā hěn jídù péngyou de chéngjì.
column7: He is very jealous of his friend's grades.
column9: Resentment of what another person has, whether success, looks or a relationship: 嫉妒別人, 嫉妒心. 羨慕 is the milder, admiring "I wish I had that".

column3: The same word as 嫉妒, used the same way: 忌妒别人, 不要忌妒. On its own 忌 is to avoid, as in 忌口 (avoiding certain foods) and 禁忌 "taboo".
column6: Bié jìdu biérén de chénggōng.
column7: Don't envy other people's success.
column9: The same word as 嫉妒, used the same way: 忌妒別人, 不要忌妒. On its own 忌 is to avoid, as in 忌口 (avoiding certain foods) and 禁忌 "taboo".

column3: Seldom alone; it is in words like 解开, 解决, 解释, 了解 and 解散. The core idea is taking apart: a knot is 解开, a problem 解决, a doubt 解答.
column6: Zhège jié wǒ jiě bù kāi.
column7: I can't untie this knot.
column9: Seldom alone; it is in words like 解開, 解決, 解釋, 了解 and 解散. The core idea is taking apart: a knot is 解開, a problem 解決, a doubt 解答.

column3: Formal: clearing up a question or difficulty someone has raised: 解答问题, 为你解答. As a noun, the answer itself. Plain 回答 just replies; 解答 explains.
column4: 老师耐心地解答我们的问题。
column5: 老師耐心地解答我們的問題。
column6: Lǎoshī nàixīn de jiědá wǒmen de wèntí.
column7: The teacher patiently answered our questions.
column9: Formal: clearing up a question or difficulty someone has raised: 解答問題, 為你解答. As a noun, the answer itself. Plain 回答 just replies; 解答 explains.

column3: Formal: the senior person receives visitors, as in 总统接见外宾 or 接见记者. A visitor never 接见s an official; for an ordinary meeting use 见面.
column4: 总统接见了外国的客人。
column5: 總統接見了外國的客人。
column6: Zǒngtǒng jiējiàn le wàiguó de kèrén.
column7: The president received the foreign guests.
column9: Formal: the senior person receives visitors, as in 總統接見外賓 or 接見記者. A visitor never 接見s an official; for an ordinary meeting use 見面.

column3: Covers a festival and the events around it: 传统节庆, 节庆活动. A single named holiday is a 节日. This 节 is the one in 春节 and 中秋节, from the sense "seasonal festival".
column6: Chūnjié shì zuì zhòngyào de jiéqìng.
column7: The Lunar New Year is the most important festival.
column9: Covers a festival and the events around it: 傳統節慶, 節慶活動. A single named holiday is a 節日. This 節 is the one in 春節 and 中秋節, from the sense "seasonal festival".

column3: The final tally when accounts are closed: 月底结算, 结算薪水, 结算金额. At a shop counter you 结账 instead.
column4: 公司每个月底都要结算。
column5: 公司每個月底都要結算。
column6: Gōngsī měi ge yuèdǐ dōu yào jiésuàn.
column7: The company settles accounts at the end of every month.
column9: The final tally when accounts are closed: 月底結算, 結算薪水, 結算金額. At a shop counter you 結帳 instead.

column3: The street as a public scene rather than a physical road: 街头艺人, 街头小吃, 流落街头 "end up on the street".
column4: 街头有很多卖小吃的摊子。
column5: 街頭有很多賣小吃的攤子。
column6: Jiētóu yǒu hěn duō mài xiǎochī de tānzi.
column7: There are many snack stalls in the street.
column9: The street as a public scene rather than a physical road: 街頭藝人, 街頭小吃, 流落街頭 "end up on the street".

column3: A boundary on a map or in the mind: 国界线, and 划清界线 "draw a clear line" between yourself and someone or something. Also the dividing line between right and wrong.
column4: 白色的线是两块地的界线。
column5: 白色的線是兩塊地的界線。
column6: Báisè de xiàn shì liǎng kuài dì de jièxiàn.
column7: The white line is the border between the two plots.
column9: A boundary on a map or in the mind: 國界線, and 劃清界線 "draw a clear line" between yourself and someone or something. Also the dividing line between right and wrong.

column3: What you say to a waiter or cashier when you are done: 我要结帐, 请结帐. On the mainland the table-side word is also 买单.
column6: Bù hǎoyìsi, wǒ yào jiézhàng.
column7: Excuse me, I'd like to pay.
column9: What you say to a waiter or cashier when you are done: 我要結帳, 請結帳. On the mainland the table-side word is also 買單.

column3: Used for a deadline or cut-off: 报名截止, 截止日期. 截止到 + a date means "up to that date", as in 截止到昨天, 已有五百人报名.
column6: Bàomíng dào míngtiān jiézhǐ.
column7: Registration closes tomorrow.
column9: Used for a deadline or cut-off: 報名截止, 截止日期. 截止到 + a date means "up to that date", as in 截止到昨天, 已有五百人報名.

column3: You wear it with 戴: 戴戒指, 结婚戒指. On its own 戒 is to give up a habit: 戒烟, 戒酒.
column6: Tā sòng tā yī ge zuànshí jièzhi.
column7: He gave her a diamond ring.
column9: You wear it with 戴: 戴戒指, 結婚戒指. On its own 戒 is to give up a habit: 戒煙, 戒酒.

column3: Two senses: a government body (政府机关) and a hidden mechanism or trap (暗藏机关, 机关枪 "machine gun"); context tells which. 机 is the same one as in 飞机 and 手机.
column6: Tā zài zhèngfǔ jīguān gōngzuò.
column7: He works in a government agency.
column9: Two senses: a government body (政府機關) and a hidden mechanism or trap (暗藏機關, 機關槍 "machine gun"); context tells which. 機 is the same one as in 飛機 and 手機.

column3: Fussing over small gains, losses or slights; mostly in the negative: 不要计较, 别跟他计较, 斤斤计较 "nitpicking".
column6: Tā cóng bù jìjiào zhèxiē xiǎoshì.
column7: He never fusses over such small matters.
column9: Fussing over small gains, losses or slights; mostly in the negative: 不要計較, 別跟他計較, 斤斤計較 "nitpicking".

column3: The empty feeling of missing company, while 孤单 stresses being alone: 感到寂寞. A place or night can be 寂寞 too. In Taiwan the first character is read jí rather than jì.
column4: 一个人住，有时候会觉得寂寞。
column5: 一個人住，有時候會覺得寂寞。
column6: Yī ge rén zhù, yǒu shíhou huì juéde jìmò.
column7: Living alone, one sometimes feels lonely.
column9: The empty feeling of missing company, while 孤單 stresses being alone: 感到寂寞. A place or night can be 寂寞 too. In Taiwan the first character is read jí rather than jì.

column3: Staying in liquid, wanted or not: 浸泡 beans, 浸湿 "soaked through", a flood 浸水. 沉浸 carries it into "immersed in" music or memories.
column4: 把豆子浸在水里一个晚上。
column5: 把豆子浸在水裡一個晚上。
column6: Bǎ dòuzi jìn zài shuǐ lǐ yī ge wǎnshang.
column7: Soak the beans in water overnight.
column9: Staying in liquid, wanted or not: 浸泡 beans, 浸濕 "soaked through", a flood 浸水. 沉浸 carries it into "immersed in" music or memories.

column3: The figure written on a bill, receipt or transfer: 总金额, 请确认金额. The 额 is the same one as in 余额 "balance" and 名额 "quota".
column6: Qǐng quèrèn jīn'é shìfǒu zhèngquè.
column7: Please confirm the amount is correct.
column9: The figure written on a bill, receipt or transfer: 總金額, 請確認金額. The 額 is the same one as in 餘額 "balance" and 名額 "quota".

column3: Goes right before the verb and carries the speaker's surprise: 竟敢 is "to have the nerve to". 竟然 is the more usual spoken form, 竟 the shorter, more written one.
column4: 他竟忘了今天是我的生日。
column5: 他竟忘了今天是我的生日。
column6: Tā jìng wàng le jīntiān shì wǒ de shēngrì.
column7: He actually forgot that today is my birthday.
column9: Goes right before the verb and carries the speaker's surprise: 竟敢 is "to have the nerve to". 竟然 is the more usual spoken form, 竟 the shorter, more written one.

column3: Bound: say 镜子 for a mirror and 眼镜 for glasses; 镜头 is a camera lens and also a shot in a film. 镜 is the same in 望远镜 and 显微镜.
column4: 她站在镜子前面看自己。
column5: 她站在鏡子前面看自己。
column6: Tā zhàn zài jìng zi qiánmiàn kàn zìjǐ.
column7: She stands in front of the mirror and looks at herself.
column9: Bound: say 鏡子 for a mirror and 眼鏡 for glasses; 鏡頭 is a camera lens and also a shot in a film. 鏡 is the same in 望遠鏡 and 顯微鏡.

column3: Written and warm, for people you look up to: teachers, elders, leaders. 敬爱的老师 opens school compositions and speeches. It is not used between peers.
column6: Wǒ hěn jìng'ài wǒ de lǎoshī.
column7: I love and respect my teacher dearly.
column9: Written and warm, for people you look up to: teachers, elders, leaders. 敬愛的老師 opens school compositions and speeches. It is not used between peers.

column3: Added after a word, 化 works like English "-ize" or "-ization". So 净化 purifies air or water (空气净化器) or the mind (净化心灵), like 绿化, 美化 and 简化.
column4: 这台机器可以净化空气。
column5: 這台機器可以淨化空氣。
column6: Zhè tái jīqì kěyǐ jìnghuà kōngqì.
column7: This machine can purify the air.
column9: Added after a word, 化 works like English "-ize" or "-ization". So 淨化 purifies air or water (空氣淨化器) or the mind (淨化心靈), like 綠化, 美化 and 簡化.

column3: At banquets and weddings one person raises a glass to another or goes from table to table, while 干杯 is everyone drinking together. 敬 also offers tea: 敬茶.
column6: Xīnláng xīnniáng xiàng kèrén jìngjiǔ.
column7: The bride and groom toast their guests.
column9: At banquets and weddings one person raises a glass to another or goes from table to table, while 干杯 is everyone drinking together. 敬 also offers tea: 敬茶.

column3: A hand salute or a bow to a teacher, and the closing 此致敬礼 in letters. In Taiwan the class monitor calls 起立、敬礼、坐下 to start a lesson; on the mainland the greeting is 老师好.
column6: Xuésheng qǐlì xiàng lǎoshī jìnglǐ.
column7: The students stood and saluted the teacher.
column9: A hand salute or a bow to a teacher, and the closing 此致敬禮 in letters. In Taiwan the class monitor calls 起立、敬禮、坐下 to start a lesson; on the mainland the greeting is 老師好.

column3: Describes a speed, number or skill so extreme it stuns you, good or bad: 惊人的速度, 成绩惊人. The 惊 is the same one as in 吃惊 and 惊讶.
column4: 这个城市发展的速度很惊人。
column5: 這個城市發展的速度很驚人。
column6: Zhège chéngshì fāzhǎn de sùdù hěn jīngrén.
column7: This city is developing at an astonishing speed.
column9: Describes a speed, number or skill so extreme it stuns you, good or bad: 驚人的速度, 成績驚人. The 驚 is the same one as in 吃驚 and 驚訝.

column3: Fine as in carefully detailed: 做工精细, 精细的分工. 精 adds the refined, high-quality side seen in 精致 and 精确, while 细 alone is thin; a careful person is 细心.
column4: 这件手工艺品做得很精细。
column5: 這件手工藝品做得很精細。
column6: Zhè jiàn shǒugōngyìpǐn zuò de hěn jīngxì.
column7: This handicraft is made very finely.
column9: Fine as in carefully detailed: 做工精細, 精細的分工. 精 adds the refined, high-quality side seen in 精緻 and 精確, while 細 alone is thin; a careful person is 細心.

column3: Goes before a verb and softens a request or promise into "try to": 请尽量早点来, 尽量不要迟到. 尽 has a second reading, jǐn, "to the greatest extent".
column6: Qǐng jìnliàng zǎo diǎn lái.
column7: Please come as early as you can.
column9: Goes before a verb and softens a request or promise into "try to": 請盡量早點來, 盡量不要遲到. 盡 has a second reading, jǐn, "to the greatest extent".

column3: Money as an idea, wealth: 金钱观, 金钱关系, 金钱不是万能的. Written and a little formal; for actual amounts say 钱, as in 多少钱.
column6: Jīnqián bù shì zuì zhòngyào de.
column7: Money is not the most important thing.
column9: Money as an idea, wealth: 金錢觀, 金錢關係, 金錢不是萬能的. Written and a little formal; for actual amounts say 錢, as in 多少錢.

column3: The finance industry and system: 金融业, 金融危机 "financial crisis". A bank (ATM) card is 金融卡 in Taiwan, 银行卡 on the mainland.
column6: Tā zài jīnróng gōngsī shàngbān.
column7: He works at a financial company.
column9: The finance industry and system: 金融業, 金融危機 "financial crisis". A bank (ATM) card is 金融卡 in Taiwan, 銀行卡 on the mainland.

column3: Eyesight strength is counted in 度, so 近视三百度 is about three diopters. The opposite is 远视, and figuratively 近视 is shortsighted: someone who can't see ahead.
column6: Wǒ jìnshì sānbǎi dù.
column7: I am nearsighted by three hundred degrees.
column9: Eyesight strength is counted in 度, so 近視三百度 is about three diopters. The opposite is 遠視, and figuratively 近視 is shortsighted: someone who can't see ahead.

column3: The general category of metals as a material: 金属制品, 重金属, 金属探测器. A particular metal is named by itself, such as 铁 or 铜.
column6: Tiě hé tóng dōu shì jīnshǔ.
column7: Iron and copper are both metals.
column9: The general category of metals as a material: 金屬製品, 重金屬, 金屬探測器. A particular metal is named by itself, such as 鐵 or 銅.

column3: A reception with drinks and snacks, often standing: 参加酒会, 欢迎酒会. It is less formal than a seated banquet (宴会). The 会 is the same as in 晚会 and 舞会.
column4: 公司明天晚上有一个酒会。
column5: 公司明天晚上有一個酒會。
column6: Gōngsī míngtiān wǎnshang yǒu yī ge jiǔhuì.
column7: The company has a reception tomorrow evening.
column9: A reception with drinks and snacks, often standing: 參加酒會, 歡迎酒會. It is less formal than a seated banquet (宴會). The 會 is the same as in 晚會 and 舞會.

column3: Fighting a fire (救火车), and figuratively rushing in to solve an urgent problem. A firefighter is 消防员. 救 works the same in 救命 and 救护车.
column6: Xiāofángyuán chōng jìnqù jiùhuǒ.
column7: The firefighters rushed in to fight the fire.
column9: Fighting a fire (救火車), and figuratively rushing in to solve an urgent problem. A firefighter is 消防員. 救 works the same in 救命 and 救護車.

column3: Starts a clause to restate something or check you understood: 就是说, 你明天不来了? In explanations 也就是说 draws the conclusion, and 换句话说 is the more formal "in other words".
column6: Jiùshìshuō, nǐ míngtiān bù lái le?
column7: So, you're not coming tomorrow?
column9: Starts a clause to restate something or check you understood: 就是說, 你明天不來了? In explanations 也就是說 draws the conclusion, and 換句話說 is the more formal "in other words".

column3: The object is something that is off: 纠正错误, 纠正发音, 纠正姿势. It is usually done by someone who knows better, such as a teacher, coach or doctor; for your own mistake, 改正 is the everyday word.
column6: Lǎoshī jiūzhèng le wǒ de fāyīn.
column7: The teacher corrected my pronunciation.
column9: The object is something that is off: 糾正錯誤, 糾正發音, 糾正姿勢. It is usually done by someone who knows better, such as a teacher, coach or doctor; for your own mistake, 改正 is the everyday word.

column3: A noun for machinery and the field around it (机械工程, 机械设备), and an adjective for something rigid and repetitive: 机械式的动作. The machine itself is 机器. 械 originally meant handcuffs or shackles, and by extension came to mean a device or mechanism.
column6: Tā zài jīxiè gōngchǎng gōngzuò.
column7: He works in a machinery factory.
column9: A noun for machinery and the field around it (機械工程, 機械設備), and an adjective for something rigid and repetitive: 機械式的動作. The machine itself is 機器. 械 originally meant handcuffs or shackles, and by extension came to mean a device or mechanism.

column3: The spoken word for how well you remember things: 记性好, 记性差. The formal, written word is 记忆力. It is about the ability, not a particular memory, which is 记忆 or 回忆.
column4: 我记性不好，常常忘记东西。
column5: 我記性不好，常常忘記東西。
column6: Wǒ jìxing bù hǎo, chángcháng wàngjì dōngxi.
column7: I have a poor memory and often forget things.
column9: The spoken word for how well you remember things: 記性好, 記性差. The formal, written word is 記憶力. It is about the ability, not a particular memory, which is 記憶 or 回憶.

column3: A verb-object phrase: 邮 here stands for 邮票 (stamp), and the hobby is 集邮. A collector is a 集邮爱好者 or 集邮迷, and the album is a 集邮册. The same 邮 is in 邮局 and 邮件.
column6: Tā de àihào shì jíyóu.
column7: His hobby is stamp collecting.
column9: A verb-object phrase: 郵 here stands for 郵票 (stamp), and the hobby is 集郵. A collector is a 集郵愛好者 or 集郵迷, and the album is a 集郵冊. The same 郵 is in 郵局 and 郵件.

column3: Both the hospital department and the visit: 挂急诊, 看急诊, 急诊室. It is for what cannot wait for an appointment. The same 诊 is in 门诊 (outpatient clinic) and 诊所 (clinic).
column4: 他半夜肚子痛，去了急诊。
column5: 他半夜肚子痛，去了急診。
column6: Tā bànyè dùzi tòng, qù le jízhěn.
column7: He had a stomachache in the middle of the night and went to the emergency room.
column9: Both the hospital department and the visit: 掛急診, 看急診, 急診室. It is for what cannot wait for an appointment. The same 診 is in 門診 (outpatient clinic) and 診所 (clinic).

column3: Rarely alone: it ends words for things you use, as in 工具, 玩具, 餐具. In formal writing 具有 and 具备 mean to have a quality or ability, and 具体 means concrete.
column4: 这座城市具有悠久的历史。
column5: 這座城市具有悠久的歷史。
column6: Zhè zuò chéngshì jù yǒu yōujiǔ de lìshǐ.
column7: This city has a long history.
column9: Rarely alone: it ends words for things you use, as in 工具, 玩具, 餐具. In formal writing 具有 and 具備 mean to have a quality or ability, and 具體 means concrete.

column3: Giving money, goods or blood for a cause, with nothing in return: 捐钱, 捐衣服. The recipient follows 给: 捐给慈善机构. The money given is a 捐款. For blood, Taiwan says 捐血 and the mainland 献血.
column4: 他每年都捐钱给孤儿院。
column5: 他每年都捐錢給孤兒院。
column6: Tā měi nián dōu juān qián gěi gū'éryuàn.
column7: Every year he donates money to the orphanage.
column9: Giving money, goods or blood for a cause, with nothing in return: 捐錢, 捐衣服. The recipient follows 給: 捐給慈善機構. The money given is a 捐款. For blood, Taiwan says 捐血 and the mainland 獻血.

column3: Both verb and noun: 向灾区捐款, 一笔捐款. It is money only, while 捐 alone can be goods or blood. 款 is a sum of money in other words too: 存款, 付款, 贷款.
column6: Hěn duō rén xiàng zāiqū juānkuǎn.
column7: Many people donate money to the disaster area.
column9: Both verb and noun: 向災區捐款, 一筆捐款. It is money only, while 捐 alone can be goods or blood. 款 is a sum of money in other words too: 存款, 付款, 貸款.

column3: A planned meal for a group, such as colleagues, classmates or family: 公司聚餐, 同学聚餐. It names the get-together, while 吃饭 only says eating. In speech the verb-object splits: 聚个餐.
column4: 我们这个星期六要聚餐。
column5: 我們這個星期六要聚餐。
column6: Wǒmen zhège xīngqīliù yào jùcān.
column7: We will have a group dinner this Saturday.
column9: A planned meal for a group, such as colleagues, classmates or family: 公司聚餐, 同學聚餐. It names the get-together, while 吃飯 only says eating. In speech the verb-object splits: 聚個餐.

column3: Almost always in compounds: 巨大, 巨人, 巨星, 巨额. It is stronger and more written than 大. In young people's slang it is also an intensifier: 巨贵, 巨好吃.
column6: Zhè shì yī ge jù dà de gōngchéng.
column7: This is an enormous project.
column9: Almost always in compounds: 巨大, 巨人, 巨星, 巨額. It is stronger and more written than 大. In young people's slang it is also an intensifier: 巨貴, 巨好吃.

column3: Before 不 or 没 it means never, firmly: 决不, 决没有. Otherwise it carries the idea of deciding inside other words: 决定, 决心, 决赛 (final), 解决 (solve).
column6: Wǒ jué bù fàngqì.
column7: I will never give up.
column9: Before 不 or 沒 it means never, firmly: 決不, 決沒有. Otherwise it carries the idea of deciding inside other words: 決定, 決心, 決賽 (final), 解決 (solve).

column3: Before a negative it means absolutely: 绝不, 绝没有. Elsewhere it ends or goes to the extreme: 绝种, 绝交, 绝望, 绝对, and 绝佳 (superb). The character in its older form was a way of cutting silk threads, and the 色 inside 绝 is most likely unrelated to 色 the color.
column6: Zhè zhǒng dòngwù yǐjīng jué zhǒng le.
column7: This kind of animal has become extinct.
column9: Before a negative it means absolutely: 絕不, 絕沒有. Elsewhere it ends or goes to the extreme: 絕種, 絕交, 絕望, 絕對, and 絕佳 (superb). The character in its older form was a way of cutting silk threads, and the 色 inside 絕 is most likely unrelated to 色 the color.

column3: A flat denial or refusal, with more force than a plain 不: 绝不放弃, 绝不原谅, 绝不可能. It sits right before the verb. 决不 is nearly the same.
column6: Wǒ juébù huì fàngqì.
column7: I will never give up.
column9: A flat denial or refusal, with more force than a plain 不: 絕不放棄, 絕不原諒, 絕不可能. It sits right before the verb. 決不 is nearly the same.

column3: Followed by a plural or a mass noun, often with 都: 绝大部分学生都, 绝大部分时间. 绝大多数 is the near-synonym for counted people or things; 绝大部分 also fits time, money and amounts. In Taiwan the last syllable of 大部分 is read fèn.
column4: 绝大部分学生都通过了考试。
column5: 絕大部分學生都通過了考試。
column6: Juédàbùfen xuésheng dōu tōngguò le kǎoshì.
column7: The vast majority of students passed the exam.
column9: Followed by a plural or a mass noun, often with 都: 絕大部分學生都, 絕大部分時間. 絕大多數 is the near-synonym for counted people or things; 絕大部分 also fits time, money and amounts. In Taiwan the last syllable of 大部分 is read fèn.

column3: As a verb, a sudden clear understanding after a failure or a lesson: 终于觉悟, 觉悟到自己的错误. It is also the Buddhist word for enlightenment. As a noun it means a person's political or moral awareness: 觉悟高, 提高觉悟, a mainland phrase.
column4: 经过这次失败，他终于觉悟了。
column5: 經過這次失敗，他終於覺悟了。
column6: Jīngguò zhè cì shībài, tā zhōngyú juéwù le.
column7: After this failure he finally realized.
column9: As a verb, a sudden clear understanding after a failure or a lesson: 終於覺悟, 覺悟到自己的錯誤. It is also the Buddhist word for enlightenment. As a noun it means a person's political or moral awareness: 覺悟高, 提高覺悟, a mainland phrase.

column3: A verb-object that splits around the count: 鞠一个躬, 鞠了三次躬. The person bowed to follows 向: 向老师鞠躬. It shows respect, thanks or apology, and a performer's bow at the end of a show. In Taiwan the first syllable is read jú.
column4: 演出结束后，他向观众鞠躬。
column5: 演出結束後，他向觀眾鞠躬。
column6: Yǎnchū jiéshù hòu, tā xiàng guānzhòng jūgōng.
column7: After the show he bowed to the audience.
column9: A verb-object that splits around the count: 鞠一個躬, 鞠了三次躬. The person bowed to follows 向: 向老師鞠躬. It shows respect, thanks or apology, and a performer's bow at the end of a show. In Taiwan the first syllable is read jú.

column3: For people or things coming together in one place: 人群聚集, 聚集在广场上; and, with an object, for amassing: 聚集力量, 聚集资金. A social get-together is 聚会, and 集合 is to assemble on command.
column6: Hěn duō rén jùjí zài guǎngchǎng shàng.
column7: Many people gathered in the square.
column9: For people or things coming together in one place: 人群聚集, 聚集在廣場上; and, with an object, for amassing: 聚集力量, 聚集資金. A social get-together is 聚會, and 集合 is to assemble on command.

column3: A verb-object, so it can split: 举个例子, 举几个例子. The set phrase 举例来说 opens an illustration, and 举例说明 means to explain by giving examples, in statements as well as requests.
column6: Qǐng nǐ jǔlì shuōmíng.
column7: Please explain with an example.
column9: A verb-object, so it can split: 舉個例子, 舉幾個例子. The set phrase 舉例來說 opens an illustration, and 舉例說明 means to explain by giving examples, in statements as well as requests.

column3: Describes strong physical action, pain or change: 剧烈运动, 剧烈的疼痛, 剧烈变化. It is common in health and medical talk. For strong feelings or opinions the word is 强烈: 强烈反对.
column6: Fàn hòu bùyào zuò jùliè yùndòng.
column7: Don't exercise hard after a meal.
column9: Describes strong physical action, pain or change: 劇烈運動, 劇烈的疼痛, 劇烈變化. It is common in health and medical talk. For strong feelings or opinions the word is 強烈: 強烈反對.

column3: Mostly a part of compounds: 军人, 军队, 空军, 海军, 从军. In contests it ranks a team: 冠军 (champion) and 亚军 (runner-up).
column6: Tā de yéye shì jūn rén.
column7: His grandfather was a soldier.
column9: Mostly a part of compounds: 軍人, 軍隊, 空軍, 海軍, 從軍. In contests it ranks a team: 冠軍 (champion) and 亞軍 (runner-up).

column3: Names the field (对军事感兴趣) or sits before a noun to mean military: 军事演习, 军事基地, 军事力量. For the people it is 军人, and for the force 军队.
column4: 这个国家的军事力量很强。
column5: 這個國家的軍事力量很強。
column6: Zhège guójiā de jūnshì lìliàng hěn qiáng.
column7: This country's military strength is very great.
column9: Names the field (對軍事感興趣) or sits before a noun to mean military: 軍事演習, 軍事基地, 軍事力量. For the people it is 軍人, and for the force 軍隊.

column3: The building for stage plays, opera and dance; films are shown in a 电影院. The same 剧 is in 戏剧, 歌剧 and 电视剧 (TV series).
column4: 我们明天晚上去剧院看表演。
column5: 我們明天晚上去劇院看表演。
column6: Wǒmen míngtiān wǎnshang qù jùyuàn kàn biǎoyǎn.
column7: We are going to a show at the theater tomorrow evening.
column9: The building for stage plays, opera and dance; films are shown in a 電影院. The same 劇 is in 戲劇, 歌劇 and 電視劇 (TV series).

column3: A formal dismissal done by an institution: 被开除, 开除学籍 for a student, 开除员工 for an employee. It is a punishment, often for misconduct, not a layoff (裁员). Spoken, being fired is 炒鱿鱼.
column4: 他迟到太多次，被公司开除了。
column5: 他遲到太多次，被公司開除了。
column6: Tā chídào tài duō cì, bèi gōngsī kāichú le.
column7: He was late too many times and got fired.
column9: A formal dismissal done by an institution: 被開除, 開除學籍 for a student, 開除員工 for an employee. It is a punishment, often for misconduct, not a layoff (裁員). Spoken, being fired is 炒魷魚.

column3: The spoken word for having surgery: 去医院开刀. The formal word is 手术, and the usual verb for it is 做手术. Figuratively 拿他开刀 means to single him out as an example or target.
column6: Tā míngtiān yào qù yīyuàn kāidāo.
column7: He will have an operation at the hospital tomorrow.
column9: The spoken word for having surgery: 去醫院開刀. The formal word is 手術, and the usual verb for it is 做手術. Figuratively 拿他開刀 means to single him out as an example or target.

column3: Starting up a machine, engine or vehicle: 开动机器; and figuratively 开动脑筋, putting your mind to work. In Taiwan 开动了 is also said before a meal, as a way of saying “let’s eat.”
column6: Gōngrén kāidòng le jīqì.
column7: The worker started the machine.
column9: Starting up a machine, engine or vehicle: 開動機器; and figuratively 開動腦筋, putting your mind to work. In Taiwan 開動了 is also said before a meal, as a way of saying “let’s eat.”

column3: A verb-object, so it splits: 开个户, 开了户. It needs the institution: 在银行开户. 账户 and 户头 mean the account itself, and 用户 is a user.
column6: Wǒ xiǎng zài zhè jiā yínháng kāihù.
column7: I would like to open an account at this bank.
column9: A verb-object, so it splits: 開個戶, 開了戶. It needs the institution: 在銀行開戶. 帳戶 and 戶頭 mean the account itself, and 用戶 is a user.

column3: Said of a school or of one course starting, or of a teacher or department offering a course: 开了一门新课. It is a verb-object: 开不开课. 开学 is the term starting; 开课 is the classes.
column6: Zhè mén kè xià xīngqī kāikè.
column7: This course starts next week.
column9: Said of a school or of one course starting, or of a teacher or department offering a course: 開了一門新課. It is a verb-object: 開不開課. 開學 is the term starting; 開課 is the classes.

column3: Praise for people who are tolerant and reasonable, most often parents, teachers or leaders: 开明的父母, 思想开明. 开放 for a person means open or liberal, at times too much so.
column6: Tā de fùmǔ hěn kāimíng.
column7: His parents are very open-minded.
column9: Praise for people who are tolerant and reasonable, most often parents, teachers or leaders: 開明的父母, 思想開明. 開放 for a person means open or liberal, at times too much so.

column3: A formal word for setting up something that goes on running: 开设分行, 开设课程, 开设账户. In everyday speech you just say 开: 开一家店.
column4: 这家银行在全国开设了很多分行。
column5: 這家銀行在全國開設了很多分行。
column6: Zhè jiā yínháng zài quánguó kāishè le hěn duō fēnháng.
column7: This bank has opened many branches across the country.
column9: A formal word for setting up something that goes on running: 開設分行, 開設課程, 開設帳戶. In everyday speech you just say 開: 開一家店.

column3: Mostly figurative now: 开拓市场, 开拓视野, 开拓新领域. A person who does it is a 开拓者 (pioneer). 开发 develops resources or software, not horizons.
column6: Gōngsī xiǎng kāituò xīn de shìchǎng.
column7: The company wants to open up new markets.
column9: Mostly figurative now: 開拓市場, 開拓視野, 開拓新領域. A person who does it is a 開拓者 (pioneer). 開發 develops resources or software, not horizons.

column3: Found on tickets, posters and announcements: 准时开演, 开演前十分钟. It is only for shows such as plays, concerts and films, while 开始 is the general word for starting.
column6: Diànyǐng shí fēnzhōng hòu kāiyǎn.
column7: The film starts in ten minutes.
column9: Found on tickets, posters and announcements: 準時開演, 開演前十分鐘. It is only for shows such as plays, concerts and films, while 開始 is the general word for starting.

column3: A heavy chop with an axe, cleaver or machete: 砍树, 砍柴, 砍头. For cutting food in the kitchen it is 切. 砍价 is to bargain a price down.
column6: Tā yòng fǔtou kǎn le yī kē shù.
column7: He cut down a tree with an axe.
column9: A heavy chop with an axe, cleaver or machete: 砍樹, 砍柴, 砍頭. For cutting food in the kitchen it is 切. 砍價 is to bargain a price down.

column3: Takes a person: 看得起他. It is mostly met in its negative, 看不起 (look down on), and in the polite 谢谢你看得起我, thanking someone for their trust. Not the 得起 of 买得起 or 吃得起 (can afford): 看得起 and 看不起 are fixed words for thinking highly of or looking down on someone.
column6: Xièxie nǐ kàndeqǐ wǒ.
column7: Thank you for thinking highly of me.
column9: Takes a person: 看得起他. It is mostly met in its negative, 看不起 (look down on), and in the polite 謝謝你看得起我, thanking someone for their trust. Not the 得起 of 買得起 or 吃得起 (can afford): 看得起 and 看不起 are fixed words for thinking highly of or looking down on someone.

column3: Both verb and noun: 向政府抗议, 提出抗议, 抗议活动. It is open objection, in words or in action, and is often by a group: residents, workers, even a government.
column4: 居民抗议在这里盖工厂。
column5: 居民抗議在這裡蓋工廠。
column6: Jūmín kàngyì zài zhèlǐ gài gōngchǎng.
column7: Residents protest against building a factory here.
column9: Both verb and noun: 向政府抗議, 提出抗議, 抗議活動. It is open objection, in words or in action, and is often by a group: residents, workers, even a government.

column3: Also describes your best skill or specialty: 看家本领 (signature skill), 看家菜 (a cook's or restaurant's best dish). 看 is read kān here, with the sense of looking after or guarding.
column4: 我出去买菜，你在家看家。
column5: 我出去買菜，你在家看家。
column6: Wǒ chūqù mǎi cài, nǐ zài jiā kānjiā.
column7: I'm going shopping; you stay home and mind the house.
column9: Also describes your best skill or specialty: 看家本領 (signature skill), 看家菜 (a cook's or restaurant's best dish). 看 is read kān here, with the sense of looking after or guarding.

column3: Doubling a verb softens it into a short try: 让我看看, 看看有没有. The same works for 试试, 想想, 听听. Also spoken: 看看就到春节了, the date arrives before you know it.
column6: Ràng wǒ kànkan nǐ de shǒujī.
column7: Let me take a look at your phone.
column9: Doubling a verb softens it into a short try: 讓我看看, 看看有沒有. The same works for 試試, 想想, 聽聽. Also spoken: 看看就到春節了, the date arrives before you know it.

column3: A spoken opener for a guess drawn from what you can see: 看样子他不会来了. The result follows as a clause. 看起来 is more often followed by an adjective: 看起来很好吃.
column6: Kànyàngzi yào xià yǔ le.
column7: It looks like it's going to rain.
column9: A spoken opener for a guess drawn from what you can see: 看樣子他不會來了. The result follows as a clause. 看起來 is more often followed by an adjective: 看起來很好吃.

column3: The sheet itself: 发考卷, 收考卷, 改考卷. The other word is 试卷, which is the more usual one on the mainland, while 考卷 is common in Taiwan.
column6: Lǎoshī zhèngzài fā kǎojuàn.
column7: The teacher is handing out the exam papers.
column9: The sheet itself: 發考卷, 收考卷, 改考卷. The other word is 試卷, which is the more usual one on the mainland, while 考卷 is common in Taiwan.

column3: Passing something selective and getting in or certified: 考取大学, 考取驾照. 考上 is the everyday spoken word for it, and 考取 sounds a little more formal.
column6: Tā kǎoqǔ le Táiwān dàxué.
column7: She was admitted to National Taiwan University.
column9: Passing something selective and getting in or certified: 考取大學, 考取駕照. 考上 is the everyday spoken word for it, and 考取 sounds a little more formal.

column3: In Taiwan 卡通 is the everyday word for a cartoon on TV; on the mainland 动画片 is more usual, and 卡通 mostly means the cartoon style, as in 卡通人物.
column6: Háizimen xǐhuan kàn kǎtōng.
column7: Children like watching cartoons.
column9: In Taiwan 卡通 is the everyday word for a cartoon on TV; on the mainland 動畫片 is more usual, and 卡通 mostly means the cartoon style, as in 卡通人物.

column3: A hotel room for guests, or the spare room for visitors at home. The sign 客房服务 is room service. It is counted with 间: 一间客房. 房间 is any room.
column4: 这家旅馆有两百间客房。
column5: 這家旅館有兩百間客房。
column6: Zhè jiā lǚguǎn yǒu liǎngbǎi jiān kèfáng.
column7: This hotel has two hundred guest rooms.
column9: A hotel room for guests, or the spare room for visitors at home. The sign 客房服務 is room service. It is counted with 間: 一間客房. 房間 is any room.

column3: A school subject or an exam subject: 考试科目, 必修科目 (required), 选修科目 (elective). In accounting it is a ledger category: 会计科目.
column6: Nǐ zuì xǐhuan nǎge kēmù?
column7: Which subject do you like best?
column9: A school subject or an exam subject: 考試科目, 必修科目 (required), 選修科目 (elective). In accounting it is a ledger category: 會計科目.

column3: Goes before a noun to mean outside the lessons: 课外活动, 课外读物 (extra reading), 课外辅导. The opposite is 课内.
column4: 他参加了很多课外活动。
column5: 他參加了很多課外活動。
column6: Tā cānjiā le hěn duō kèwài huódòng.
column7: He joined many extracurricular activities.
column9: Goes before a noun to mean outside the lessons: 課外活動, 課外讀物 (extra reading), 課外輔導. The opposite is 課內.

column3: Written style, for a result or news worth being glad about: 可喜的成绩, 可喜的进步, and the congratulation 可喜可贺. It is not for how you feel yourself, which is 高兴.
column4: 他的成绩有了可喜的进步。
column5: 他的成績有了可喜的進步。
column6: Tā de chéngjì yǒu le kěxǐ de jìnbù.
column7: His grades show gratifying progress.
column9: Written style, for a result or news worth being glad about: 可喜的成績, 可喜的進步, and the congratulation 可喜可賀. It is not for how you feel yourself, which is 高興.

column3: More often absurd than amusing: 真可笑, 可笑的想法. For something funny, like a joke, use 好笑. 可 plus a verb means worth doing, as in 可爱 and 可怕.
column6: Tā de xiǎngfǎ zhēn kěxiào.
column7: His idea is really ridiculous.
column9: More often absurd than amusing: 真可笑, 可笑的想法. For something funny, like a joke, use 好笑. 可 plus a verb means worth doing, as in 可愛 and 可怕.

column3: Both the feeling of dread and terrorism: 恐怖电影 (horror film), 恐怖分子 (terrorist). A terrorist attack is 恐怖袭击 on the mainland and 恐怖攻击 in Taiwan. In speech 好恐怖 is just creepy.
column6: Wǒ bù gǎn kàn kǒngbù diànyǐng.
column7: I don't dare watch horror films.
column9: Both the feeling of dread and terrorism: 恐怖電影 (horror film), 恐怖分子 (terrorist). A terrorist attack is 恐怖襲擊 on the mainland and 恐怖攻擊 in Taiwan. In speech 好恐怖 is just creepy.

column3: Written style, for scale and achievement: 空前成功, 盛况空前, 空前的规模; also for bad things: 空前的灾难. The pair 空前绝后 adds that nothing will follow either.
column6: Zhè chǎng yǎnchànghuì shèngkuàng kōngqián.
column7: The concert was a record-breaking success.
column9: Written style, for scale and achievement: 空前成功, 盛況空前, 空前的規模; also for bad things: 空前的災難. The pair 空前絕後 adds that nothing will follow either.

column3: Three everyday uses: fasten (扣好安全带, 扣子 button), deduct (扣钱, 扣分, 扣除), and spike in sports (扣球). 打折扣 means to give a discount, or figuratively to fall short.
column6: Chídào yào kòu fēn.
column7: You lose points for being late.
column9: Three everyday uses: fasten (扣好安全帶, 釦子 button), deduct (扣錢, 扣分, 扣除), and spike in sports (扣球). 打折扣 means to give a discount, or figuratively to fall short.

column3: A skill that is praised: 口才好, 很有口才, 训练口才. It means speaking clearly and persuasively, and works as a noun after 有 or 好.
column6: Tā kǒucái hěn hǎo.
column7: He is very eloquent.
column9: A skill that is praised: 口才好, 很有口才, 訓練口才. It means speaking clearly and persuasively, and works as a noun after 有 or 好.

column3: Counted with 支: 一支口红. You put it on with 涂 or 擦. Lip gloss is 唇彩 on the mainland and 唇蜜 in Taiwan; lip balm is 润唇膏 and 护唇膏.
column6: Tā mǎi le yī zhī xīn kǒuhóng.
column7: She bought a new lipstick.
column9: Counted with 支: 一支口紅. You put it on with 塗 or 擦. Lip gloss is 唇彩 on the mainland and 唇蜜 in Taiwan; lip balm is 潤唇膏 and 護唇膏.

column3: It names the attitude you hear in how something is said, good or bad: 口气很差, 用命令的口气. 好大的口气 is a big boast.
column6: Tā de kǒuqì hěn bù kèqi.
column7: His tone is very rude.
column9: It names the attitude you hear in how something is said, good or bad: 口氣很差, 用命令的口氣. 好大的口氣 is a big boast.

column3: Used for school, language and thesis exams, and set against 笔试, the written exam. For a job interview the word is 面试, not 口试.
column6: Míngtiān yǒu yī ge Yīngwén kǒushì.
column7: Tomorrow there is an English oral exam.
column9: Used for school, language and thesis exams, and set against 筆試, the written exam. For a job interview the word is 面試, not 口試.

column3: It goes with 流 (drool), 吞 (swallow) and 吐 (spit). 流口水 also says that you badly want something, and 口水战 is a war of words.
column6: Kàndào dàngāo, tā jiù liú kǒushuǐ.
column7: At the sight of the cake he started to drool.
column9: It goes with 流 (drool), 吞 (swallow) and 吐 (spit). 流口水 also says that you badly want something, and 口水戰 is a war of words.

column3: Your region or first language shows in how you speak: 有口音, 北京口音, 外国口音. 听得出口音 means you can hear where someone is from.
column6: Tā shuō Zhōngwén yǒu yīdiǎn kǒuyin.
column7: He speaks Chinese with a slight accent.
column9: Your region or first language shows in how you speak: 有口音, 北京口音, 外國口音. 聽得出口音 means you can hear where someone is from.

column3: Beyond stepping over things, it works like "across" before a noun: 跨国公司 (multinational), 跨年 (see in the new year), 跨领域 (across fields). One scholar derives the word for pants, 裤, from 跨.
column6: Tā yī bù kuà guò le shuǐgōu.
column7: He stepped over the ditch in one stride.
column9: Beyond stepping over things, it works like "across" before a noun: 跨國公司 (multinational), 跨年 (see in the new year), 跨領域 (across fields). One scholar derives the word for pants, 褲, from 跨.

column3: The object tells you which sense: 夸自己 is bragging, 夸别人 is praising. 夸口 and 夸张 are the negative words, 夸奖 the positive one.
column6: Lǎoshī kuā tā hěn cōngming.
column7: The teacher praised him for being clever.
column9: The object tells you which sense: 誇自己 is bragging, 誇別人 is praising. 誇口 and 誇張 are the negative words, 誇獎 the positive one.

column3: Real praise, usually from a parent, teacher or boss to someone younger: 受到夸奖, 夸奖孩子. The modest reply is 过奖了, "you flatter me".
column6: Lǎoshī kuājiǎng le tā de zuòyè.
column7: The teacher praised his homework.
column9: Real praise, usually from a parent, teacher or boss to someone younger: 受到誇獎, 誇獎孩子. The modest reply is 過獎了, "you flatter me".

column3: It is the cut or shape of clothes, shoes or furniture, not the color: 款式新, 款式很多. 款 alone counts models, as in 这款手机.
column4: 这家店的鞋子款式很多。
column5: 這家店的鞋子款式很多。
column6: Zhè jiā diàn de xiézi kuǎnshì hěn duō.
column7: This shop has many styles of shoes.
column9: It is the cut or shape of clothes, shoes or furniture, not the color: 款式新, 款式很多. 款 alone counts models, as in 這款手機.

column3: Use 按 for a car horn and 吹 for playing the instrument. It also names the speaker of a phone or stereo, and 喇叭裤 are bell-bottoms.
column6: Hòumiàn de chē yīzhí àn lǎba.
column7: The car behind keeps honking.
column9: Use 按 for a car horn and 吹 for playing the instrument. It also names the speaker of a phone or stereo, and 喇叭褲 are bell-bottoms.

column3: Before a verb it means doing it back and forth (来回走, 来回跑). After a trip word or with a time it means round trip: 来回票, 来回两小时.
column6: Tā zài fángjiān lǐ láihuí zǒu.
column7: He paces back and forth in the room.
column9: Before a verb it means doing it back and forth (來回走, 來回跑). After a trip word or with a time it means round trip: 來回票, 來回兩小時.

column3: A formal, written word whose subject is a season, event or time of day: 春天来临, 节日来临, 危机来临. A person arriving is 到 or 来到, never 来临.
column4: 夜晚来临，大家都回家了。
column5: 夜晚來臨，大家都回家了。
column6: Yèwǎn láilín, dàjiā dōu huí jiā le.
column7: Night came and everyone went home.
column9: A formal, written word whose subject is a season, event or time of day: 春天來臨, 節日來臨, 危機來臨. A person arriving is 到 or 來到, never 來臨.

column3: Before a noun it describes traffic: 来往的行人, 来往的车辆. Between people it is keeping in touch, usually with 少 or 密切: 我们很少来往. The reversed 往来 is more formal and common in business: 商业往来.
column6: Jiē shàng láiwǎng de rén hěn duō.
column7: There are many people coming and going on the street.
column9: Before a noun it describes traffic: 來往的行人, 來往的車輛. Between people it is keeping in touch, usually with 少 or 密切: 我們很少來往. The reversed 往來 is more formal and common in business: 商業往來.

column3: The whole pepper, fresh or dried, and the base of 辣椒酱 and 辣椒油 (chili oil). 椒 also turns up in other peppers, such as 胡椒 and 青椒.
column6: Tā bù gǎn chī làjiāo.
column7: He doesn't dare eat chili.
column9: The whole pepper, fresh or dried, and the base of 辣椒醬 and 辣椒油 (chili oil). 椒 also turns up in other peppers, such as 胡椒 and 青椒.

column3: Blunt when said of a person: 他很懒. People also say it of themselves, half joking: 我太懒了. 偷懒 is slacking off, 懒人 a lazy person.
column6: Tā tài lǎn le, bù ài zuò jiāwù.
column7: He is too lazy and doesn't like doing chores.
column9: Blunt when said of a person: 他很懶. People also say it of themselves, half joking: 我太懶了. 偷懶 is slacking off, 懶人 a lazy person.

column3: Followed by a verb and nearly always about yourself: 我懒得去. It says the effort isn't worth it, not that you are a lazy person. 懒得理你 is a common brush-off.
column6: Wàimiàn tài lěng, wǒ lǎnde chūmén.
column7: It's too cold outside; I can't be bothered to go out.
column9: Followed by a verb and nearly always about yourself: 我懶得去. It says the effort isn't worth it, not that you are a lazy person. 懶得理你 is a common brush-off.

column3: As in English, 狼 stands for a greedy or predatory man: 色狼 is a lecher. 狼群 is a pack, and 大野狼 the big bad wolf of fairy tales.
column6: Sēnlín lǐ yǒu yī zhī láng.
column7: There is a wolf in the forest.
column9: As in English, 狼 stands for a greedy or predatory man: 色狼 is a lecher. 狼群 is a pack, and 大野狼 the big bad wolf of fairy tales.

column3: It also leads words about being unrestrained: 浪费 (waste), 流浪 (wander), 浪漫 (romantic). 海浪 and 浪花 stay with the actual sea. It may be a colloquial variant of 澜, another word for wave.
column6: Hǎibiān de làng hěn dà.
column7: The waves at the seaside are big.
column9: It also leads words about being unrestrained: 浪費 (waste), 流浪 (wander), 浪漫 (romantic). 海浪 and 浪花 stay with the actual sea. It may be a colloquial variant of 瀾, another word for wave.

column3: The usual objects are power, drugs and resources: 滥用权力, 滥用药物, 滥用职权. It names a serious wrong, unlike 误用, which is a simple mistake in using something.
column6: Bù néng lànyòng quánlì.
column7: Power must not be abused.
column9: The usual objects are power, drugs and resources: 濫用權力, 濫用藥物, 濫用職權. It names a serious wrong, unlike 誤用, which is a simple mistake in using something.

column3: Alone it appears mostly in 坐牢, "serve time". For the building, 监狱 is the neutral word, and 牢房 is a cell. In 牢固 and 牢记 it means firm: 牢记在心.
column4: 他因为犯法坐了三年牢。
column5: 他因為犯法坐了三年牢。
column6: Tā yīnwèi fànfǎ zuò le sān nián láo.
column7: He spent three years in prison for breaking the law.
column9: Alone it appears mostly in 坐牢, "serve time". For the building, 監獄 is the neutral word, and 牢房 is a cell. In 牢固 and 牢記 it means firm: 牢記在心.

column3: Lifting something out of liquid with a net, spoon or hand: 捞鱼, 捞面, 打捞 (salvage). Informally 捞钱 is raking in money, often not honestly.
column4: 他用网子把鱼捞了起来。
column5: 他用網子把魚撈了起來。
column6: Tā yòng wǎngzi bǎ yú lāo le qǐlái.
column7: He scooped the fish up with a net.
column9: Lifting something out of liquid with a net, spoon or hand: 撈魚, 撈麵, 打撈 (salvage). Informally 撈錢 is raking in money, often not honestly.

column3: Children are counted by birth order with 老: 老二, 老三 and so on. Outside the family 老大 is whoever calls the shots, an informal word: 这里谁是老大?
column4: 我是家里的老大，有两个弟弟。
column5: 我是家裡的老大，有兩個弟弟。
column6: Wǒ shì jiālǐ de lǎodà, yǒu liǎng ge dìdi.
column7: I am the eldest in my family and have two younger brothers.
column9: Children are counted by birth order with 老: 老二, 老三 and so on. Outside the family 老大 is whoever calls the shots, an informal word: 這裡誰是老大?

column3: Repeating the same advice or worries, typically a parent or spouse: 妈妈老爱唠叨. It can also be a noun, 听她的唠叨, and carries mild annoyance.
column4: 妈妈每天都唠叨我早点睡。
column5: 媽媽每天都嘮叨我早點睡。
column6: Māma měi tiān dōu láodao wǒ zǎo diǎn shuì.
column7: Mom nags me every day to go to bed early.
column9: Repeating the same advice or worries, typically a parent or spouse: 媽媽老愛嘮叨. It can also be a noun, 聽她的嘮叨, and carries mild annoyance.

column3: In Taiwan this is the standard term for wage workers in law and news: 劳工局, 劳工保险, 外籍劳工. On the mainland 工人 or 劳动者 is more usual.
column4: 很多外籍劳工在台湾工作。
column5: 很多外籍勞工在台灣工作。
column6: Hěn duō wàijí láogōng zài Táiwān gōngzuò.
column7: Many migrant workers work in Taiwan.
column9: In Taiwan this is the standard term for wage workers in law and news: 勞工局, 勞工保險, 外籍勞工. On the mainland 工人 or 勞動者 is more usual.

column3: Bodily work, set against 劳心, mental work: 出卖劳力 means to sell your labor. It is a business or economics word more than a daily one.
column6: Tā kào láolì zhuàn qián.
column7: He earns his money by physical labor.
column9: Bodily work, set against 勞心, mental work: 出賣勞力 means to sell your labor. It is a business or economics word more than a daily one.

column3: Almost always in 发牢骚 or 满腹牢骚. It is grumbling to let off steam, not a formal complaint: that is 投诉. The tone is spoken and a little weary.
column6: Tā zhěngtiān fā láosāo.
column7: He grumbles all day.
column9: Almost always in 發牢騷 or 滿腹牢騷. It is grumbling to let off steam, not a formal complaint: that is 投訴. The tone is spoken and a little weary.

column3: It opens a sentence before an opinion the listener may not like, so it can sound blunt. 说实话 means the same and is just as common.
column4: 老实说，我不太喜欢这家店。
column5: 老實說，我不太喜歡這家店。
column6: Lǎoshíshuō, wǒ bù tài xǐhuan zhè jiā diàn.
column7: Honestly, I don't like this shop very much.
column9: It opens a sentence before an opinion the listener may not like, so it can sound blunt. 說實話 means the same and is just as common.

column3: Counted with 根 or 支: 一根蜡烛. You 点 (light) and 吹 (blow out) one, and 生日蜡烛 sit on a birthday cake. 蜡 alone is wax, as in 蜡笔 (crayon).
column4: 他吹熄了生日蛋糕上的蜡烛。
column5: 他吹熄了生日蛋糕上的蠟燭。
column6: Tā chuīxī le shēngrì dàngāo shàng de làzhú.
column7: He blew out the candles on his birthday cake.
column9: Counted with 根 or 支: 一根蠟燭. You 點 (light) and 吹 (blow out) one, and 生日蠟燭 sit on a birthday cake. 蠟 alone is wax, as in 蠟筆 (crayon).

column3: The opposite is 热门 (popular). Typical things are 冷门专业 and 冷门景点. In sports and contests, 爆冷门 is an upset by an unlikely winner.
column6: Zhège zhuānyè bǐjiào lěngmén.
column7: This major is rather unpopular.
column9: The opposite is 熱門 (popular). Typical things are 冷門專業 and 冷門景點. In sports and contests, 爆冷門 is an upset by an unlikely winner.

column3: It is a shop or menu category, set against 热饮: 冷饮店. On the mainland 冷饮 also covers ice cream and popsicles.
column6: Xiàtiān wǒ cháng hē lěngyǐn.
column7: In summer I often drink cold drinks.
column9: It is a shop or menu category, set against 熱飲: 冷飲店. On the mainland 冷飲 also covers ice cream and popsicles.

column3: A warmer word than 愿意 for being willing, followed by a verb: 乐意帮忙, 我很乐意. 不乐意 sounds put out, not just unwilling.
column6: Wǒ hěn lèyì bāng nǐ de máng.
column7: I am glad to help you.
column9: A warmer word than 願意 for being willing, followed by a verb: 樂意幫忙, 我很樂意. 不樂意 sounds put out, not just unwilling.

column3: Alone as a verb it means paying attention to someone and is nearly always negated: 不理我, 别理他. Elsewhere it sits in compounds: 管理, 整理, 道理, 理由. One old account says it meant to polish jade, and "to order, tidy up" may come from that.
column6: Wǒ jiào tā, tā bù lǐ wǒ.
column7: I called him, but he ignored me.
column9: Alone as a verb it means paying attention to someone and is nearly always negated: 不理我, 別理他. Elsewhere it sits in compounds: 管理, 整理, 道理, 理由. One old account says it meant to polish jade, and "to order, tidy up" may come from that.

column3: Mostly in compounds. 有利 and 不利 take 对: 对我们有利. It also means "going well" in 顺利, 胜利 and 便利, and "profit" in 利息 and 利润.
column6: Zhèyàng zuò duì wǒmen yǒu lì.
column7: Doing it this way is good for us.
column9: Mostly in compounds. 有利 and 不利 take 對: 對我們有利. It also means "going well" in 順利, 勝利 and 便利, and "profit" in 利息 and 利潤.

column3: It counts small things that come as separate bits: 一粒米, 一粒糖, 一粒药. In Taiwan speech it also counts bigger round things, such as a watermelon.
column6: Dì shàng diào le jǐ lì mǐ.
column7: A few grains of rice fell on the ground.
column9: It counts small things that come as separate bits: 一粒米, 一粒糖, 一粒藥. In Taiwan speech it also counts bigger round things, such as a watermelon.

column3: Sharing a pear (分梨) sounds like parting (分离), so couples traditionally avoid splitting one. Shops and menus often say plain 梨, as in 水梨.
column6: Zhège lízi yòu tián yòu duō zhī.
column7: This pear is sweet and juicy.
column9: Sharing a pear (分梨) sounds like parting (分離), so couples traditionally avoid splitting one. Shops and menus often say plain 梨, as in 水梨.

column3: It appears only in 伎俩, tricks or schemes, and the sense is always negative: 耍伎俩, 小伎俩.
column4: 他的伎俩被大家看穿了。
column5: 他的伎倆被大家看穿了。
column6: Tā de jì liǎng bèi dàjiā kànchuān le.
column7: Everyone saw through his tricks.
column9: It appears only in 伎倆, tricks or schemes, and the sense is always negative: 耍伎倆, 小伎倆.

column3: A polite, formal word. Notices and apologies use it: 敬请谅解, 请多多谅解. It asks for understanding of circumstances, where 原谅 is forgiveness for a wrong.
column6: Xièxie nǐ de liàngjiě.
column7: Thank you for your understanding.
column9: A polite, formal word. Notices and apologies use it: 敬請諒解, 請多多諒解. It asks for understanding of circumstances, where 原諒 is forgiveness for a wrong.

column3: Said of a cup, wall, ground or dry lips splitting along a line: 裂开, 裂了一条缝. Figuratively 分裂 is splitting apart and 关系破裂 a relationship breaking down.
column6: Bēizi liè le yī tiáo fèng.
column7: The cup has a crack.
column9: Said of a cup, wall, ground or dry lips splitting along a line: 裂開, 裂了一條縫. Figuratively 分裂 is splitting apart and 關係破裂 a relationship breaking down.

column3: Either rain falling on you (淋雨, 淋湿) or you pouring liquid onto food (淋酱汁, 淋油). 淋浴 is taking a shower.
column6: Wǒ méi dài sǎn, lín le yī shēn yǔ.
column7: I had no umbrella and got soaked in the rain.
column9: Either rain falling on you (淋雨, 淋濕) or you pouring liquid onto food (淋醬汁, 淋油). 淋浴 is taking a shower.

column3: Before a verb it sets the moment just before: 临走, 临睡前. In compounds: 面临 (face a challenge), 临时 (temporary), and 光临, the "honored arrival" of 欢迎光临.
column6: Lín zǒu qián, tā bǎ mén guān hǎo le.
column7: Before leaving, he closed the door properly.
column9: Before a verb it sets the moment just before: 臨走, 臨睡前. In compounds: 面臨 (face a challenge), 臨時 (temporary), and 光臨, the "honored arrival" of 歡迎光臨.

column3: It comes with a clock time for the hours between midnight and dawn: 凌晨一点, 凌晨三点. Once it is light, people say 清晨 or 早上.
column6: Tā língchén liǎng diǎn cái shuì.
column7: He didn't go to sleep until 2 a.m.
column9: It comes with a clock time for the hours between midnight and dawn: 凌晨一點, 凌晨三點. Once it is light, people say 清晨 or 早上.

column3: Praise for a mind, fingers, a plan or a rule that adapts: 头脑灵活, 灵活运用, 灵活处理. The opposite for rules and thinking is 死板, rigid.
column6: Tā de tóunǎo hěn línghuó.
column7: He has a quick, flexible mind.
column9: Praise for a mind, fingers, a plan or a rule that adapts: 頭腦靈活, 靈活運用, 靈活處理. The opposite for rules and thinking is 死板, rigid.

column3: A part of a machine, car or appliance that can be replaced or bought separately: 汽车零件, 更换零件. 零 means odd bits here, as in 零钱 (small change) and 零食 (snacks).
column6: Zhè tái jīqì quē yī ge língjiàn.
column7: This machine is missing a part.
column9: A part of a machine, car or appliance that can be replaced or bought separately: 汽車零件, 更換零件. 零 means odd bits here, as in 零錢 (small change) and 零食 (snacks).

column3: A trade term, set against 批发 (wholesale): 零售商, 零售价, 零售业. A shop that sells single items directly to buyers can also say 零售 on its sign.
column4: 这家店只做零售，不做批发。
column5: 這家店只做零售，不做批發。
column6: Zhè jiā diàn zhǐ zuò língshòu, bù zuò pīfā.
column7: This shop only does retail, not wholesale.
column9: A trade term, set against 批發 (wholesale): 零售商, 零售價, 零售業. A shop that sells single items directly to buyers can also say 零售 on its sign.

column3: A political term: 领土完整, 领土争议, 领土主权. Related words share 领 for what a state controls: 领海 (territorial waters) and 领空 (airspace).
column4: 这座岛是这个国家的领土。
column5: 這座島是這個國家的領土。
column6: Zhè zuò dǎo shì zhège guójiā de lǐngtǔ.
column7: This island is the territory of this country.
column9: A political term: 領土完整, 領土爭議, 領土主權. Related words share 領 for what a state controls: 領海 (territorial waters) and 領空 (airspace).

column3: A respected head of a nation, party or movement, more elevated than the everyday 领导: 精神领袖, 国家领袖, 学生领袖. 领 began as the neck or collar, and "to lead" came by way of "to take by the neck".
column6: Tā shì xuésheng lǐngxiù.
column7: He is a student leader.
column9: A respected head of a nation, party or movement, more elevated than the everyday 領導: 精神領袖, 國家領袖, 學生領袖. 領 began as the neck or collar, and "to lead" came by way of "to take by the neck".

column3: A more formal or commercial word than 礼物, the everyday word for a present from a friend: 礼品店, 礼品卡, 赠送礼品. Companies give 礼品.
column6: Zhè shì gōngsī sòng de lǐpǐn.
column7: This is a gift from the company.
column9: A more formal or commercial word than 禮物, the everyday word for a present from a friend: 禮品店, 禮品卡, 贈送禮品. Companies give 禮品.

column3: A quick, smooth, quiet move, often a sneaky one: 溜走, 溜出去, 溜进来. It also covers gliding on ice, as in 溜冰.
column6: Xiǎotōu cóng hòumén liū zǒu le.
column7: The thief slipped away through the back door.
column9: A quick, smooth, quiet move, often a sneaky one: 溜走, 溜出去, 溜進來. It also covers gliding on ice, as in 溜冰.

column3: The spoken word for skating: 溜冰场, 溜冰鞋. 滑冰 is the standard sports term. As slang, 溜冰 can also mean using meth, so context matters.
column6: Dōngtiān wǒmen qù liūbīng.
column7: In winter we go skating.
column9: The spoken word for skating: 溜冰場, 溜冰鞋. 滑冰 is the standard sports term. As slang, 溜冰 can also mean using meth, so context matters.

column3: It comes last in a phrase to give the purpose: 拍照留念, 合影留念, 签名留念. It is typical of photos at scenic spots and farewells.
column6: Wǒmen zài ménkǒu héyǐng liúniàn.
column7: We took a group photo at the entrance as a keepsake.
column9: It comes last in a phrase to give the purpose: 拍照留念, 合影留念, 簽名留念. It is typical of photos at scenic spots and farewells.

column3: Spoken only. It softens an announcement or warning with a playful lilt: 我先走喽, 开饭喽, 小心喽. In writing or formal speech use 了.
column6: Wǒ xiān zǒu lou!
column7: I'm off first!
column9: Spoken only. It softens an announcement or warning with a playful lilt: 我先走嘍, 開飯嘍, 小心嘍. In writing or formal speech use 了.

column3: Usually followed by 着, 住 or 在 and the person held: 搂着, 搂住, 搂在怀里. It is a warm, physical hug; 拥抱 is the more formal word, used for greetings and in writing.
column6: Māma lǒu zhe háizi.
column7: Mom holds the child in her arms.
column9: Usually followed by 著, 住 or 在 and the person held: 摟著, 摟住, 摟在懷裡. It is a warm, physical hug; 擁抱 is the more formal word, used for greetings and in writing.

column3: Dew is 露水, and 露天 and 露营 are about the open air: an open-air market, camping out. Possibly it is a derivative of 落, literally "what has been dropped".
column4: 早上草地上有很多露水。
column5: 早上草地上有很多露水。
column6: Zǎoshang cǎodì shàng yǒu hěn duō lù shuǐ.
column7: In the morning there is a lot of dew on the grass.
column9: Dew is 露水, and 露天 and 露營 are about the open air: an open-air market, camping out. Possibly it is a derivative of 落, literally "what has been dropped".

column3: 灯 is the everyday word for any lamp or light, so it turns up in many compounds: 台灯 for a desk lamp, 红绿灯 for traffic lights, 灯泡 for a bulb. Street lights are said to come on (亮) at dusk.
column6: Tiān hēi le, lùdēng liàng le.
column7: It got dark and the street lights came on.
column9: 燈 is the everyday word for any lamp or light, so it turns up in many compounds: 檯燈 for a desk lamp, 紅綠燈 for traffic lights, 燈泡 for a bulb. Street lights are said to come on (亮) at dusk.

column3: The bean behind 绿豆汤, a sweet soup eaten cold in summer to cool down, and 绿豆糕, a pastry. 绿豆沙 is the sweet paste, and 绿豆芽 are the sprouts.
column6: Xiàtiān hē lǜdòu tāng hěn shūfu.
column7: In summer, mung bean soup is refreshing.
column9: The bean behind 綠豆湯, a sweet soup eaten cold in summer to cool down, and 綠豆糕, a pastry. 綠豆沙 is the sweet paste, and 綠豆芽 are the sprouts.

column3: Before a one-syllable verb it means a little or slightly, in a more written style: 略懂, 略有不同, 略胜一筹. It also means to omit, as in 省略, 忽略, and a plan, as in 策略, 战略.
column6: Wǒ lüè dǒng yīdiǎn Rìyǔ.
column7: I know a little Japanese.
column9: Before a one-syllable verb it means a little or slightly, in a more written style: 略懂, 略有不同, 略勝一籌. It also means to omit, as in 省略, 忽略, and a plan, as in 策略, 戰略.

column3: One of the three branches, with 海军 and 空军. 陆 on its own is land: 陆地 is dry land, 大陆 is a continent or the mainland, and 陆战队 are the marines.
column6: Tā zài lùjūn fúyì.
column7: He serves in the army.
column9: One of the three branches, with 海軍 and 空軍. 陸 on its own is land: 陸地 is dry land, 大陸 is a continent or the mainland, and 陸戰隊 are the marines.

column3: A bound word that mostly sits in compounds: 讨论, 理论, 论文, 无论. Before a unit it means by the, so a price is set per unit: 论斤卖, 论个卖. 无论 ... 都 means no matter how or what.
column6: Zhèxiē shuǐguǒ shì lùn jīn mài de.
column7: These fruits are sold by weight.
column9: A bound word that mostly sits in compounds: 討論, 理論, 論文, 無論. Before a unit it means by the, so a price is set per unit: 論斤賣, 論個賣. 無論 ... 都 means no matter how or what.

column3: It goes before the verb for what each person does in turn: 轮流做饭, 轮流值班, 轮流发言. For something that happens in a fixed cycle, as with seasons or shifts, 轮换 is also used.
column6: Wǒmen lúnliú kāichē.
column7: We take turns driving.
column9: It goes before the verb for what each person does in turn: 輪流做飯, 輪流值班, 輪流發言. For something that happens in a fixed cycle, as with seasons or shifts, 輪換 is also used.

column3: It describes people, ideas or equipment that have not kept up: 观念落伍, 落伍了. A little critical. 过时 only says a thing is out of fashion, while 落伍 can also be said of a person.
column6: Zhè zhǒng shǒujī yǐjīng luòwǔ le.
column7: This type of phone is already outdated.
column9: It describes people, ideas or equipment that have not kept up: 觀念落伍, 落伍了. A little critical. 過時 only says a thing is out of fashion, while 落伍 can also be said of a person.

column3: An employer's decision after interviews: 被录用, 录用通知. Offered a place at a school after an exam, you are 被录取 instead. Used of staff and also of articles or manuscripts that a publisher accepts.
column6: Tā bèi zhè jiā gōngsī lùyòng le.
column7: He was hired by this company.
column9: An employer's decision after interviews: 被錄用, 錄用通知. Offered a place at a school after an exam, you are 被錄取 instead. Used of staff and also of articles or manuscripts that a publisher accepts.

column3: Also the numb or tingling feeling when a limb falls asleep (脚麻了, 手麻了), and the root of a family: 麻烦 trouble, 麻辣 numbing-spicy, 芝麻 sesame, 麻将 mahjong, 麻醉 anesthesia. It is said to be a picture of hemp leaves.
column6: Wǒ zuò tài jiǔ, jiǎo má le.
column7: I sat too long and my foot has gone numb.
column9: Also the numb or tingling feeling when a limb falls asleep (腳麻了, 手麻了), and the root of a family: 麻煩 trouble, 麻辣 numbing-spicy, 芝麻 sesame, 麻將 mahjong, 麻醉 anesthesia. It is said to be a picture of hemp leaves.

column3: Said of someone who skips details, or of work done carelessly: 别马虎, 做事马虎. Doubled, 马马虎虎 is a modest answer to how are you or how is work, meaning so-so.
column6: Tā zuòshì tài mǎhu le.
column7: He is too careless in his work.
column9: Said of someone who skips details, or of work done carelessly: 別馬虎, 做事馬虎. Doubled, 馬馬虎虎 is a modest answer to how are you or how is work, meaning so-so.

column3: Usually has a place: 埋在土里, 埋在院子里. It also means to hide away or devote oneself to something, as in 埋头 and 埋藏.
column4: 小狗把骨头埋在院子里。
column5: 小狗把骨頭埋在院子裡。
column6: Xiǎogǒu bǎ gǔtou mái zài yuànzi lǐ.
column7: The puppy buried the bone in the yard.
column9: Usually has a place: 埋在土里, 埋在院子里. It also means to hide away or devote oneself to something, as in 埋頭 and 埋藏.

column3: Said in a restaurant to ask for the check, as a server hears it, or to say that you are paying: 我来买单. Figuratively, 不买单 means not buying it, not accepting a claim or an excuse.
column6: Jīntiān wǒ qǐngkè, wǒ lái mǎidān.
column7: Today it's my treat; I'll pay.
column9: Said in a restaurant to ask for the check, as a server hears it, or to say that you are paying: 我來買單. Figuratively, 不買單 means not buying it, not accepting a claim or an excuse.

column3: Said of films, plays and concerts, and also restaurants, that draw a full house: 很卖座, 卖座电影. It is about ticket sales and attendance, not about how good the thing is.
column6: Zhè bù diànyǐng fēicháng màizuò.
column7: This film is a big box-office hit.
column9: Said of films, plays and concerts, and also restaurants, that draw a full house: 很賣座, 賣座電影. It is about ticket sales and attendance, not about how good the thing is.

column3: A little more written than 忙, and it describes a whole stretch of time that is filled with work: 忙碌的一天, 忙碌的生活, 整天忙碌. 碌 is hardly used alone, so it is learned only with this word and 碌碌无为.
column6: Tā měi tiān dōu guò de hěn mánglù.
column7: She is busy every day.
column9: A little more written than 忙, and it describes a whole stretch of time that is filled with work: 忙碌的一天, 忙碌的生活, 整天忙碌. 碌 is hardly used alone, so it is learned only with this word and 碌碌無為.

column3: Blind in the sense of acting without thought or information: 盲目跟风, 盲目乐观, 盲目崇拜. It is never said of people who cannot see; for that use 盲人.
column6: Bùyào mángmù gēn fēng.
column7: Don't follow the trend blindly.
column9: Blind in the sense of acting without thought or information: 盲目跟風, 盲目樂觀, 盲目崇拜. It is never said of people who cannot see; for that use 盲人.

column3: The common sparrow of towns and parks: 一只麻雀. The game of mahjong is 麻将, and 麻雀 is what Cantonese calls that game. 雀 is a small bird.
column6: Gōngyuán lǐ yǒu hěn duō máquè.
column7: There are many sparrows in the park.
column9: The common sparrow of towns and parks: 一隻麻雀. The game of mahjong is 麻將, and 麻雀 is what Cantonese calls that game. 雀 is a small bird.

column3: It is said of how a thing made by people looks: a room, a building, a page, a dish. It pairs with 大方 or 实用: 美观大方, 美观实用. For natural scenery people say 美丽 or 漂亮.
column6: Zhège pánzi hěn měiguān.
column7: This plate looks very nice.
column9: It is said of how a thing made by people looks: a room, a building, a page, a dish. It pairs with 大方 or 實用: 美觀大方, 美觀實用. For natural scenery people say 美麗 or 漂亮.

column3: A winter flower that blooms in the cold, so it stands for courage and endurance. In card games it is also the suit of clubs, 梅花 A being the ace.
column6: Yángmíngshān shàng de méihuā kāi le.
column7: The plum blossoms on Yangmingshan are out.
column9: A winter flower that blooms in the cold, so it stands for courage and endurance. In card games it is also the suit of clubs, 梅花 A being the ace.

column3: Used of a person, a place or a way of speaking: 有魅力, 个人魅力, 魅力十足. It is a warm word and almost always positive; the pull is felt, not explained.
column6: Tā hěn yǒu mèilì.
column7: He has a lot of charm.
column9: Used of a person, a place or a way of speaking: 有魅力, 個人魅力, 魅力十足. It is a warm word and almost always positive; the pull is felt, not explained.

column3: A little literary, used for what delights the ear or the heart: 美妙的音乐, 美妙的夜晚, 美妙的声音. It is not said of food or of how a person looks.
column6: Tā de gēshēng hěn měimiào.
column7: Her singing voice is lovely.
column9: A little literary, used for what delights the ear or the heart: 美妙的音樂, 美妙的夜晚, 美妙的聲音. It is not said of food or of how a person looks.

column3: Where women go for facials and skin care, and often nails and body care; for hair alone it is 美发店 or 美发院. A 院 is an institution or a venue (医院, 电影院).
column6: Tā měi ge yuè qù měiróngyuàn.
column7: She goes to the beauty salon every month.
column9: Where women go for facials and skin care, and often nails and body care; for hair alone it is 美髮店 or 美髮院. A 院 is an institution or a venue (醫院, 電影院).

column3: Strength in fire, wind and rain: 火很猛, 猛烈. Before a verb it means suddenly: 猛地站起来, 猛一抬头. In speech it is also slang praise: 你好猛！ means you are amazing.
column6: Tā měng de zhàn le qǐlái.
column7: He suddenly stood up.
column9: Strength in fire, wind and rain: 火很猛, 猛烈. Before a verb it means suddenly: 猛地站起來, 猛一抬頭. In speech it is also slang praise: 你好猛！ means you are amazing.

column3: The person or thing dreamed about follows right after: 梦到老朋友. 梦见 is the same and 梦到 is more spoken; for the dreaming itself, use 做梦. Its oldest form shows a person lying on a bed.
column4: 我昨天梦到了小时候的家。
column5: 我昨天夢到了小時候的家。
column6: Wǒ zuótiān mèngdào le xiǎoshíhou de jiā.
column7: Yesterday I dreamed of the home I had as a child.
column9: The person or thing dreamed about follows right after: 夢到老朋友. 夢見 is the same and 夢到 is more spoken; for the dreaming itself, use 做夢. Its oldest form shows a person lying on a bed.

column3: Hot weather with no breeze and heavy humidity, as before a summer storm: 天气闷热, 闷热的夏天. The same 闷 is in 闷得慌, feeling stuffy.
column6: Jīntiān tiānqì hěn mēnrè.
column7: The weather is sultry today.
column9: Hot weather with no breeze and heavy humidity, as before a summer storm: 天氣悶熱, 悶熱的夏天. The same 悶 is in 悶得慌, feeling stuffy.

column3: Mostly seen in compounds: 棉布, 棉被, 棉花, 纯棉. It also means padded with cotton, as in 棉衣 and 棉鞋, clothing made for winter. It is a variant of 绵 with 木 in place of 糸.
column6: Zhè jiàn chènshān shì chún mián de.
column7: This shirt is pure cotton.
column9: Mostly seen in compounds: 棉布, 棉被, 棉花, 純棉. It also means padded with cotton, as in 棉衣 and 棉鞋, clothing made for winter. It is a variant of 綿 with 木 in place of 糸.

column3: The padded bedcover for cold weather: 盖棉被, 一条棉被. 被子 is the general word for any bedcover, and 棉被 says it is cotton-filled; it goes with the measure word 条 or 床.
column6: Tiānqì lěng le, yào gài miánbèi.
column7: It has turned cold, so we need a quilt.
column9: The padded bedcover for cold weather: 蓋棉被, 一條棉被. 被子 is the general word for any bedcover, and 棉被 says it is cotton-filled; it goes with the measure word 條 or 床.

column3: It begins the second clause and names a bad result that the first clause is meant to prevent: 早点走，免得迟到. The result is always unwanted, so it is never used for a good outcome.
column6: Dài bǎ sǎn ba, miǎnde línshī.
column7: Take an umbrella so you don't get wet.
column9: It begins the second clause and names a bad result that the first clause is meant to prevent: 早點走，免得遲到. The result is always unwanted, so it is never used for a good outcome.
