column3: Wheat flour for noodles, dumplings and bread: 一袋面粉. Rice flour is 米粉, which also names rice noodles, and 粉 means powder in general: 奶粉, 辣椒粉. 粉 is believed to have first meant face powder.
column6: Zuò miànbāo yào yòng miànfěn.
column7: You need flour to make bread.
column9: Wheat flour for noodles, dumplings and bread: 一袋面粉. Rice flour is 米粉, which also names rice noodles, and 粉 means powder in general: 奶粉, 辣椒粉. 粉 is believed to have first meant face powder.

column3: The fiber itself, or a wad of it: 一团棉花, 棉花糖 (cotton candy), 棉花棒 (cotton swab). The plant in the field is also 棉花.
column6: Yīshēng yòng miánhua cā shāngkǒu.
column7: The doctor wipes the wound with cotton.
column9: The fiber itself, or a wad of it: 一團棉花, 棉花糖 (cotton candy), 棉花棒 (cotton swab). The plant in the field is also 棉花.

column3: Three ways: barely good enough (勉强可以), doing something unwillingly (勉强笑了笑), and as a verb, to force someone (不要勉强他). In all three, the effort shows and the result is not ideal.
column6: Zhège bànfǎ miǎnqiǎng kěyǐ.
column7: This method will just about do.
column9: Three ways: barely good enough (勉強可以), doing something unwillingly (勉強笑了笑), and as a verb, to force someone (不要勉強他). In all three, the effort shows and the result is not ideal.

column3: A fairly formal word for a talk held in person rather than by phone or letter: 约时间面谈, 当面谈谈. For a job interview, 面试 is the usual word; 面谈 suits a talk with a teacher or a counselor.
column6: Lǎoshī xiǎng hé jiāzhǎng miàntán.
column7: The teacher wants to talk to the parents face to face.
column9: A fairly formal word for a talk held in person rather than by phone or letter: 約時間面談, 當面談談. For a job interview, 面試 is the usual word; 面談 suits a talk with a teacher or a counselor.

column3: As a single character it works as an exclamation (妙！) or a short judgment (这个主意很妙). It carries some surprise: neat and unexpected. Elsewhere it sits in 美妙, 巧妙, 奇妙.
column6: Zhège zhǔyi zhēn miào!
column7: What a clever idea!
column9: As a single character it works as an exclamation (妙！) or a short judgment (這個主意很妙). It carries some surprise: neat and unexpected. Elsewhere it sits in 美妙, 巧妙, 奇妙.

column3: Used for states, peoples and species, not for a single person or a fire: 国家灭亡, 恐龙灭亡. It takes an object when someone destroys something: 灭亡一个国家. The scale is large and final.
column6: Kǒnglóng wèishénme huì mièwáng?
column7: Why did the dinosaurs die out?
column9: Used for states, peoples and species, not for a single person or a fire: 國家滅亡, 恐龍滅亡. It takes an object when someone destroys something: 滅亡一個國家. The scale is large and final.

column3: The insect that makes honey: 一只蜜蜂, 蜜蜂采蜜. Reversed, 蜂蜜 is the honey itself. 蜂 on its own is any bee or wasp, as in 黄蜂 and 蜂巢.
column6: Mìfēng zài huā shàng cǎi mì.
column7: The bee collects honey from the flowers.
column9: The insect that makes honey: 一隻蜜蜂, 蜜蜂採蜜. Reversed, 蜂蜜 is the honey itself. 蜂 on its own is any bee or wasp, as in 黃蜂 and 蜂巢.

column3: Mostly part of a compound: 蜜蜂, 蜂蜜, 蜂巢, 黄蜂 for a wasp. As a verb part, 蜂拥 means to swarm like bees, as of crowds pouring in.
column6: Fēng cháo lǐ yǒu hěn duō mìfēng.
column7: There are many bees in the hive.
column9: Mostly part of a compound: 蜜蜂, 蜂蜜, 蜂巢, 黃蜂 for a wasp. As a verb part, 蜂擁 means to swarm like bees, as of crowds pouring in.

column3: Two uses: a half-awake or dazed state (我还迷糊着), and a forgetful, scatterbrained character (她很迷糊). The second sounds more affectionate than rude.
column6: Wǒ gāng shuìxǐng, nǎozi hái míhu.
column7: I just woke up and my head is still foggy.
column9: Two uses: a half-awake or dazed state (我還迷糊著), and a forgetful, scatterbrained character (她很迷糊). The second sounds more affectionate than rude.

column3: Designer or famous-brand goods: 名牌包, 穿名牌. It suggests status and a high price. A name tag or desk nameplate is also 名牌, but the brand sense is the one you will hear most.
column6: Tā xǐhuān mǎi míngpái bāo.
column7: She likes to buy designer bags.
column9: Designer or famous-brand goods: 名牌包, 穿名牌. It suggests status and a high price. A name tag or desk nameplate is also 名牌, but the brand sense is the one you will hear most.

column3: It can be a traditional folk song, such as 恒春民谣, or a modern acoustic song with guitar. 民歌 is close to it, and leans more toward traditional songs of a region or a people.
column4: 他会弹吉他，也会唱民谣。
column5: 他會彈吉他，也會唱民謠。
column6: Tā huì tán jítā, yě huì chàng mínyáo.
column7: He can play the guitar and also sing folk songs.
column9: It can be a traditional folk song, such as 恆春民謠, or a modern acoustic song with guitar. 民歌 is close to it, and leans more toward traditional songs of a region or a people.

column3: The public in news and speeches: 一般民众, 保护民众, 民众的意见. It sets ordinary people against the government or the police. It is a collective; one person is 一位市民, and 老百姓 is the everyday counterpart.
column6: Zhèngfǔ yào bǎohù mínzhòng.
column7: The government must protect the public.
column9: The public in news and speeches: 一般民眾, 保護民眾, 民眾的意見. It sets ordinary people against the government or the police. It is a collective; one person is 一位市民, and 老百姓 is the everyday counterpart.

column3: Both a noun and an adjective: 民主国家, 民主制度, 民主选举. As an adjective it also describes a leader or manner that listens: 他的作风很民主. The opposite in that use is 专制.
column4: 台湾是一个民主的地方。
column5: 臺灣是一個民主的地方。
column6: Táiwān shì yī ge mínzhǔ de dìfang.
column7: Taiwan is a democratic place.
column9: Both a noun and an adjective: 民主國家, 民主制度, 民主選舉. As an adjective it also describes a leader or manner that listens: 他的作風很民主. The opposite in that use is 專制.

column3: To lose one's bearings, on a road or in life: 迷失方向, 迷失自我. It is a little literary; for simply getting lost in a place, the spoken word is 迷路.
column4: 我们在山里迷失了方向。
column5: 我們在山裡迷失了方向。
column6: Wǒmen zài shān lǐ míshī le fāngxiàng.
column7: We lost our way in the mountains.
column9: To lose one's bearings, on a road or in life: 迷失方向, 迷失自我. It is a little literary; for simply getting lost in a place, the spoken word is 迷路.

column3: You spread something over a surface with a hand, cloth or brush: 抹药, 抹桌子, 抹防晒乳. It also counts wisps of light, cloud or a smile: 一抹微笑, 一抹红霞.
column6: Chūmén qián yào mǒ fángshàirǔ.
column7: Put on sunscreen before you go out.
column9: You spread something over a surface with a hand, cloth or brush: 抹藥, 抹桌子, 抹防曬乳. It also counts wisps of light, cloud or a smile: 一抹微笑, 一抹紅霞.

column3: Besides grinding and sharpening (磨刀, 磨咖啡豆), it means to wear down over time, and to dawdle or pester: 磨蹭, 磨时间. 磨牙 is to grind one's teeth.
column6: Tā měitiān mó kāfēi dòu.
column7: He grinds coffee beans every day.
column9: Besides grinding and sharpening (磨刀, 磨咖啡豆), it means to wear down over time, and to dawdle or pester: 磨蹭, 磨時間. 磨牙 is to grind one's teeth.

column3: 地 here means a place, as in 出生地 (birthplace), 发源地 (place of origin) and 殖民地 (colony).
column6: Wǒmen kuài dào mùdìdì le.
column7: We are almost at our destination.
column9: 地 here means a place, as in 出生地 (birthplace), 發源地 (place of origin) and 殖民地 (colony).

column3: The contents page of a book, also a list of items. On a computer, a folder is 目录 only in technical talk; everyday words differ by place: 资料夹 in Taiwan, 文件夹 on the mainland.
column6: Qǐng xiān kàn mùlù, zài zhǎo yèshù.
column7: Look at the table of contents first, then find the page.
column9: The contents page of a book, also a list of items. On a computer, a folder is 目錄 only in technical talk; everyday words differ by place: 資料夾 in Taiwan, 文件夾 on the mainland.

column3: Powdered milk for babies and for adults who make milk drinks: 冲奶粉 is the verb for mixing it with water. 婴儿奶粉 is infant formula, and 奶粉罐 is the tin it comes in.
column6: Bǎobao hē nǎifěn.
column7: The baby drinks formula.
column9: Powdered milk for babies and for adults who make milk drinks: 沖奶粉 is the verb for mixing it with water. 嬰兒奶粉 is infant formula, and 奶粉罐 is the tin it comes in.

column3: Said of things, not people: 这双鞋很耐用. It often comes with 便宜 or 结实, and for consumer goods it is a good word. 耐 shows up in 耐心, 耐烦 and 耐寒 too, always about the ability to hold up.
column6: Zhège guō yòu piányí yòu nàiyòng.
column7: This pot is both cheap and durable.
column9: Said of things, not people: 這雙鞋很耐用. It often comes with 便宜 or 結實, and for consumer goods it is a good word. 耐 shows up in 耐心, 耐煩 and 耐寒 too, always about the ability to hold up.

column3: Spoken word for how one thinks or solves things: 动脑筋, 伤脑筋 (to be a headache), 脑筋急转弯 (brainteaser), 他脑筋很好. A rigid thinker is 死脑筋, and 脑筋转不过来 is being unable to see another way.
column4: 这个问题要动一下脑筋。
column5: 這個問題要動一下腦筋。
column6: Zhège wèntí yào dòng yīxià nǎojīn.
column7: This problem takes some thinking.
column9: Spoken word for how one thinks or solves things: 動腦筋, 傷腦筋 (to be a headache), 腦筋急轉彎 (brainteaser), 他腦筋很好. A rigid thinker is 死腦筋, and 腦筋轉不過來 is being unable to see another way.

column3: The everyday word in Taiwan for the busiest shopping and nightlife area of a city; on the mainland people more often say 闹市 or 市中心. Goes with 逛 and 去: 周末去闹区逛街.
column6: Zhōumò de nàoqū rén hěn duō.
column7: The downtown area is crowded on weekends.
column9: The everyday word in Taiwan for the busiest shopping and nightlife area of a city; on the mainland people more often say 鬧市 or 市中心. Goes with 逛 and 去: 週末去鬧區逛街.

column3: Contrasts with 沿海 and 海边: the interior away from the coast, though 内陆 is the more usual word for a country's inland part today. 内地 is also the mainland's own word for the mainland (against 港澳台) and Hong Kong's; Taiwan says 大陆.
column4: 内地的天气比海边干燥。
column5: 內地的天氣比海邊乾燥。
column6: Nèidì de tiānqì bǐ hǎibiān gānzào.
column7: The weather inland is drier than by the sea.
column9: Contrasts with 沿海 and 海邊: the interior away from the coast, though 內陸 is the more usual word for a country's inland part today. 內地 is also the mainland's own word for the mainland (against 港澳臺) and Hong Kong's; Taiwan says 大陸.

column3: Describes someone who knows a trade or subject well, either as a predicate (他很内行) or before 人. The opposite is 外行. The 行 in this word is the one meaning a line of business, a trade.
column6: Tā duì diànnǎo hěn nèiháng.
column7: He is an expert on computers.
column9: Describes someone who knows a trade or subject well, either as a predicate (他很內行) or before 人. The opposite is 外行. The 行 in this word is the one meaning a line of business, a trade.

column3: The word of news, policy and school texts, for oil, coal, solar and the like. Typical partners are 能源危机 and 节省能源.
column6: Wǒmen yīnggāi jiéshěng néngyuán.
column7: We should save energy.
column9: The word of news, policy and school texts, for oil, coal, solar and the like. Typical partners are 能源危機 and 節省能源.

column3: Alone it is wet earth, mud on shoes or hands. It also turns up in 泥巴, 烂泥 and 水泥 (cement). For dry earth you walk on, 泥土 or 土 is the word.
column6: Tā de xiézi shàng dōu shì ní.
column7: His shoes are covered in mud.
column9: Alone it is wet earth, mud on shoes or hands. It also turns up in 泥巴, 爛泥 and 水泥 (cement). For dry earth you walk on, 泥土 or 土 is the word.

column3: Said of food that is too oily or too sweet (油腻), and also of a feeling: 吃腻了 or 看腻了 means you have had too much of something and are tired of it.
column6: Zhè dào cài tài nì le.
column7: This dish is too greasy.
column9: Said of food that is too oily or too sweet (油膩), and also of a feeling: 吃膩了 or 看膩了 means you have had too much of something and are tired of it.

column3: Adjective and verb: 黏黏的 is sticky to the touch, and 黏在一起 is to be stuck together. It is the standard form for sticky everywhere; 粘 is common in casual writing.
column6: Tángguǒ nián zài yáchǐ shàng le.
column7: The candy stuck to my teeth.
column9: Adjective and verb: 黏黏的 is sticky to the touch, and 黏在一起 is to be stuck together. It is the standard form for sticky everywhere; 粘 is common in casual writing.

column3: A common casual-writing variant of 黏 in the sense of sticky or to stick together (粘在一起). The standard form for it is 黏.
column6: Qǐng bǎ zhàopiàn nián zài zhèlǐ.
column7: Please stick the photo here.
column9: A common casual-writing variant of 黏 in the sense of sticky or to stick together (粘在一起). The standard form for it is 黏.

column3: Both a verb and a noun, and an everyday word: 尿床 for wetting the bed, 尿布 for a diaper, 尿液 in a medical setting. In polite speech people say 上厕所 instead of 尿尿.
column6: Bǎobao niào chuáng le.
column7: The baby wet the bed.
column9: Both a verb and a noun, and an everyday word: 尿床 for wetting the bed, 尿布 for a diaper, 尿液 in a medical setting. In polite speech people say 上廁所 instead of 尿尿.

column3: Done with the thumb and fingers: 捏鼻子, 捏面团, 捏一下. In 捏一把冷汗 it means to be anxious on someone's behalf, as when you watch a risky act.
column6: Tā niē zhe bízi zǒu guòqù.
column7: He walked past holding his nose.
column9: Done with the thumb and fingers: 捏鼻子, 捏麵團, 捏一下. In 捏一把冷汗 it means to be anxious on someone's behalf, as when you watch a risky act.

column3: Marks your choice between two options you may not like, in the pattern 㝉可 A 也不 B: you accept A rather than B. 㝉愿 means the same and the two are nearly interchangeable, though 㝉可 sounds a bit more written.
column4: 我宁可走路，也不想挤地铁。
column5: 我寧可走路，也不想擠地鐵。
column6: Wǒ nìngkě zǒulù, yě bù xiǎng jǐ dìtiě.
column7: I would rather walk than squeeze onto the subway.
column9: Marks your choice between two options you may not like, in the pattern 宁可 A 也不 B: you accept A rather than B. 宁愿 means the same and the two are nearly interchangeable, though 宁可 sounds a bit more written.

column3: Same pattern as 㝉可: 㝉愿 A 也不 B. Because 愿 means willing, it stresses that you are willing to accept the first thing, and it is slightly more spoken than 㝉可.
column4: 我宁愿早点出门，也不想迟到。
column5: 我寧願早點出門，也不想遲到。
column6: Wǒ nìngyuàn zǎodiǎn chūmén, yě bù xiǎng chídào.
column7: I would rather leave early than be late.
column9: Same pattern as 宁可: 宁愿 A 也不 B. Because 愿 means willing, it stresses that you are willing to accept the first thing, and it is slightly more spoken than 宁可.

column4: 雨后泥土的味道很好闻。
column5: 雨後泥土的味道很好聞。
column6: Yǔ hòu nítǔ de wèidào hěn hǎo wén.
column7: The smell of the earth after rain is lovely.

column3: The 场 here is a place for an activity, as in 牧场 and 养鸡场. Many farms open to visitors, and a 休闲农场 lets you pick fruit and stay the night.
column4: 我们周末去农场摘草莓。
column5: 我們週末去農場摘草莓。
column6: Wǒmen zhōumò qù nóngchǎng zhāi cǎoméi.
column7: On weekends we go to a farm to pick strawberries.
column9: The 場 here is a place for an activity, as in 牧場 and 養雞場. Many farms open to visitors, and a 休閒農場 lets you pick fruit and stay the night.

column3: What follows is the thing you got wrong: 弄错日期, 弄错人. Usually used when apologizing, as 我弄错了. 弄 is a general verb for doing, and the same pattern gives 弄坏 (break) and 弄脏 (make dirty).
column6: Duìbuqǐ, wǒ nòngcuò shíjiān le.
column7: Sorry, I got the time wrong.
column9: What follows is the thing you got wrong: 弄錯日期, 弄錯人. Usually used when apologizing, as 我弄錯了. 弄 is a general verb for doing, and the same pattern gives 弄壞 (break) and 弄髒 (make dirty).

column3: Goes with abstract nouns (兴趣, 气氛, 色彩, 乡土味) and with fog or clouds. For strong tea or coffee in everyday speech, 浓 alone is used.
column4: 他对历史有浓厚的兴趣。
column5: 他對歷史有濃厚的興趣。
column6: Tā duì lìshǐ yǒu nónghòu de xìngqù.
column7: He has a strong interest in history.
column9: Goes with abstract nouns (興趣, 氣氛, 色彩, 鄉土味) and with fog or clouds. For strong tea or coffee in everyday speech, 濃 alone is used.

column3: Somewhat storybook: 农夫与蛇 is a well-known fable. Today a farmer as a job is more often 农民, and 农夫 appears in stories and songs.
column4: 农夫早上很早就下田了。
column5: 農夫早上很早就下田了。
column6: Nóngfū zǎoshang hěn zǎo jiù xià tián le.
column7: The farmer goes down to the fields very early in the morning.
column9: Somewhat storybook: 農夫與蛇 is a well-known fable. Today a farmer as a job is more often 農民, and 農夫 appears in stories and songs.

column6: Zhèxiē shūcài méiyǒu nóngyào.
column7: These vegetables have no pesticide.

column3: A variant of the standard 偶尔. It sits before the verb: 偶而吃一次. Pair it with 经常 and 总是 to learn the range of frequency.
column6: Wǒ ǒu'ér huì qù páshān.
column7: I occasionally go hiking.
column9: A variant of the standard 偶爾. It sits before the verb: 偶而吃一次. Pair it with 經常 and 總是 to learn the range of frequency.

column3: Done by a group or by the body to what does not belong: 排斥新同学, 排斥新事物, and 排斥反应 after an organ transplant. It is stronger than 不喜欢 and means actively keeping something out.
column6: Tāmen páichì xīn lái de tóngxué.
column7: They shut out the new classmate.
column9: Done by a group or by the body to what does not belong: 排斥新同學, 排斥新事物, and 排斥反應 after an organ transplant. It is stronger than 不喜歡 and means actively keeping something out.

column3: Mostly in compounds: 攀岩 (rock climbing), 攀登 (climb a mountain, or reach a peak in a career) and 攀爬. It is also used for claiming connections with someone above you: 攀关系.
column6: Tāmen yīqǐ qù pān yán.
column7: They go rock climbing together.
column9: Mostly in compounds: 攀岩 (rock climbing), 攀登 (climb a mountain, or reach a peak in a career) and 攀爬. It is also used for claiming connections with someone above you: 攀關係.

column3: Mostly met in 大炮 (cannon) and 鞭炮 (firecrackers), which people set off with 放 at weddings, temple events and the New Year.
column6: Xīnnián shí dàjiā huì fàng biān pào.
column7: At New Year people set off firecrackers.
column9: Mostly met in 大炮 (cannon) and 鞭炮 (firecrackers), which people set off with 放 at weddings, temple events and the New Year.

column3: Said to someone's face or about them, and means respect for what they can do or have done: 我很佩服你, 令人佩服. It is warmer than 尊敬 and fits skill and courage more than rank.
column6: Wǒ hěn pèifú tā de yǒngqì.
column7: I really admire his courage.
column9: Said to someone's face or about them, and means respect for what they can do or have done: 我很佩服你, 令人佩服. It is warmer than 尊敬 and fits skill and courage more than rank.

column3: A formal word for going along with a guest, an official or a patient: 由老师陪同, 陪同参观. In ordinary speech use 陪 alone or 陪着.
column4: 家长陪同孩子一起参加。
column5: 家長陪同孩子一起參加。
column6: Jiāzhǎng péitóng háizi yīqǐ cānjiā.
column7: Parents take part together with their children.
column9: A formal word for going along with a guest, an official or a patient: 由老師陪同, 陪同參觀. In ordinary speech use 陪 alone or 陪著.

column3: Both hands held together, cupped: 捧着一杯茶, 一捧米 (a double handful, a measure word). A second sense is to flatter or praise: 捧场 means to support an event by coming.
column6: Tā shǒu lǐ pěng zhe yī wǎn rè tāng.
column7: She holds a bowl of hot soup in both hands.
column9: Both hands held together, cupped: 捧著一杯茶, 一捧米 (a double handful, a measure word). A second sense is to flatter or praise: 捧場 means to support an event by coming.

column3: Said of things that swell, from a balloon to a budget, and of the mind: 通货膨胀 is inflation, and 自信心膨胀 is an overblown sense of self-confidence.
column4: 通货膨胀让东西变贵了。
column5: 通貨膨脹讓東西變貴了。
column6: Tōnghuò péngzhàng ràng dōngxi biàn guì le.
column7: Inflation makes things more expensive.
column9: Said of things that swell, from a balloon to a budget, and of the mind: 通貨膨脹 is inflation, and 自信心膨脹 is an overblown sense of self-confidence.

column3: Before an adjective it softens: 偏小, 偏瘦, 偏贵, a bit on that side. As an adverb it means to do the opposite of what is wanted, out of stubbornness: 你不让我去，我偏要去. The doubled 偏偏 is its own word.
column6: Zhège fángjiān piān xiǎo.
column7: This room is on the small side.
column9: Before an adjective it softens: 偏小, 偏瘦, 偏貴, a bit on that side. As an adverb it means to do the opposite of what is wanted, out of stubbornness: 你不讓我去，我偏要去. The doubled 偏偏 is its own word.

column3: Spoken, with a complaint in it: things turn out the opposite of what you wanted (我一出门，偏偏下雨), or one person is singled out (为什么偏偏是我?). It can also mean insisting on doing what is not wanted.
column6: Wǒ gāng chūmén, piānpiān xiàyǔ le.
column7: Just as I went out, of all times, it started to rain.
column9: Spoken, with a complaint in it: things turn out the opposite of what you wanted (我一出門，偏偏下雨), or one person is singled out (為什麼偏偏是我?). It can also mean insisting on doing what is not wanted.

column3: A habit of eating only some kinds of food, most often said of children who refuse vegetables: 小孩偏食. It is a verb as well as a noun: 他很偏食. The word is a mild criticism.
column6: Háizi piānshí, bù chī qīngcài.
column7: The child is a picky eater and doesn't eat green vegetables.
column9: A habit of eating only some kinds of food, most often said of children who refuse vegetables: 小孩偏食. It is a verb as well as a noun: 他很偏食. The word is a mild criticism.

column3: For a preference or tendency: 偏向选这个. When about a judge, a parent or a referee, it means unfair favoring of one side: 偏向某一方.
column6: Wǒ piānxiàng mǎi piányi yīdiǎn de.
column7: I lean toward buying the cheaper one.
column9: For a preference or tendency: 偏向選這個. When about a judge, a parent or a referee, it means unfair favoring of one side: 偏向某一方.

column3: A casual word for a film, counted with 部: 看片子, 一部好片子. 电影 is the neutral word. Taiwan reads it piànzi, as on this card, and also piānzi; the mainland says piānzi.
column6: Zhè bù piànzi hěn hǎokàn.
column7: This film is really good.
column9: A casual word for a film, counted with 部: 看片子, 一部好片子. 電影 is the neutral word. Taiwan reads it piànzi, as on this card, and also piānzi; the mainland says piānzi.

column3: What the wind or air carries: 雪花飘下来, 飘着香味, and a flag flutters as 飘扬. It describes slow, light motion, not fast flying.
column6: Shùyè zài fēng zhōng piāo zhe.
column7: The leaves drift in the wind.
column9: What the wind or air carries: 雪花飄下來, 飄著香味, and a flag flutters as 飄揚. It describes slow, light motion, not fast flying.

column3: The everyday word, a bit rude in formal talk (in a doctor's office, people say 臀部). It also names the back end of things: 车屁股. 打屁股 is to spank.
column6: Tā shuāi le yī jiāo, pìgu hěn tòng.
column7: He fell and his bottom hurts.
column9: The everyday word, a bit rude in formal talk (in a doctor's office, people say 臀部). It also names the back end of things: 車屁股. 打屁股 is to spank.

column3: Tiredness of the body or the mind, more written than 累: 感到疲倦, 疲倦的脸. It suits tiredness that has built up, and it does not describe being bored.
column6: Liánxù gōngzuò hòu tā hěn píjuàn.
column7: After working nonstop he is very tired.
column9: Tiredness of the body or the mind, more written than 累: 感到疲倦, 疲倦的臉. It suits tiredness that has built up, and it does not describe being bored.

column3: Works as a noun and as an adjective (感到疲劳, 他很疲劳), and is the word of warnings and health talk: 疲劳驾驶 (drowsy driving), 视觉疲劳 (eye strain), 消除疲劳. 疲倦 is more about how you feel; 疲劳 is about fatigue from work.
column6: Píláo jiàshǐ hěn wēixiǎn.
column7: Driving while tired is dangerous.
column9: Works as a noun and as an adjective (感到疲勞, 他很疲勞), and is the word of warnings and health talk: 疲勞駕駛 (drowsy driving), 視覺疲勞 (eye strain), 消除疲勞. 疲倦 is more about how you feel; 疲勞 is about fatigue from work.

column3: A person's conduct and values, in a written, school-like register: 品德高尚, 品德教育. It is not used for a thing's quality.
column4: 老师很重视学生的品德。
column5: 老師很重視學生的品德。
column6: Lǎoshī hěn zhòngshì xuéshēng de pǐndé.
column7: The teacher cares a lot about students' character.
column9: A person's conduct and values, in a written, school-like register: 品德高尚, 品德教育. It is not used for a thing's quality.

column3: Used for the body and for abstract things: 保持平衡, 失去平衡, 收支平衡, 工作与生活的平衡. It also works as a verb: 平衡一下 means to bring things into balance.
column6: Qí zìxíngchē yào bǎochí pínghéng.
column7: You have to keep your balance when riding a bicycle.
column9: Used for the body and for abstract things: 保持平衡, 失去平衡, 收支平衡, 工作與生活的平衡. It also works as a verb: 平衡一下 means to bring things into balance.

column3: The name of the sport on the mainland, and of the little ball everywhere. Taiwan's official and sports name for the game is 桌球, but 乒乓球 is also common in everyday speech there.
column6: Tāmen zài dǎ pīngpāngqiú.
column7: They are playing table tennis.
column9: The name of the sport on the mainland, and of the little ball everywhere. Taiwan's official and sports name for the game is 桌球, but 乒乓球 is also common in everyday speech there.

column3: Taiwan's usual name for table tennis: 打桌球, 桌球比赛, and the mainland says 乒乓球. In Taiwan billiards is 撞球, while in Hong Kong 桌球 means billiards or snooker.
column6: Wǒ gēge xǐhuān dǎ zhuōqiú.
column7: My older brother likes to play table tennis.
column9: Taiwan's usual name for table tennis: 打桌球, 桌球比賽, and the mainland says 乒乓球. In Taiwan billiards is 撞球, while in Hong Kong 桌球 means billiards or snooker.

column3: Goes before a verb and shows effort to the limit: 拼命工作, 拼命跑, 拼命道歉. It can be used with 地 (拼命地跑). Literally you risk your life, but the word is not grim and is used for ordinary effort.
column6: Tā pīnmìng de pǎo xiàng chēzhàn.
column7: He ran to the station as hard as he could.
column9: Goes before a verb and shows effort to the limit: 拼命工作, 拼命跑, 拼命道歉. It can be used with 地 (拼命地跑). Literally you risk your life, but the word is not grim and is used for ordinary effort.

column3: A formal word for hiring a professional for their skill: 聘请律师, 聘请专家, 聘请老师. The employer is a school, company or family. 聘用 is the term for taking someone on staff.
column4: 公司聘请了一位新律师。
column5: 公司聘請了一位新律師。
column6: Gōngsī pìnqǐng le yī wèi xīn lǜshī.
column7: The company hired a new lawyer.
column9: A formal word for hiring a professional for their skill: 聘請律師, 聘請專家, 聘請老師. The employer is a school, company or family. 聘用 is the term for taking someone on staff.

column3: The written word for being poor: 贫穷的家庭, 摆脱贫穷. In speech people say 穷, and 贫穷 sounds like a report or a story.
column6: Tā xiǎoshíhou jiālǐ hěn pínqióng.
column7: His family was very poor when he was little.
column9: The written word for being poor: 貧窮的家庭, 擺脫貧窮. In speech people say 窮, and 貧窮 sounds like a report or a story.

column3: Rarely alone, and mostly written-style in compounds: 贫穷, 贫血 (anemia), 贫富 (rich and poor), 清贫 (poor but honest). In northern speech it can mean talkative, as in 贫嘴.
column6: Pín fù chājù yuèláiyuè dà.
column7: The gap between rich and poor keeps growing.
column9: Rarely alone, and mostly written-style in compounds: 貧窮, 貧血 (anemia), 貧富 (rich and poor), 清貧 (poor but honest). In northern speech it can mean talkative, as in 貧嘴.

column3: A serious, public criticism, stronger and more formal than 批评: 批判政府, 受到批判. It is aimed at ideas, policies and behavior of a group more than at a person's small slip.
column4: 这篇文章批判了社会问题。
column5: 這篇文章批判了社會問題。
column6: Zhè piān wénzhāng pīpàn le shèhuì wèntí.
column7: This article criticizes problems in society.
column9: A serious, public criticism, stronger and more formal than 批評: 批判政府, 受到批判. It is aimed at ideas, policies and behavior of a group more than at a person's small slip.

column3: An adverb of degree in a written or formal style: 颇有名, 颇为满意, 颇有道理. It goes before an adjective or before 有.
column6: Zhè jiā cāntīng pō yǒumíng.
column7: This restaurant is quite well known.
column9: An adverb of degree in a written or formal style: 頗有名, 頗為滿意, 頗有道理. It goes before an adjective or before 有.

column3: Describes things in poor shape (clothes, a car, a house) and looks down on them. As a noun it means junk: 收破烂 is to collect scrap for sale.
column4: 他穿着一件破烂的外套。
column5: 他穿著一件破爛的外套。
column6: Tā chuān zhe yī jiàn pòlàn de wàitào.
column7: He wore a tattered coat.
column9: Describes things in poor shape (clothes, a car, a house) and looks down on them. As a noun it means junk: 收破爛 is to collect scrap for sale.

column6: Liǎng guó de tánpàn pòliè le.
column7: The talks between the two countries broke down.

column3: A wife calls her husband's mother 婆婆, and her own mother is 妈妈. The wife's mother, said by her son-in-law or in writing, is 岳母. In some places 婆婆 is also a kindly address for an old woman.
column6: Wǒ pópo zhù zài Táinán.
column7: My mother-in-law lives in Tainan.
column9: A wife calls her husband's mother 婆婆, and her own mother is 媽媽. The wife's mother, said by her son-in-law or in writing, is 岳母. In some places 婆婆 is also a kindly address for an old woman.

column3: To throw oneself forward at someone or something: 扑向, 扑过来. A dog or child that jumps up on you does it. 扑了个空 is to grab at nothing.
column6: Xiǎogǒu pū dào wǒ shēnshang.
column7: The puppy jumped onto me.
column9: To throw oneself forward at someone or something: 撲向, 撲過來. A dog or child that jumps up on you does it. 撲了個空 is to grab at nothing.

column3: As a verb it means to spread out: 铺床 (make the bed), 铺地毯, 铺路 (pave). The noun, a shop, is a different reading, as in 店铺.
column6: Qǐng bāng wǒ pū chuáng.
column7: Please help me make the bed.
column9: As a verb it means to spread out: 鋪床 (make the bed), 鋪地毯, 鋪路 (pave). The noun, a shop, is a different reading, as in 店鋪.

column3: Count it with 道 or 条 for the stream of falling water, or with 座 when it is a landmark in the scenery. Place names put it last: 黄果树瀑布.
column4: 山里有一座很高的瀑布。
column5: 山裡有一座很高的瀑布。
column6: Shān lǐ yǒu yī zuò hěn gāo de pùbù.
column7: There is a very tall waterfall in the mountains.
column9: Count it with 道 or 條 for the stream of falling water, or with 座 when it is a landmark in the scenery. Place names put it last: 黃果樹瀑布.

column3: The object is a fire or something that spreads: 火灾, 疫情, 害虫. It is a verb of news reports. A candle or a small flame is 吹灭, and the plain phrase for putting out a fire is 灭火.
column4: 消防员很快扑灭了大火。
column5: 消防員很快撲滅了大火。
column6: Xiāofángyuán hěn kuài pūmiè le dàhuǒ.
column7: The firefighters quickly put out the big fire.
column9: The object is a fire or something that spreads: 火災, 疫情, 害蟲. It is a verb of news reports. A candle or a small flame is 吹滅, and the plain phrase for putting out a fire is 滅火.

column3: The general word for board games, played with the verb 下: 下棋. A particular game is named in front of it: 象棋, 围棋, 跳棋. The pieces are 棋子 and the board is 棋盘.
column6: Yéye xǐhuān xià qí.
column7: Grandpa likes to play chess.
column9: The general word for board games, played with the verb 下: 下棋. A particular game is named in front of it: 象棋, 圍棋, 跳棋. The pieces are 棋子 and the board is 棋盤.

column3: Counted with 面: 一面旗. Alone it turns up in verbs and compounds: 升旗 to raise it, 降旗 to lower it, 国旗, 红旗. The everyday noun for a flag you hold in your hand is 旗子.
column6: Xuéxiào měitiān zǎoshang shēng qí.
column7: The school raises the flag every morning.
column9: Counted with 面: 一面旗. Alone it turns up in verbs and compounds: 升旗 to raise it, 降旗 to lower it, 國旗, 紅旗. The everyday noun for a flag you hold in your hand is 旗子.

column3: Counted with 面: 一面旗子. It is the everyday noun for a flag you hold, wave (挥, 摇) or see on a pole; 旗 alone is kept for compounds such as 国旗 and verbs such as 升旗.
column6: Háizimen huī zhe xiǎo qízi.
column7: The children are waving little flags.
column9: Counted with 面: 一面旗子. It is the everyday noun for a flag you hold, wave (揮, 搖) or see on a pole; 旗 alone is kept for compounds such as 國旗 and verbs such as 升旗.

column3: Used in compounds and formal writing: 妻子, 夫妻, 未婚妻, 妻儿. On its own it sounds written, so in speech people say 老婆 or 太太, and 妻子 in careful speech.
column6: Tā hé qī zi yī qǐ lái le.
column7: He came together with his wife.
column9: Used in compounds and formal writing: 妻子, 夫妻, 未婚妻, 妻兒. On its own it sounds written, so in speech people say 老婆 or 太太, and 妻子 in careful speech.

column3: What you do to a leash, a child, a bike or someone's hand: 牵狗, 牵着孩子, 牵车, 牵手 for holding hands. In compounds it means to involve: 牵涉, 牵连. In Taiwan 牵手 also means a spouse.
column6: Tā qiān zhe gǒu zài gōngyuán sànbù.
column7: He is walking his dog in the park.
column9: What you do to a leash, a child, a bike or someone's hand: 牽狗, 牽著孩子, 牽車, 牽手 for holding hands. In compounds it means to involve: 牽涉, 牽連. In Taiwan 牽手 also means a spouse.

column3: A formal verb, found mostly in compounds: 搬迁 and 迁移 to relocate or migrate, 迁居 to change residence, 迁都 to move the capital. In speech, moving house is 搬家; 搬迁 suits a company, school or village.
column4: 这些候鸟每年都要迁移。
column5: 這些候鳥每年都要遷移。
column6: Zhè xiē hòuniǎo měi nián dōu yào qiān yí.
column7: These migratory birds migrate every year.
column9: A formal verb, found mostly in compounds: 搬遷 and 遷移 to relocate or migrate, 遷居 to change residence, 遷都 to move the capital. In speech, moving house is 搬家; 搬遷 suits a company, school or village.

column3: Common on signs and in directions: 前方施工, 前方路口. It looks ahead along the way you are going, farther off than 前面, and in war it is the front line. Its pair is 后方, the rear.
column4: 前方有一辆车停在路中间。
column5: 前方有一輛車停在路中間。
column6: Qiánfāng yǒu yī liàng chē tíng zài lù zhōngjiān.
column7: There is a car stopped in the middle of the road ahead.
column9: Common on signs and in directions: 前方施工, 前方路口. It looks ahead along the way you are going, farther off than 前面, and in war it is the front line. Its pair is 后方, the rear.

column3: Mostly met as 女强人, a woman who has made it in her career, said with admiration though it can hint at someone hard-driving. In politics it is a strongman: 政治强人.
column6: Tā shì gōngsī lǐ de nǚ qiángrén.
column7: She is a powerful career woman at the company.
column9: Mostly met as 女強人, a woman who has made it in her career, said with admiration though it can hint at someone hard-driving. In politics it is a strongman: 政治強人.

column3: A written, polite word for the feeling behind an apology, in set phrases: 表示歉意, 深表歉意, 致以歉意. Notices and official statements use it; to say sorry out loud, say 对不起 or 抱歉.
column6: Wǒ duì cǐ shēn biǎo qiànyì.
column7: I am deeply sorry for this.
column9: A written, polite word for the feeling behind an apology, in set phrases: 表示歉意, 深表歉意, 致以歉意. Notices and official statements use it; to say sorry out loud, say 對不起 or 抱歉.

column3: Its pair is 后院, the back yard. A yard in general is 院子 in everyday speech, and 前院 is the one at the front of a house or a traditional courtyard home.
column4: 他家的前院种了很多花。
column5: 他家的前院種了很多花。
column6: Tā jiā de qiányuàn zhòng le hěn duō huā.
column7: The front yard of his house is planted with lots of flowers.
column9: Its pair is 後院, the back yard. A yard in general is 院子 in everyday speech, and 前院 is the one at the front of a house or a traditional courtyard home.

column3: Praises a method, design, plan or reply that solves a problem neatly: 巧妙的办法, 巧妙地回答. It is about the cleverness of the technique, not of a person, who is 聪明. Sly or crafty is 狡猾.
column4: 他巧妙地解决了这个问题。
column5: 他巧妙地解決了這個問題。
column6: Tā qiǎomiào de jiějué le zhège wèntí.
column7: He solved the problem cleverly.
column9: Praises a method, design, plan or reply that solves a problem neatly: 巧妙的辦法, 巧妙地回答. It is about the cleverness of the technique, not of a person, who is 聰明. Sly or crafty is 狡猾.

column3: Hardly used alone: it is found in doubled and set words such as 悄悄 (on the quiet, softly), 悄悄话 (whispered words, secrets) and 悄然. The dictionary reads 悄悄 as qiāoqiāo, with Taiwan reading it qiǎoqiǎo.
column6: Tā qiǎo qiǎo de zǒujìn fángjiān.
column7: He walked quietly into the room.
column9: Hardly used alone: it is found in doubled and set words such as 悄悄 (on the quiet, softly), 悄悄話 (whispered words, secrets) and 悄然. The dictionary reads 悄悄 as qiāoqiāo, with Taiwan reading it qiǎoqiǎo.

column3: Equipment for a particular activity, with the activity in front: 运动器材, 摄影器材, 医疗器材, 实验器材. It names the gear as a group, not one machine; 设备 is for installed machinery and 工具 for hand tools.
column4: 健身房里有很多运动器材。
column5: 健身房裡有很多運動器材。
column6: Jiànshēnfáng lǐ yǒu hěn duō yùndòng qìcái.
column7: The gym has a lot of sports equipment.
column9: Equipment for a particular activity, with the activity in front: 運動器材, 攝影器材, 醫療器材, 實驗器材. It names the gear as a group, not one machine; 設備 is for installed machinery and 工具 for hand tools.

column3: Opens the story of a change and is usually answered by 后来: 起初…后来…. It looks back at how things were at the start, so it never goes with a plan for the future; for that use 先 or 首先.
column4: 起初我不习惯这里的天气。
column5: 起初我不習慣這裡的天氣。
column6: Qǐchū wǒ bù xíguàn zhèlǐ de tiānqì.
column7: At first I wasn't used to the weather here.
column9: Opens the story of a change and is usually answered by 後來: 起初…後來…. It looks back at how things were at the start, so it never goes with a plan for the future; for that use 先 or 首先.

column3: Stronger than 生气: the anger is at something unfair or insulting, not a small annoyance. 非常气愤, 令人气愤, 气愤地说. A more formal near-synonym is 愤怒.
column4: 听到这个消息，他非常气愤。
column5: 聽到這個消息，他非常氣憤。
column6: Tīngdào zhège xiāoxi, tā fēicháng qìfèn.
column7: When he heard the news he was furious.
column9: Stronger than 生氣: the anger is at something unfair or insulting, not a small annoyance. 非常氣憤, 令人氣憤, 氣憤地說. A more formal near-synonym is 憤怒.

column3: How a room, meeting or party feels. Adjectives: 热烈, 紧张, 轻松. Verbs for changing it: 活跃气氛 to liven up, 缓和气氛 to ease, 破坏气氛 to spoil. A more written twin is 氛围.
column6: Cāntīng lǐ de qìfēn hěn qīngsōng.
column7: The atmosphere in the restaurant is relaxed.
column9: How a room, meeting or party feels. Adjectives: 熱烈, 緊張, 輕鬆. Verbs for changing it: 活躍氣氛 to liven up, 緩和氣氛 to ease, 破壞氣氛 to spoil. A more written twin is 氛圍.

column3: The verb of news reports for a building, vehicle or factory catching fire: 房子起火了, 起火原因. In speech 着火 is also common.
column4: 昨晚附近的工厂起火了。
column5: 昨晚附近的工廠起火了。
column6: Zuówǎn fùjìn de gōngchǎng qǐhuǒ le.
column7: A factory nearby caught fire last night.
column9: The verb of news reports for a building, vehicle or factory catching fire: 房子起火了, 起火原因. In speech 着火 is also common.

column3: Means getting rid of something completely: 清除垃圾, 清除积雪, 清除障碍, 清除病毒, 清除缓存. 清理 is tidying up or sorting out; 清除 is removing it for good.
column4: 工人正在清除路上的积雪。
column5: 工人正在清除路上的積雪。
column6: Gōngrén zhèngzài qīngchú lùshàng de jīxuě.
column7: Workers are clearing the snow off the road.
column9: Means getting rid of something completely: 清除垃圾, 清除積雪, 清除障礙, 清除病毒, 清除緩存. 清理 is tidying up or sorting out; 清除 is removing it for good.

column3: For food that is not oily or heavily seasoned: 清淡的菜, 口味清淡. Doctors say 饮食清淡 to someone who is ill. It also fits a pale color and slow business: 生意清淡.
column4: 生病的时候要吃清淡的东西。
column5: 生病的時候要吃清淡的東西。
column6: Shēngbìng de shíhou yào chī qīngdàn de dōngxi.
column7: When you are ill you should eat light food.
column9: For food that is not oily or heavily seasoned: 清淡的菜, 口味清淡. Doctors say 飲食清淡 to someone who is ill. It also fits a pale color and slow business: 生意清淡.

column3: Paired with 重伤. In accident reports the number of people comes first: 两人轻伤, 一人重伤. A person 受轻伤; damage to things is not called 轻伤.
column4: 这次车祸只有两个人受了轻伤。
column5: 這次車禍只有兩個人受了輕傷。
column6: Zhè cì chēhuò zhǐyǒu liǎng ge rén shòu le qīngshāng.
column7: Only two people were slightly hurt in the accident.
column9: Paired with 重傷. In accident reports the number of people comes first: 兩人輕傷, 一人重傷. A person 受輕傷; damage to things is not called 輕傷.

column3: The object is a person or a problem: 轻视对手, 轻视困难. It covers both contempt and careless underestimating, so 不能轻视 often just means do not take it lightly. In speech, to look down on someone is 看不起.
column4: 不要轻视任何一个对手。
column5: 不要輕視任何一個對手。
column6: Bù yào qīngshì rènhé yī ge duìshǒu.
column7: Don't underestimate any opponent.
column9: The object is a person or a problem: 輕視對手, 輕視困難. It covers both contempt and careless underestimating, so 不能輕視 often just means do not take it lightly. In speech, to look down on someone is 看不起.

column6: Tā gěi tā xiě le yī fēng qíngshū.
column7: He wrote her a love letter.

column3: Describes what you see, hear or think: 画面清晰, 声音清晰, 记忆清晰, 思路清晰. It is written and slightly formal; in speech 清楚 is more common, and it also covers understanding: 我很清楚.
column6: Zhè zhāng zhàopiàn pāi de hěn qīngxī.
column7: This photo is very sharp.
column9: Describes what you see, hear or think: 畫面清晰, 聲音清晰, 記憶清晰, 思路清晰. It is written and slightly formal; in speech 清楚 is more common, and it also covers understanding: 我很清楚.

column3: Both a noun and a verb. Noun: 有…的倾向, 政治倾向, 暴力倾向. Verb: 倾向于 plus a view or choice, as in 我倾向于接受. It describes a pattern or a lean, not a single act.
column6: Tā yǒu tuōyán de qīngxiàng.
column7: He has a tendency to put things off.
column9: Both a noun and a verb. Noun: 有…的傾向, 政治傾向, 暴力傾向. Verb: 傾向於 plus a view or choice, as in 我傾向於接受. It describes a pattern or a lean, not a single act.

column3: A state of mind that comes and goes: 情绪好, 情绪低落, 情绪激动, 控制情绪. 心情 is the plain word for how you feel; 情绪 is more psychological. 有情绪 means to be upset about something.
column6: Tā jīntiān qíngxù bù tài hǎo.
column7: He is not in a good mood today.
column9: A state of mind that comes and goes: 情緒好, 情緒低落, 情緒激動, 控制情緒. 心情 is the plain word for how you feel; 情緒 is more psychological. 有情緒 means to be upset about something.

column3: The object is a right or an interest, or someone's body or health: 侵害权利, 侵害隐私, 侵害消费者利益. It is the language of law and news. 侵犯 is a common close word for violating rights; 侵害 stresses the harm done.
column4: 这样做侵害了别人的隐私。
column5: 這樣做侵害了別人的隱私。
column6: Zhèyàng zuò qīnhài le biérén de yǐnsī.
column7: Doing this infringes on other people's privacy.
column9: The object is a right or an interest, or someone's body or health: 侵害權利, 侵害隱私, 侵害消費者利益. It is the language of law and news. 侵犯 is a common close word for violating rights; 侵害 stresses the harm done.

column3: Goes before a verb of speaking, hearing or tasting to say the person did it directly, not through a rumor: 亲口说, 亲口承认, 亲口尝. 亲 forms a set with other body words: 亲眼, 亲耳, 亲手.
column6: Zhè shì tā qīnkǒu gàosu wǒ de.
column7: He told me this himself.
column9: Goes before a verb of speaking, hearing or tasting to say the person did it directly, not through a rumor: 親口說, 親口承認, 親口嘗. 親 forms a set with other body words: 親眼, 親耳, 親手.

column3: Praise for steady hard work without complaint, often for farmers, workers or a mother: 勤劳的人, 勤劳致富. 勤奋 is the one for studying. 努力 is a push toward a goal, while 勤劳 is a habit.
column6: Tā shì yī ge qínláo de nóngfū.
column7: He is a hardworking farmer.
column9: Praise for steady hard work without complaint, often for farmers, workers or a mother: 勤勞的人, 勤勞致富. 勤奮 is the one for studying. 努力 is a push toward a goal, while 勤勞 is a habit.

column3: Relatives beyond your own household. 走亲戚 is visiting them, a big part of the New Year: 亲戚朋友. To address or name a particular relative you use the title, such as 舅舅 or 姑姑.
column4: 过年的时候我们去看亲戚。
column5: 過年的時候我們去看親戚。
column6: Guònián de shíhou wǒmen qù kàn qīnqi.
column7: At New Year we go to see our relatives.
column9: Relatives beyond your own household. 走親戚 is visiting them, a big part of the New Year: 親戚朋友. To address or name a particular relative you use the title, such as 舅舅 or 姑姑.

column3: Entering where you have no right: a territory (侵入领空), a home (侵入住宅), a computer system. It is the language of news and law. 入侵 is the reversed twin and more common for armies and viruses.
column4: 有人侵入了公司的电脑系统。
column5: 有人侵入了公司的電腦系統。
column6: Yǒu rén qīnrù le gōngsī de diànnǎo xìtǒng.
column7: Someone broke into the company's computer system.
column9: Entering where you have no right: a territory (侵入領空), a home (侵入住宅), a computer system. It is the language of news and law. 入侵 is the reversed twin and more common for armies and viruses.

column3: A room in a school or the military where several people sleep: 学生寝室, 寝室管理. It is the everyday student word for a dorm room. At home a bedroom is 卧室, and 宿舍 is the dorm as a whole.
column6: Wǒ de qǐnshì yǒu sì ge rén.
column7: There are four people in my dorm room.
column9: A room in a school or the military where several people sleep: 學生寢室, 寢室管理. It is the everyday student word for a dorm room. At home a bedroom is 臥室, and 宿舍 is the dorm as a whole.

column3: Counted with 件: 穿旗袍, 一件旗袍. Today it is dressy clothing for weddings, banquets and performances.
column4: 她穿着一件红色的旗袍。
column5: 她穿著一件紅色的旗袍。
column6: Tā chuān zhe yī jiàn hóngsè de qípáo.
column7: She is wearing a red cheongsam.
column9: Counted with 件: 穿旗袍, 一件旗袍. Today it is dressy clothing for weddings, banquets and performances.

column3: The object is a person who trusted you: 欺骗顾客, 欺骗感情, 被欺骗. Stronger than 说谎, which is just lying. In speech 骗 alone is the common verb: 骗人, 被骗; a con artist is 骗子.
column6: Tā qīpiàn le hěn duō lǎorén.
column7: He cheated a lot of old people.
column9: The object is a person who trusted you: 欺騙顧客, 欺騙感情, 被欺騙. Stronger than 說謊, which is just lying. In speech 騙 alone is the common verb: 騙人, 被騙; a con artist is 騙子.

column3: Followed by the group that is treated worse: 歧视外国人, 种族歧视, 性别歧视, 年龄歧视. 受到歧视 is to suffer it. The same word is both the verb and the noun.
column4: 我们不应该歧视任何人。
column5: 我們不應該歧視任何人。
column6: Wǒmen bù yīnggāi qíshì rènhé rén.
column7: We should not discriminate against anyone.
column9: Followed by the group that is treated worse: 歧視外國人, 種族歧視, 性別歧視, 年齡歧視. 受到歧視 is to suffer it. The same word is both the verb and the noun.

column3: Used for an attempt that is disapproved of: 企图逃跑, 企图抢劫, 企图掩盖. For a neutral or good plan use 试图 or 打算. As a noun: 他的企图, 犯罪企图.
column6: Tā qǐtú cóng hòumén táozǒu.
column7: He tried to escape through the back door.
column9: Used for an attempt that is disapproved of: 企圖逃跑, 企圖搶劫, 企圖掩蓋. For a neutral or good plan use 試圖 or 打算. As a noun: 他的企圖, 犯罪企圖.

column3: A verb plus its object, so the person goes after 向: 向她求婚, not 求婚她. Around it: 求婚戒指, then 订婚 and 结婚. The answer is 答应 or 拒绝.
column6: Tā zài hǎibiān xiàng tā qiúhūn.
column7: He proposed to her at the seaside.
column9: A verb plus its object, so the person goes after 向: 向她求婚, not 求婚她. Around it: 求婚戒指, then 訂婚 and 結婚. The answer is 答應 or 拒絕.

column3: A smell as a property of something: 难闻的气味, 香甜的气味, 没有气味. Counted with 股. 味道 is the everyday word and covers both taste and smell; 气味 is only smell.
column4: 房间里有一股奇怪的气味。
column5: 房間裡有一股奇怪的氣味。
column6: Fángjiān lǐ yǒu yī gǔ qíguài de qìwèi.
column7: There is a strange smell in the room.
column9: A smell as a property of something: 難聞的氣味, 香甜的氣味, 沒有氣味. Counted with 股. 味道 is the everyday word and covers both taste and smell; 氣味 is only smell.

column3: A faint feel that something gives off, mostly figurative: 春天的气息, 生活气息, 泥土的气息. It can also be a person's breath when weak: 气息微弱. To breathe is 呼吸.
column6: Kōngqì lǐ yǒu chūntiān de qìxī.
column7: There is a breath of spring in the air.
column9: A faint feel that something gives off, mostly figurative: 春天的氣息, 生活氣息, 泥土的氣息. It can also be a person's breath when weak: 氣息微弱. To breathe is 呼吸.

column3: Said of the man: he 娶 the woman, and she 嫁 him: 娶老婆, 嫁给他. It takes the bride as its object and is never said of the woman. The pair together is 嫁娶.
column6: Tā dǎsuàn míngnián qǔ tā.
column7: He plans to marry her next year.
column9: Said of the man: he 娶 the woman, and she 嫁 him: 娶老婆, 嫁給他. It takes the bride as its object and is never said of the woman. The pair together is 嫁娶.

column3: A fist you clench (握紧拳头) or swing (挥拳头); 一拳 counts a punch: 打了他一拳. In business writing 拳头产品 is a flagship product.
column6: Tā shēngqì de wòjǐn le quántou.
column7: He angrily clenched his fist.
column9: A fist you clench (握緊拳頭) or swing (揮拳頭); 一拳 counts a punch: 打了他一拳. In business writing 拳頭產品 is a flagship product.

column3: For being absent from a meeting, a court session or a ceremony: 缺席会议, 无故缺席, 缺席审判 (trial in absentia). For school or work, 请假 is asking for leave and 旷课 is skipping class.
column6: Tā jīntiān quēxí le huìyì.
column7: He was absent from the meeting today.
column9: For being absent from a meeting, a court session or a ceremony: 缺席會議, 無故缺席, 缺席審判 (trial in absentia). For school or work, 請假 is asking for leave and 曠課 is skipping class.

column3: Makes someone the butt of the laughter: 取笑别人, 别取笑我, 被取笑. It can be friendly teasing between friends; 嘲笑 is the harsher, mocking one.
column4: 大家都取笑他的新发型。
column5: 大家都取笑他的新髮型。
column6: Dàjiā dōu qǔxiào tā de xīn fàxíng.
column7: Everyone teased him about his new hairstyle.
column9: Makes someone the butt of the laughter: 取笑別人, 別取笑我, 被取笑. It can be friendly teasing between friends; 嘲笑 is the harsher, mocking one.

column3: Describes a road or river that winds, and a story, process or career with many twists: 曲折的小路, 曲折的经历, 几经曲折. The twists usually involve setbacks. A plain bend in a line or pipe is 弯曲.
column6: Zhè tiáo shānlù hěn qūzhé.
column7: This mountain road is very winding.
column9: Describes a road or river that winds, and a story, process or career with many twists: 曲折的小路, 曲折的經歷, 幾經曲折. The twists usually involve setbacks. A plain bend in a line or pipe is 彎曲.

column3: A verb that also works as a noun: 作出让步, 互相让步, 不肯让步. In talks it means giving up part of your position. Literal giving way is 让路 for a road and 让座 for a seat.
column6: Shuāngfāng dōu bù kěn ràngbù.
column7: Neither side is willing to give way.
column9: A verb that also works as a noun: 作出讓步, 互相讓步, 不肯讓步. In talks it means giving up part of your position. Literal giving way is 讓路 for a road and 讓座 for a seat.

column3: Followed by what you cause or whom you provoke: 惹麻烦, 惹祸, 惹他生气, 别惹我. 惹人喜欢 is the pleasant side, meaning endearing.
column6: Nǐ bié rě tā shēngqì.
column7: Don't make him angry.
column9: Followed by what you cause or whom you provoke: 惹麻煩, 惹禍, 惹他生氣, 別惹我. 惹人喜歡 is the pleasant side, meaning endearing.

column3: A person's moral character and dignity: 人格高尚, 尊重人格, 侮辱人格. Psychology uses it for personality as a whole: 人格测试. A lively personality in everyday talk is 个性 or 性格.
column4: 他的人格受到大家的尊敬。
column5: 他的人格受到大家的尊敬。
column6: Tā de réngé shòudào dàjiā de zūnjìng.
column7: His character is respected by everyone.
column9: A person's moral character and dignity: 人格高尚, 尊重人格, 侮辱人格. Psychology uses it for personality as a whole: 人格測試. A lively personality in everyday talk is 個性 or 性格.

column3: Warmth you feel from people: 有人情味 or 缺乏人情味, said of a person, shop, company or neighborhood. 人情 alone is favors and social obligations, as in 欠人情, to owe a favor.
column6: Zhè jiā xiǎo diàn hěn yǒu rénqíngwèi.
column7: This little shop has a lot of human warmth.
column9: Warmth you feel from people: 有人情味 or 缺乏人情味, said of a person, shop, company or neighborhood. 人情 alone is favors and social obligations, as in 欠人情, to owe a favor.

column3: The same word with the 儿 ending of northern speech: 有人情味儿, warm and kind. Without the 儿 it is 人情味, with the same meaning.
column4: 这个城市很有人情味儿。
column5: 這個城市很有人情味兒。
column6: Zhège chéngshì hěn yǒu rénqíngwèir.
column7: This city has a lot of human warmth.
column9: The same word with the 兒 ending of northern speech: 有人情味兒, warm and kind. Without the 兒 it is 人情味, with the same meaning.

column3: A word of news, law and school civics, plural in sense: the rights every person has, as in 人权组织, 尊重人权 and 侵犯人权.
column6: Měi ge rén dōu yīnggāi yǒu rénquán.
column7: Everyone should have human rights.
column9: A word of news, law and school civics, plural in sense: the rights every person has, as in 人權組織, 尊重人權 and 侵犯人權.

column3: In a company it is the department that handles hiring, pay and promotion, with set phrases such as 人事部门 and 人事调动. The "ways of the world" sense is rarer, as in 不懂人事.
column4: 他在公司的人事部门工作。
column5: 他在公司的人事部門工作。
column6: Tā zài gōngsī de rénshì bùmén gōngzuò.
column7: He works in the company's personnel department.
column9: In a company it is the department that handles hiring, pay and promotion, with set phrases such as 人事部門 and 人事調動. The "ways of the world" sense is rarer, as in 不懂人事.

column3: A scientific and medical word, the body as an object of study: 人体结构, 人体模型, 对人体有害. For your own health in everyday talk, say 身体: 身体不舒服.
column6: Zhè zhǒng dōngxi duì réntǐ yǒuhài.
column7: This stuff is harmful to the human body.
column9: A scientific and medical word, the body as an object of study: 人體結構, 人體模型, 對人體有害. For your own health in everyday talk, say 身體: 身體不舒服.

column3: It stands for what the public feels, never one person's heart (that is 心 or 内心): 得人心 wins support, 人心惶惶 means people are in a panic, and 人心不古 laments that people have changed for the worse.
column6: Zhège zhèngcè hěn dé rénxīn.
column7: This policy is popular with the people.
column9: It stands for what the public feels, never one person's heart (that is 心 or 內心): 得人心 wins support, 人心惶惶 means people are in a panic, and 人心不古 laments that people have changed for the worse.

column3: Mostly in questions and negatives, about whether you can bring yourself to do something hard to someone: 我不忍心拒绝他 "I can't bring myself to refuse him", 你怎么忍心? "how could you?".
column4: 我不忍心看他这么辛苦。
column5: 我不忍心看他這麼辛苦。
column6: Wǒ bù rěnxīn kàn tā zhème xīnkǔ.
column7: I can't bear to see him work so hard.
column9: Mostly in questions and negatives, about whether you can bring yourself to do something hard to someone: 我不忍心拒絕他 "I can't bring myself to refuse him", 你怎麼忍心? "how could you?".

column3: Said of someone who does what they like and won't listen to others, often a child or a favored person: 任性的孩子. It can be a gentle, even fond complaint, not always a harsh one.
column6: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù hěn rènxìng.
column7: She has been willful since she was small.
column9: Said of someone who does what they like and won't listen to others, often a child or a favored person: 任性的孩子. It can be a gentle, even fond complaint, not always a harsh one.

column3: The paved strip beside a road: 走人行道, 人行道上停满了车. The road itself is 马路, and the place where walkers cross is 斑马线 (crosswalk).
column4: 请走人行道，不要走马路。
column5: 請走人行道，不要走馬路。
column6: Qǐng zǒu rénxíngdào, bù yào zǒu mǎlù.
column7: Please use the sidewalk, don't walk on the road.
column9: The paved strip beside a road: 走人行道, 人行道上停滿了車. The road itself is 馬路, and the place where walkers cross is 斑馬線 (crosswalk).

column3: Looks ahead to an unspecified time, a little formal: 日后再说 "let's deal with it later", 日后有机会. It is not for tomorrow or next week, and it goes at the start of a clause or before the verb.
column4: 日后有机会，我们再一起去。
column5: 日後有機會，我們再一起去。
column6: Rìhòu yǒu jīhuì, wǒmen zài yīqǐ qù.
column7: If there's a chance later on, let's go together again.
column9: Looks ahead to an unspecified time, a little formal: 日後再說 "let's deal with it later", 日後有機會. It is not for tomorrow or next week, and it goes at the start of a clause or before the verb.

column4: 我去超市买一些日用品。
column5: 我去超市買一些日用品。
column6: Wǒ qù chāoshì mǎi yīxiē rìyòngpǐn.
column7: I'm going to the supermarket to buy some household items.

column3: Rare on its own in speech, but common in compounds: 容易 "easy" (the one to learn first, with 不容易), 容纳 "have room for", 容忍 "tolerate", and "appearance" in 笑容, 美容 and 面容.
column4: 这个房间可以容纳五十个人。
column5: 這個房間可以容納五十個人。
column6: Zhège fángjiān kěyǐ róng nà wǔshí ge rén.
column7: This room can hold fifty people.
column9: Rare on its own in speech, but common in compounds: 容易 "easy" (the one to learn first, with 不容易), 容納 "have room for", 容忍 "tolerate", and "appearance" in 笑容, 美容 and 面容.

column3: For ice, snow and other solids that turn liquid with heat, and for feelings too. For chocolate or ice cream people often just say 化了. Of the melting characters, 融 is for melting at normal temperature, 熔 for smelting at a high temperature and 溶 for dissolving in a liquid.
column4: 太阳出来后，雪就融化了。
column5: 太陽出來後，雪就融化了。
column6: Tàiyáng chūlái hòu, xuě jiù rónghuà le.
column7: After the sun came out, the snow melted.
column9: For ice, snow and other solids that turn liquid with heat, and for feelings too. For chocolate or ice cream people often just say 化了. Of the melting characters, 融 is for melting at normal temperature, 熔 for smelting at a high temperature and 溶 for dissolving in a liquid.

column3: Polite and formal, for guests, introductions and speeches: 很荣幸认识您. The usual reply is 这是我的荣幸 "the honor is mine".
column6: Hěn róngxìng rènshi nín.
column7: I am honored to meet you.
column9: Polite and formal, for guests, introductions and speeches: 很榮幸認識您. The usual reply is 這是我的榮幸 "the honor is mine".

column3: A bound form in compounds: 入口 "entrance", 入学, 入境, 进入, 加入, 收入. In speech people say 进 for entering (进来, 进去), and the opposite of 入口 is 出口.
column6: Rù kǒu zài dàlóu de zuǒbian.
column7: The entrance is on the left side of the building.
column9: A bound form in compounds: 入口 "entrance", 入學, 入境, 進入, 加入, 收入. In speech people say 進 for entering (進來, 進去), and the opposite of 入口 is 出口.

column3: Adds 说 to 如果 to set up a statement for argument or illustration, often followed by 那么: 如果说…那么… "if X is so, then Y". It is a bit more talk-like than plain 如果.
column4: 如果说他是天才，那么他也是最努力的天才。
column5: 如果說他是天才，那麼他也是最努力的天才。
column6: Rúguǒshuō tā shì tiāncái, nàme tā yě shì zuì nǔlì de tiāncái.
column7: If he is a genius, then he is the hardest-working genius.
column9: Adds 說 to 如果 to set up a statement for argument or illustration, often followed by 那麼: 如果說…那麼… "if X is so, then Y". It is a bit more talk-like than plain 如果.

column3: Seen at airports and borders: arrivals go to the 入境 counter, departures through 出境. Set phrases are 入境许可 and 办理入境手续. The idiom for following local customs is 入境随俗 in Taiwan and more often 入乡随俗 on the mainland.
column4: 请在这里排队办理入境手续。
column5: 請在這裡排隊辦理入境手續。
column6: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ páiduì bànlǐ rùjìng shǒuxù.
column7: Please line up here for entry procedures.
column9: Seen at airports and borders: arrivals go to the 入境 counter, departures through 出境. Set phrases are 入境許可 and 辦理入境手續. The idiom for following local customs is 入境隨俗 in Taiwan and more often 入鄉隨俗 on the mainland.

column3: It is the moment of starting at a school, with 入学考试 "entrance exam" and 入学典礼 "opening ceremony"; after that you 上学 every day. Moving on to the next level of school is 升学.
column6: Tā jīnnián jiǔyuè rùxué.
column7: He starts school this September.
column9: It is the moment of starting at a school, with 入學考試 "entrance exam" and 入學典禮 "opening ceremony"; after that you 上學 every day. Moving on to the next level of school is 升學.

column3: The verb for stuffing things into a tight space: 塞进 "stuff into", 塞满 "stuff full", 塞住 "plug up", and a stopper is 塞子.
column6: Tā bǎ shū sāi jìn le bèibāo.
column7: He stuffed the books into his backpack.
column9: The verb for stuffing things into a tight space: 塞進 "stuff into", 塞滿 "stuff full", 塞住 "plug up", and a stopper is 塞子.

column3: Taiwan's usual word for a traffic jam, where the mainland more often says 堵车. 路上塞车 is the classic excuse for being late.
column4: 路上塞车，我可能会晚到。
column5: 路上塞車，我可能會晚到。
column6: Lùshàng sāichē, wǒ kěnéng huì wǎn dào.
column7: There's a traffic jam, so I may be late.
column9: Taiwan's usual word for a traffic jam, where the mainland more often says 堵車. 路上塞車 is the classic excuse for being late.

column3: It is specifically a footrace: 百米赛跑, 跟他赛跑 "race him", a staple of a child's sports day. Other contests use 比赛, and a car race is 赛车.
column4: 我们来赛跑，看谁跑得快。
column5: 我們來賽跑，看誰跑得快。
column6: Wǒmen lái sàipǎo, kàn shéi pǎo de kuài.
column7: Let's race and see who is faster.
column9: It is specifically a footrace: 百米賽跑, 跟他賽跑 "race him", a staple of a child's sports day. Other contests use 比賽, and a car race is 賽車.

column3: Formal, for something abstract that one had and cannot easily get back: 丧失信心, 丧失能力, 丧失机会. For an object you lost, say 丢 or 丢失.
column6: Tā sàngshī le xìnxīn.
column7: He lost his confidence.
column9: Formal, for something abstract that one had and cannot easily get back: 喪失信心, 喪失能力, 喪失機會. For an object you lost, say 丟 or 丟失.

column3: 形 makes a shape word, as in 正方形 "square", 长方形 "rectangle" and 圆形 "circle". In math class you also meet 等边三角形 "equilateral triangle".
column6: Zhège pánzi shì sānjiǎoxíng de.
column7: This plate is triangular.
column9: 形 makes a shape word, as in 正方形 "square", 長方形 "rectangle" and 圓形 "circle". In math class you also meet 等邊三角形 "equilateral triangle".

column3: The classifier for ships, boats and spacecraft: 一艘船, 两艘军舰, 三艘游艇, 一艘宇宙飞船.
column6: Gǎngkǒu tíng zhe sān sōu dà chuán.
column7: Three large ships are docked in the harbor.
column9: The classifier for ships, boats and spacecraft: 一艘船, 兩艘軍艦, 三艘遊艇, 一艘宇宙飛船.

column3: A strong word, used in warnings and rules about content: 禁止色情, 色情网站, 色情电影. It is never used for romance, which is 爱情.
column4: 网站上不能出现色情内容。
column5: 網站上不能出現色情內容。
column6: Wǎngzhàn shàng bù néng chūxiàn sèqíng nèiróng.
column7: Pornographic content must not appear on the site.
column9: A strong word, used in warnings and rules about content: 禁止色情, 色情網站, 色情電影. It is never used for romance, which is 愛情.

column3: Beyond "sand" itself, it shows up in 沙滩, 沙漠 and 沙发 (a sound loan from "sofa"), and as "hoarse" in 声音沙哑. On its own it is rarer in speech than 沙子.
column6: Xiézi lǐ jìn le shā zi.
column7: Sand got into my shoes.
column9: Beyond "sand" itself, it shows up in 沙灘, 沙漠 and 沙發 (a sound loan from "sofa"), and as "hoarse" in 聲音沙啞. On its own it is rarer in speech than 沙子.

column3: The buyer pushing the price down, as in 杀价杀得很凶; 讨价还价 is the whole back-and-forth. 杀价 is the usual word in Taiwan, and on the mainland 砍价 is more common. It works at markets and night markets, not in shops with fixed prices.
column4: 在夜市买东西可以杀价。
column5: 在夜市買東西可以殺價。
column6: Zài yèshì mǎi dōngxi kěyǐ shājià.
column7: You can haggle when you buy things at a night market.
column9: The buyer pushing the price down, as in 殺價殺得很兇; 討價還價 is the whole back-and-forth. 殺價 is the usual word in Taiwan, and on the mainland 砍價 is more common. It works at markets and night markets, not in shops with fixed prices.

column6: Táiwān yǒu hěn duō shāndì.
column7: Taiwan has a lot of mountainous land.

column3: Spoken, for a problem that makes you think hard or worry: 真伤脑筋 "what a headache", 这件事很伤脑筋. 脑筋 by itself is how you think, as in 动脑筋 "use your head".
column6: Zhège wèntí zhēn shāngnǎojīn.
column7: This problem is a real headache.
column9: Spoken, for a problem that makes you think hard or worry: 真傷腦筋 "what a headache", 這件事很傷腦筋. 腦筋 by itself is how you think, as in 動腦筋 "use your head".

column3: A new product goes on sale (新手机上市), and seasonal produce is now in the shops (荔枝上市了). For a company, going public on the stock exchange is also 上市; in Taiwan a smaller one on the over-the-counter market is 上柜.
column6: Xīn shǒujī xià ge yuè shàngshì.
column7: The new phone comes out next month.
column9: A new product goes on sale (新手機上市), and seasonal produce is now in the shops (荔枝上市了). For a company, going public on the stock exchange is also 上市; in Taiwan a smaller one on the over-the-counter market is 上櫃.

column3: A formal written word for reports, notices and exams, pointing back to something said earlier in the same text: 上述原因, 上述内容. Aloud people say 上面说的 or 刚才说的.
column4: 由于上述原因，会议改期了。
column5: 由於上述原因，會議改期了。
column6: Yóuyú shàngshù yuányīn, huìyì gǎiqī le.
column7: For the reasons given above, the meeting has been put off.
column9: A formal written word for reports, notices and exams, pointing back to something said earlier in the same text: 上述原因, 上述內容. Aloud people say 上面說的 or 剛才說的.

column3: The everyday use is going up on stage: 上台表演, 上台领奖. Its opposite 下台 is leaving the stage, or stepping down from power; both are used of politicians.
column4: 他上台领奖的时候很紧张。
column5: 他上台領獎的時候很緊張。
column6: Tā shàngtái lǐng jiǎng de shíhou hěn jǐnzhāng.
column7: He was nervous when he went up to receive the prize.
column9: The everyday use is going up on stage: 上台表演, 上台領獎. Its opposite 下臺 is leaving the stage, or stepping down from power; both are used of politicians.

column3: The ending is neutral. Spoken, for the top of something (桌子上头) and for the people in charge (上头交代的 "what the boss told us"). The plainer word for "on top" is 上面.
column4: 上头的人要我们明天交报告。
column5: 上頭的人要我們明天交報告。
column6: Shàngtou de rén yào wǒmen míngtiān jiāo bàogào.
column7: The people above want us to hand in the report tomorrow.
column9: The ending is neutral. Spoken, for the top of something (桌子上頭) and for the people in charge (上頭交代的 "what the boss told us"). The plainer word for "on top" is 上面.

column3: The opposite is 下游. In industry 上游 means the makers of raw materials and 下游 the makers and sellers of end products, and 力争上游 means to strive for the top.
column4: 这条河的上游有一座水库。
column5: 這條河的上游有一座水庫。
column6: Zhè tiáo hé de shàngyóu yǒu yī zuò shuǐkù.
column7: There is a reservoir on the upper reaches of this river.
column9: The opposite is 下游. In industry 上游 means the makers of raw materials and 下游 the makers and sellers of end products, and 力爭上游 means to strive for the top.

column3: A girl of roughly 12 to 20, in a slightly literary tone that suits stories and songs: 少女时代 "girlhood", 一位少女. In plain speech say 女孩.
column6: Nàge shàonǚ zài hébiān chànggē.
column7: That girl is singing by the river.
column9: A girl of roughly 12 to 20, in a slightly literary tone that suits stories and songs: 少女時代 "girlhood", 一位少女. In plain speech say 女孩.

column3: The sand itself, where 海边 is the general word for the seaside: 去沙滩玩, 沙滩排球, 沙滩裤 "board shorts". 滩 also counts a puddle of liquid, as in 一滩水.
column6: Wǒmen zhōumò qù shātān wán.
column7: We're going to the beach on the weekend.
column9: The sand itself, where 海邊 is the general word for the seaside: 去沙灘玩, 沙灘排球, 沙灘褲 "board shorts". 灘 also counts a puddle of liquid, as in 一灘水.

column3: Meeting people in a polite or professional way: 社交活动, 社交能力, 不擅长社交 "bad at socializing". For social media the mainland says 社交软件 and 社交媒体, while Taiwan usually says 社群软体 and 社群媒体.
column6: Tā bù tài huì shèjiāo.
column7: He is not very good at socializing.
column9: Meeting people in a polite or professional way: 社交活動, 社交能力, 不擅長社交 "bad at socializing". For social media the mainland says 社交軟件 and 社交媒體, while Taiwan usually says 社群軟體 and 社群媒體.

column3: An authority or committee (审查委员会) checks something against the rules before it can go ahead: 资格审查, 审查申请, 电影审查. For an everyday check of something you use, say 检查.
column4: 评审会正在审查这份申请。
column5: 評審會正在審查這份申請。
column6: Píngshěnhuì zhèngzài shěnchá zhè fèn shēnqǐng.
column7: The panel is reviewing this application.
column9: An authority or committee (審查委員會) checks something against the rules before it can go ahead: 資格審查, 審查申請, 電影審查. For an everyday check of something you use, say 檢查.

column3: Used on forms and in law: 以学生的身分 "as a student", 身分地位 "social standing". Taiwan writes 身分 and the mainland 身份; both are said the same way.
column6: Qǐng chūshì nǐ de shēnfèn zhèngmíng.
column7: Please show proof of your identity.
column9: Used on forms and in law: 以學生的身分 "as a student", 身分地位 "social standing". Taiwan writes 身分 and the mainland 身份; both are said the same way.

column3: The national ID card citizens carry: 带身分证, 办身分证. In Taiwan the number starts with a letter and is the 身分证字号; on the mainland it is the 身份证号码.
column6: Chūmén bié wàng le dài shēnfènzhèng.
column7: Don't forget to take your ID card when you go out.
column9: The national ID card citizens carry: 帶身分證, 辦身分證. In Taiwan the number starts with a letter and is the 身分證字號; on the mainland it is the 身份證號碼.

column3: A bound form: speech says 绳子, and 绳 turns up in compounds such as 跳绳 "jump rope", 麻绳 "hemp rope" and 绳索.
column4: 他用一条粗绳子把箱子绑好。
column5: 他用一條粗繩子把箱子綁好。
column6: Tā yòng yī tiáo cū shéng zi bǎ xiāngzi bǎng hǎo.
column7: He tied up the box with a thick rope.
column9: A bound form: speech says 繩子, and 繩 turns up in compounds such as 跳繩 "jump rope", 麻繩 "hemp rope" and 繩索.

column3: The everyday word for anything from a thin string to a thick rope, counted with 条 or 根: 用绳子绑 "tie with a rope", 跳绳 "jump rope".
column6: Qǐng gěi wǒ yī tiáo shéngzi.
column7: Please give me a rope.
column9: The everyday word for anything from a thin string to a thick rope, counted with 條 or 根: 用繩子綁 "tie with a rope", 跳繩 "jump rope".

column3: It comes in the second part of a sentence and names the trouble you save yourself: 早点出门，省得迟到. Close to 免得, but 省得 stresses saving trouble, time or money.
column4: 你先打个电话，省得白跑一趟。
column5: 你先打個電話，省得白跑一趟。
column6: Nǐ xiān dǎ ge diànhuà, shěngde bái pǎo yī tàng.
column7: Call first, so you don't make the trip for nothing.
column9: It comes in the second part of a sentence and names the trouble you save yourself: 早點出門，省得遲到. Close to 免得, but 省得 stresses saving trouble, time or money.

column3: Also "level up" in a game, and 升级版 is an upgraded version of a product. An upgrade to a better class on a flight is 升等 in Taiwan and 升舱 on the mainland.
column6: Shǒujī xūyào shēngjí xìtǒng.
column7: The phone needs a system upgrade.
column9: Also "level up" in a game, and 升級版 is an upgraded version of a product. An upgrade to a better class on a flight is 升等 in Taiwan and 升艙 on the mainland.

column3: To say yours, use 属: 我属兔. Asking is 你属什么? or 你的生肖是什么?. The twelve animals run 鼠牛虎兔龙蛇马羊猴鸡狗猪.
column6: Nǐ de shēngxiào shì shénme?
column7: What is your zodiac animal?
column9: To say yours, use 屬: 我屬兔. Asking is 你屬什麼? or 你的生肖是什麼?. The twelve animals run 鼠牛虎兔龍蛇馬羊猴雞狗豬.

column3: A familiar worry: going from junior high to senior high, or senior high to university. 升学考试, 升学压力, 升学率. Going up a grade within a school is 升级, not this.
column4: 很多学生有升学的压力。
column5: 很多學生有升學的壓力。
column6: Hěn duō xuéshēng yǒu shēngxué de yālì.
column7: Many students feel the pressure of getting into the next school.
column9: A familiar worry: going from junior high to senior high, or senior high to university. 升學考試, 升學壓力, 升學率. Going up a grade within a school is 升級, not this.

column3: Praise or mockery depending on tone and context: a sharp look (穿上制服很神气), or showing off (别神气了 "don't get so full of yourself", 神气活现 "swaggering").
column4: 他穿上制服，看起来很神气。
column5: 他穿上制服，看起來很神氣。
column6: Tā chuān shàng zhìfú, kàn qǐlái hěn shénqì.
column7: In his uniform he looks very smart.
column9: Praise or mockery depending on tone and context: a sharp look (穿上制服很神氣), or showing off (別神氣了 "don't get so full of yourself", 神氣活現 "swaggering").

column3: A pair of opposites that makes a noun for a degree, like 大小 "size": 水的深浅, 颜色的深浅 "shade". With no measurement, 说话没有深浅 means having no sense of limits.
column4: 下水之前先试一试水的深浅。
column5: 下水之前先試一試水的深淺。
column6: Xià shuǐ zhīqián xiān shì yī shì shuǐ de shēnqiǎn.
column7: Test how deep the water is before you get in.
column9: A pair of opposites that makes a noun for a degree, like 大小 "size": 水的深淺, 顏色的深淺 "shade". With no measurement, 說話沒有深淺 means having no sense of limits.

column3: Lofty language for a duty, a place, a mission or a right: 神圣的使命, 神圣的地方, 神圣不可侵犯 "sacred and inviolable".
column4: 保护国家是神圣的责任。
column5: 保護國家是神聖的責任。
column6: Bǎohù guójiā shì shénshèng de zérèn.
column7: Defending the country is a sacred duty.
column9: Lofty language for a duty, a place, a mission or a right: 神圣的使命, 神圣的地方, 神圣不可侵犯 "sacred and inviolable".

column3: A verb with its object inside, so it can split: 伸出手, 他伸了伸手. Figurative uses are 伸手要钱 "always asking for money" and 伸手不见五指 "pitch dark".
column6: Tā shēnshǒu ná zhuō shàng de bēizi.
column7: He reached for the cup on the table.
column9: A verb with its object inside, so it can split: 伸出手, 他伸了伸手. Figurative uses are 伸手要錢 "always asking for money" and 伸手不見五指 "pitch dark".

column3: Beyond the legends (the Eight Immortals are 八仙), it is used for a carefree person or life: 像神仙一样, 过神仙日子 "live a life of ease".
column4: 这里的风景像神仙住的地方。
column5: 這裡的風景像神仙住的地方。
column6: Zhèlǐ de fēngjǐng xiàng shénxiān zhù de dìfang.
column7: The scenery here is like the home of immortals.
column9: Beyond the legends (the Eight Immortals are 八仙), it is used for a carefree person or life: 像神仙一樣, 過神仙日子 "live a life of ease".

column3: The hours well after dark, around or past midnight, in speech and writing: 深夜十二点, 在深夜工作. 半夜 is the casual word for the middle of the night: 半夜醒来.
column6: Tā chángcháng gōngzuò dào shēnyè.
column7: He often works until late at night.
column9: The hours well after dark, around or past midnight, in speech and writing: 深夜十二點, 在深夜工作. 半夜 is the casual word for the middle of the night: 半夜醒來.

column3: Fits a weighty decision or matter, as in 慎重考虑 and 慎重处理, and is a bit formal. 小心 is for watching your step; 慎重 is for handling something important with thought.
column4: 结婚是大事，要慎重考虑。
column5: 結婚是大事，要慎重考慮。
column6: Jiéhūn shì dàshì, yào shènzhòng kǎolǜ.
column7: Marriage is a big matter, so think carefully.
column9: Fits a weighty decision or matter, as in 慎重考慮 and 慎重處理, and is a bit formal. 小心 is for watching your step; 慎重 is for handling something important with thought.

column3: Goes with verbs such as 伸 and 咬: 伸出舌头, 咬到舌头. 舌头打结 describes stumbling over your words, much like English tongue-tied.
column6: Wǒ bù xiǎoxīn yǎo dào le shétou.
column7: I accidentally bit my tongue.
column9: Goes with verbs such as 伸 and 咬: 伸出舌頭, 咬到舌頭. 舌頭打結 describes stumbling over your words, much like English tongue-tied.

column3: A bound form that works inside compounds such as 舌尖, 口舌 and 舌苔; for the organ itself, speech says 舌头. It began as a picture of a snake's tongue coming up out of a mouth.
column6: Tā de shé jiān bèi tàngshāng le.
column7: The tip of his tongue was scalded.
column9: A bound form that works inside compounds such as 舌尖, 口舌 and 舌苔; for the organ itself, speech says 舌頭. It began as a picture of a snake's tongue coming up out of a mouth.

column3: The usual word for student clubs and extracurricular groups: 参加社团, 社团活动. Individual clubs often end in 社, as in 吉他社 and 摄影社. It also names registered civic organizations.
column4: 大学生活里，他加入了摄影社团。
column5: 大學生活裡，他加入了攝影社團。
column6: Dàxué shēnghuó lǐ, tā jiārù le shèyǐng shètuán.
column7: At university he joined the photography club.
column9: The usual word for student clubs and extracurricular groups: 參加社團, 社團活動. Individual clubs often end in 社, as in 吉他社 and 攝影社. It also names registered civic organizations.

column3: Seldom stands alone in speech; it works inside words such as 世界, 世纪, 世代 and 去世. One account ties it to the leaves of a tree: successive foliages of a tree became generations.
column4: 二十一世纪是网路的世纪。
column5: 二十一世紀是網路的世紀。
column6: Èrshíyī shì jì shì wǎnglù de shì jì.
column7: The twenty-first century is the century of the internet.
column9: Seldom stands alone in speech; it works inside words such as 世界, 世紀, 世代 and 去世. One account ties it to the leaves of a tree: successive foliages of a tree became generations.

column3: Mostly bound in compounds such as 视力, 电视, 重视 and 无视. On its own as a verb it is literary, so speech uses 看 instead.
column6: Tā de shì lì yuèláiyuè chà.
column7: His eyesight is getting worse and worse.
column9: Mostly bound in compounds such as 視力, 電視, 重視 and 無視. On its own as a verb it is literary, so speech uses 看 instead.

column3: Formal and common for what fits the situation. It works before a noun (适当的方法, 适当的时候) and as an adverb (适当休息, 适当地). 合适 is the everyday word for something suiting a person.
column6: Yùndòng yào shìdàng, bù yào tài lèi.
column7: Exercise in moderation and don't get too tired.
column9: Formal and common for what fits the situation. It works before a noun (適當的方法, 適當的時候) and as an adverb (適當休息, 適當地). 合適 is the everyday word for something suiting a person.

column3: Fits things you had and no longer have, especially abstract ones: 失掉信心, 失掉机会, 失掉工作. For a physical object such as keys, 丢 is the usual verb.
column6: Tā shīdiào le yī cì hǎo jīhuì.
column7: He missed a good chance.
column9: Fits things you had and no longer have, especially abstract ones: 失掉信心, 失掉機會, 失掉工作. For a physical object such as keys, 丟 is the usual verb.

column3: Two uses: judging morality (明辨是非, 是非不分) and gossip or trouble talked about behind people's backs (惹是非, 搬弄是非).
column6: Háizi yào xuéhuì fēnbiàn shìfēi.
column7: Children need to learn to tell right from wrong.
column9: Two uses: judging morality (明辨是非, 是非不分) and gossip or trouble talked about behind people's backs (惹是非, 搬弄是非).

column3: A respectful address for a skilled worker such as a driver, repairman or cook, for a monk or nun, and for a craft teacher: 拜师父 means to become an apprentice. On the mainland it is more often written 师傅.
column6: Shīfu jiāo tā zěnme zuò mùgōng.
column7: The master teaches him how to do woodwork.
column9: A respectful address for a skilled worker such as a driver, repairman or cook, for a monk or nun, and for a craft teacher: 拜師父 means to become an apprentice. On the mainland it is more often written 師傅.

column3: The word on site barriers and signs: 施工中, 道路施工. It is the doing of the work by a crew; 工程 is the project itself.
column6: Qiánmiàn zài shīgōng, qǐng ràolù.
column7: There are roadworks ahead, please take another road.
column9: The word on site barriers and signs: 施工中, 道路施工. It is the doing of the work by a crew; 工程 is the project itself.

column3: Goes before an institution run by a city: 市立图书馆, 市立医院, 市立大学. Its siblings are 国立 for national, 县立 for county, and 私立 for private.
column6: Zhè shì yī suǒ shìlì túshūguǎn.
column7: This is a municipal library.
column9: Goes before an institution run by a city: 市立圖書館, 市立醫院, 市立大學. Its siblings are 國立 for national, 縣立 for county, and 私立 for private.

column4: 他最近压力大，常常失眠。
column5: 他最近壓力大，常常失眠。
column6: Tā zuìjìn yālì dà, chángcháng shīmián.
column7: He is under a lot of stress lately and often can't sleep.

column3: People of a city as a community, as in 台北市民 and in city notices: 市民大会, 市民热线. 公民 is a citizen of a country, and 居民 is simply a resident.
column4: 市政府请市民节约用水。
column5: 市政府請市民節約用水。
column6: Shìzhèngfǔ qǐng shìmín jiéyuē yòngshuǐ.
column7: The city government asks residents to save water.
column9: People of a city as a community, as in 臺北市民 and in city notices: 市民大會, 市民熱線. 公民 is a citizen of a country, and 居民 is simply a resident.

column3: A respectful address for the wife of your teacher or master: 师母好. It is used for the wife of any of your teachers, in school as well as in crafts and martial arts.
column4: 每次去老师家，师母都准备很多好吃的。
column5: 每次去老師家，師母都準備很多好吃的。
column6: Měi cì qù lǎoshī jiā, shīmǔ dōu zhǔnbèi hěn duō hǎochī de.
column7: Every time we visit the teacher's home, his wife has prepared lots of good food.
column9: A respectful address for the wife of your teacher or master: 師母好. It is used for the wife of any of your teachers, in school as well as in crafts and martial arts.

column3: A stretch of time with its own character, from a few years to decades: 学生时期, 战争时期, 特殊时期. For a point in time, say 时候.
column4: 这是我人生最快乐的时期。
column5: 這是我人生最快樂的時期。
column6: Zhè shì wǒ rénshēng zuì kuàilè de shíqī.
column7: This is the happiest period of my life.
column9: A stretch of time with its own character, from a few years to decades: 學生時期, 戰爭時期, 特殊時期. For a point in time, say 時候.

column3: A written, emphatic way to say all the time, as in 时时提醒 and the set phrase 时时刻刻. In speech 常常 or 一直 sounds more natural.
column6: Wǒmen yào shíshí zhùyì ānquán.
column7: We must pay attention to safety at all times.
column9: A written, emphatic way to say all the time, as in 時時提醒 and the set phrase 時時刻刻. In speech 常常 or 一直 sounds more natural.

column3: Protesting by marching or gathering: 示威游行, 示威抗议. News reports use it, and it can also describe a display of force.
column6: Mínzhòng zài jiētóu shìwēi.
column7: People are demonstrating in the street.
column9: Protesting by marching or gathering: 示威遊行, 示威抗議. News reports use it, and it can also describe a display of force.

column3: The look or cut of clothes, furniture or buildings: 式样新颖, 各种式样. In shops 款式 is the more common word, and 式样 is a bit more formal.
column4: 这家店的鞋子式样很多。
column5: 這家店的鞋子式樣很多。
column6: Zhè jiā diàn de xiézi shìyàng hěn duō.
column7: This shop has shoes in many styles.
column9: The look or cut of clothes, furniture or buildings: 式樣新穎, 各種式樣. In shops 款式 is the more common word, and 式樣 is a bit more formal.

column3: Both the literal view (视野开阔, 窗外的视野) and a mental outlook (国际视野). Travel and study are said to 开阔 or 扩大 it.
column4: 出国旅行可以开阔视野。
column5: 出國旅行可以開闊視野。
