column6: Chūguó lǚxíng kěyǐ kāikuò shìyě.
column7: Traveling abroad can broaden your horizons.
column9: Both the literal view (視野開闊, 窗外的視野) and a mental outlook (國際視野). Travel and study are said to 開闊 or 擴大 it.

column3: A written, bound form for selling, found in 出售, 零售, 售价, 售票处, and 售完 on signs. In speech the verb is 卖.
column6: Zhè běn shū yǐjīng shòu wán le.
column7: This book is sold out.
column9: A written, bound form for selling, found in 出售, 零售, 售價, 售票處, and 售完 on signs. In speech the verb is 賣.

column3: The measure word is 支 or 把, and 电筒 is a common short form. The batteries die as 没电了.
column6: Tíngdiàn le, kuài ná shǒudiàntǒng lái.
column7: The power's out, quickly bring the flashlight.
column9: The measure word is 支 or 把, and 電筒 is a common short form. The batteries die as 沒電了.

column3: Proof that money or goods were received, which you ask for (开收据) and keep (保留收据), often for returns or expenses. 发票 is the official tax invoice, a different document.
column6: Qǐng bǎoliú shōujù, yǐbiàn tuìhuò.
column7: Please keep the receipt in case you return the goods.
column9: Proof that money or goods were received, which you ask for (開收據) and keep (保留收據), often for returns or expenses. 發票 is the official tax invoice, a different document.

column3: Covers people, animals and things that run for a while: 平均寿命, 电池的寿命. It pairs with 长 and 短, as in 寿命很长.
column4: 台湾人的平均寿命越来越长。
column5: 台灣人的平均壽命越來越長。
column6: Táiwānrén de píngjūn shòumìng yuèláiyuè cháng.
column7: The average life span of people in Taiwan keeps getting longer.
column9: Covers people, animals and things that run for a while: 平均壽命, 電池的壽命. It pairs with 長 and 短, as in 壽命很長.

column3: Mostly met in compounds for a number: 数字, 数量, 人数, 数学. Before a number word it means several, as in 数十年.
column6: Zhèlǐ de xuéshēng shù liàng bù duō.
column7: There are not many students here.
column9: Mostly met in compounds for a number: 數字, 數量, 人數, 數學. Before a number word it means several, as in 數十年.

column3: Covers both rats and mice in English, and the measure word is 只. 老 is only a prefix here, with no sense of old; the zodiac animal is 鼠 alone.
column6: Chúfáng lǐ yǒu yī zhī lǎoshǔ.
column7: There is a mouse in the kitchen.
column9: Covers both rats and mice in English, and the measure word is 只. 老 is only a prefix here, with no sense of old; the zodiac animal is 鼠 alone.

column3: Spoken, with a flavor of playing or putting on a show, often mildly critical: 耍帅, 耍宝, 耍脾气, 耍花招.
column6: Tā yòu zài shuǎ shuài le.
column7: He is showing off again.
column9: Spoken, with a flavor of playing or putting on a show, often mildly critical: 耍帥, 耍寶, 耍脾氣, 耍花招.

column3: Spoken and forceful: you get rid of something with a swing. 甩手 swings the arms, 甩掉 shakes something off, and 被甩了 means got dumped by a partner.
column4: 他把头发一甩，转身走了。
column5: 他把頭髮一甩，轉身走了。
column6: Tā bǎ tóufa yī shuǎi, zhuǎnshēn zǒu le.
column7: He tossed his hair and turned and left.
column9: Spoken and forceful: you get rid of something with a swing. 甩手 swings the arms, 甩掉 shakes something off, and 被甩了 means got dumped by a partner.

column3: For weakening over time, in an economy (经济衰退) or in a body or mind (记忆力衰退, 体力衰退). It describes a gradual slide, with 进步 as its opposite.
column6: Rén lǎo le, jìyìlì huì shuāituì.
column7: When people get old their memory declines.
column9: For weakening over time, in an economy (經濟衰退) or in a body or mind (記憶力衰退, 體力衰退). It describes a gradual slide, with 進步 as its opposite.

column3: Counted with 对: 一对双胞胎. Types have their own words: 龙凤胎 is a boy and a girl, and 同卵双胞胎 are identical twins.
column4: 他们是双胞胎，长得一模一样。
column5: 他們是雙胞胎，長得一模一樣。
column6: Tāmen shì shuāngbāotāi, zhǎng de yīmúyīyàng.
column7: They are twins and look exactly alike.
column9: Counted with 對: 一對雙胞胎. Types have their own words: 龍鳳胎 is a boy and a girl, and 同卵雙胞胎 are identical twins.

column3: Both a verb (疏忽了细节) and a noun (一时疏忽), for a small, unintended lapse in attention. It names the slip itself, while 马虎 describes a careless habit.
column4: 因为一时疏忽，他忘了锁门。
column5: 因為一時疏忽，他忘了鎖門。
column6: Yīnwèi yīshí shūhu, tā wàng le suǒ mén.
column7: Through a moment of carelessness he forgot to lock the door.
column9: Both a verb (疏忽了細節) and a noun (一時疏忽), for a small, unintended lapse in attention. It names the slip itself, while 馬虎 describes a careless habit.

column3: Builds many words with a verb or kind: 缴税 pay tax, 报税 file a return, 退税 refund, 所得税 income tax, 营业税 business tax.
column6: Měi nián wǔyuè yào bào shuì.
column7: You file your taxes in May every year.
column9: Builds many words with a verb or kind: 繳稅 pay tax, 報稅 file a return, 退稅 refund, 所得稅 income tax, 營業稅 business tax.

column3: A formal word for books as a category, used on library and publisher notices: 阅读书籍, 各类书籍. It takes no measure word; for one book, say 一本书.
column6: Túshūguǎn lǐ yǒu gèzhǒng shūjí.
column7: The library has all kinds of books.
column9: A formal word for books as a category, used on library and publisher notices: 閱讀書籍, 各類書籍. It takes no measure word; for one book, say 一本書.

column3: As an adjective it means smooth (顺利), as a verb or preposition follow or along (顺着这条路). It also appears in 顺路, 顺便 and 孝顺. One old reading takes it as going with a river's current.
column6: Nǐ shùn zhe zhè tiáo lù yīzhí zǒu.
column7: Just follow this road straight ahead.
column9: As an adjective it means smooth (順利), as a verb or preposition follow or along (順著這條路). It also appears in 順路, 順便 and 孝順. One old reading takes it as going with a river's current.

column3: Something done in passing, with no extra effort: 顺手关门. It also describes a tool that feels handy: 这支笔很顺手. 顺便 is about the chance, 顺手 about what the hand does.
column4: 你出门时顺手把垃圾带下去。
column5: 你出門時順手把垃圾帶下去。
column6: Nǐ chūmén shí shùnshǒu bǎ lājī dài xiàqù.
column7: Take the garbage down with you as you go out.
column9: Something done in passing, with no extra effort: 順手關門. It also describes a tool that feels handy: 這支筆很順手. 順便 is about the chance, 順手 about what the hand does.

column3: The summer break as a period for programs and jobs: 暑期班, 暑期打工, 暑期活动. 暑假 is the vacation itself.
column4: 他暑期在便利商店打工。
column5: 他暑期在便利商店打工。
column6: Tā shǔqī zài biànlì shāngdiàn dǎgōng.
column7: He works part time in a convenience store during the summer break.
column9: The summer break as a period for programs and jobs: 暑期班, 暑期打工, 暑期活動. 暑假 is the vacation itself.

column3: As a measure word it counts a trace of something: 一丝希望, 一丝笑容. In cooking it means shreds, as in 肉丝, and 丝绸 is silk cloth.
column4: 我对未来还有一丝希望。
column5: 我對未來還有一絲希望。
column6: Wǒ duì wèilái hái yǒu yī sī xīwàng.
column7: I still have a thread of hope for the future.
column9: As a measure word it counts a trace of something: 一絲希望, 一絲笑容. In cooking it means shreds, as in 肉絲, and 絲綢 is silk cloth.

column3: You tear paper or cloth with your hands: 撕开, 撕掉, 撕破. The result word shows what happens: opened, torn off, or a hole.
column6: Tā bǎ xìn sī chéng le liǎng bàn.
column7: He tore the letter in two.
column9: You tear paper or cloth with your hands: 撕開, 撕掉, 撕破. The result word shows what happens: opened, torn off, or a hole.

column3: Neutral to slightly written, and comes before a verb of moving or searching: 四处走走, 四处乱跑. In speech 到处 is more common, as in 到处找.
column4: 我四处找都找不到钥匙。
column5: 我四處找都找不到鑰匙。
column6: Wǒ sìchù zhǎo dōu zhǎo bu dào yàoshi.
column7: I looked everywhere and couldn't find the key.
column9: Neutral to slightly written, and comes before a verb of moving or searching: 四處走走, 四處亂跑. In speech 到處 is more common, as in 到處找.

column3: In writing it means all around: 来自四方, 四面八方. As a shape, 四方形 is a square.
column4: 游客从四方来到这座小城。
column5: 遊客從四方來到這座小城。
column6: Yóukè cóng sìfāng lái dào zhè zuò xiǎochéng.
column7: Visitors come to this small town from all around.
column9: In writing it means all around: 來自四方, 四面八方. As a shape, 四方形 is a square.

column3: Used in 四季分明 (four distinct seasons), 一年四季 (all year) and the set phrase 四季如春, said of places with mild weather all year.
column4: 这个地方四季都很舒服。
column5: 這個地方四季都很舒服。
column6: Zhège dìfang sìjì dōu hěn shūfu.
column7: The weather in this place is pleasant all year round.
column9: Used in 四季分明 (four distinct seasons), 一年四季 (all year) and the set phrase 四季如春, said of places with mild weather all year.

column3: Goes before a school, hospital or university run by private owners: 私立学校, 私立医院. Its opposite is 公立.
column4: 她在一所私立学校教书。
column5: 她在一所私立學校教書。
column6: Tā zài yī suǒ sīlì xuéxiào jiāoshū.
column7: She teaches at a private school.
column9: Goes before a school, hospital or university run by private owners: 私立學校, 私立醫院. Its opposite is 公立.

column3: A written word for thinking that goes on for a while: 思索问题, 陷入思索, 思索良久. For everyday thinking, 想 is the word.
column4: 他低着头，思索着这个问题。
column5: 他低著頭，思索著這個問題。
column6: Tā dī zhe tóu, sīsuǒ zhe zhège wèntí.
column7: He lowered his head, pondering the problem.
column9: A written word for thinking that goes on for a while: 思索問題, 陷入思索, 思索良久. For everyday thinking, 想 is the word.

column3: Formal and news-style, for the fact of death: 死亡人数, 死亡率, 死亡证明. In speech you say 死 or the softer 去世.
column4: 这次事故造成三人死亡。
column5: 這次事故造成三人死亡。
column6: Zhè cì shìgù zàochéng sān rén sǐwáng.
column7: The accident caused three deaths.
column9: Formal and news-style, for the fact of death: 死亡人數, 死亡率, 死亡證明. In speech you say 死 or the softer 去世.

column3: For feeding and looking after animals, on a farm or at home: 饲养宠物, 饲养牛羊, and 禁止饲养 on notices. A child is 养, never 饲养.
column4: 这个农场饲养了很多牛羊。
column5: 這個農場飼養了很多牛羊。
column6: Zhège nóngchǎng sìyǎng le hěn duō niú yáng.
column7: This farm raises lots of cattle and sheep.
column9: For feeding and looking after animals, on a farm or at home: 飼養寵物, 飼養牛羊, and 禁止飼養 on notices. A child is 養, never 飼養.

column3: You go along to the station or airport as the traveler leaves: 去机场送行, 为他送行. The people who come are 送行的人.
column4: 朋友们都到机场来送行。
column5: 朋友們都到機場來送行。
column6: Péngyoumen dōu dào jīchǎng lái sòngxíng.
column7: My friends all came to the airport to see me off.
column9: You go along to the station or airport as the traveler leaves: 去機場送行, 為他送行. The people who come are 送行的人.

column3: A bound form with two sides: shared custom (风俗, 习俗) and a low or crude taste (俗气 tacky). 通俗 means popular and easy to understand.
column6: Guònián yǒu hěn duō chuántǒng xí sú.
column7: There are many traditional customs at New Year.
column9: A bound form with two sides: shared custom (風俗, 習俗) and a low or crude taste (俗氣 tacky). 通俗 means popular and easy to understand.

column3: Opens a statement drawn from counting or comparing: 算起来他是我表哥, by my reckoning he is my cousin. Common in speech.
column4: 算起来，我们认识十年了。
column5: 算起來，我們認識十年了。
column6: Suànqǐlái, wǒmen rènshi shí nián le.
column7: All told, we have known each other for ten years.
column9: Opens a statement drawn from counting or comparing: 算起來他是我表哥, by my reckoning he is my cousin. Common in speech.

column3: Puts something in a class, often with a sense of more or less: 这算是好消息, 他算是我的老师. It can also mean at last: 今天算是做完了.
column6: Zhè cì kǎoshì suànshì jiǎndān de.
column7: This exam counts as an easy one.
column9: Puts something in a class, often with a sense of more or less: 這算是好消息, 他算是我的老師. It can also mean at last: 今天算是做完了.

column3: A saying most people know and quote, introduced as 俗话说 or 俗话说得好, then something like 人多力量大. Not a literary quotation.
column6: Súhuà shuō: rén duō lìliàng dà.
column7: As the saying goes, many hands make light work.
column9: A saying most people know and quote, introduced as 俗話說 or 俗話說得好, then something like 人多力量大. Not a literary quotation.

column3: It opens a proverb or piece of folk wisdom that follows right after, as in 俗话说，一分耕耘，一分收获. Adding 得好 (俗话说得好) stresses that the saying holds true.
column4: 俗话说，早起的鸟儿有虫吃。
column5: 俗話說，早起的鳥兒有蟲吃。
column6: Súhuàshuō, zǎo qǐ de niǎor yǒu chóng chī.
column7: As the saying goes, the early bird catches the worm.
column9: It opens a proverb or piece of folk wisdom that follows right after, as in 俗話說，一分耕耘，一分收獲. Adding 得好 (俗話說得好) stresses that the saying holds true.

column3: A spoken word, mostly about the age of older people: 多大岁数 asks it politely, and 上了岁数 or 岁数大了 means getting on in years. To ask a child, say 几岁 instead.
column4: 爷爷的岁数大了，走路要小心。
column5: 爺爺的歲數大了，走路要小心。
column6: Yéye de suìshu dà le, zǒulù yào xiǎoxīn.
column7: Grandpa is getting on in years and must be careful when he walks.
column9: A spoken word, mostly about the age of older people: 多大歲數 asks it politely, and 上了歲數 or 歲數大了 means getting on in years. To ask a child, say 幾歲 instead.

column3: In Taiwan this is the everyday word for plastic, as in 塑胶袋 and 塑胶瓶; the mainland usually says 塑料 instead.
column6: Qǐng bù yào shǐyòng sùjiāo dài.
column7: Please do not use plastic bags.
column9: In Taiwan this is the everyday word for plastic, as in 塑膠袋 and 塑膠瓶; the mainland usually says 塑料 instead.

column3: The verb for things getting smaller or shorter, or a person pulling back. It is the base of many compounds: 缩小 (make smaller), 缩短 (shorten), 缩写 (an abbreviation), 退缩 (to shrink back from something).
column6: Yīfu xǐ le yǐhòu suō le.
column7: The clothes shrank after being washed.
column9: The verb for things getting smaller or shorter, or a person pulling back. It is the base of many compounds: 縮小 (make smaller), 縮短 (shorten), 縮寫 (an abbreviation), 退縮 (to shrink back from something).

column3: The everyday word for clothes that shrink in the wash. In the news it is just as common for money or size that shrinks: 预算缩水 is a budget cut down, and 薪水缩水 is a paycheck that falls.
column6: Zhè jiàn chènshān yī xǐ jiù suōshuǐ.
column7: This shirt shrinks as soon as it is washed.
column9: The everyday word for clothes that shrink in the wash. In the news it is just as common for money or size that shrinks: 預算縮水 is a budget cut down, and 薪水縮水 is a paycheck that falls.

column3: Works both as a noun and as a modifier: 素食餐厅 (a vegetarian restaurant), 素食者 (a vegetarian). To say you are one, use the verb 吃素, as in 我吃素. 纯素 is the word for vegan.
column6: Zhè jiā cāntīng tígōng sùshí.
column7: This restaurant serves vegetarian food.
column9: Works both as a noun and as a modifier: 素食餐廳 (a vegetarian restaurant), 素食者 (a vegetarian). To say you are one, use the verb 吃素, as in 我吃素. 純素 is the word for vegan.

column3: Mostly found in compounds: 踏上 (step onto, set out on), 踏步 (march in place), 踏青 (go for a walk in the countryside in spring). In Taiwan a bicycle is 脚踏车; the mainland says 自行车.
column6: Tā tà shàng le xīn de lǚchéng.
column7: He set out on a new journey.
column9: Mostly found in compounds: 踏上 (step onto, set out on), 踏步 (march in place), 踏青 (go for a walk in the countryside in spring). In Taiwan a bicycle is 腳踏車; the mainland says 自行車.

column3: Said of buildings, walls and roofs falling in: 房子塌了, and 倒塌 and 塌方 (a landslide or cave-in) are the common compounds. It also means to sag or sink, as in 塌鼻子 (a flat nose).
column6: Dìzhèn hòu, nà dòng fángzi tā le.
column7: After the earthquake, that house collapsed.
column9: Said of buildings, walls and roofs falling in: 房子塌了, and 倒塌 and 塌方 (a landslide or cave-in) are the common compounds. It also means to sag or sink, as in 塌鼻子 (a flat nose).

column3: The verb is 打: 打太极拳. It is a slow, flowing exercise that many older people practice in parks in the early morning, yet it is still a martial art, which the 拳 (fist) in its name says.
column4: 公园里有很多人在打太极拳。
column5: 公園裡有很多人在打太極拳。
column6: Gōngyuán lǐ yǒu hěn duō rén zài dǎ tàijíquán.
column7: Many people are practicing tai chi in the park.
column9: The verb is 打: 打太極拳. It is a slow, flowing exercise that many older people practice in parks in the early morning, yet it is still a martial art, which the 拳 (fist) in its name says.

column3: It reaches forward to find something out, and mostly turns up in compounds: 探路 (feel out the way), 探索 (explore), 探望 and 探病 (visit someone, a patient), 探头 (stick one's head out).
column6: Tā tàn tóu kàn le kàn chuāngwài.
column7: He stuck his head out and looked outside.
column9: It reaches forward to find something out, and mostly turns up in compounds: 探路 (feel out the way), 探索 (explore), 探望 and 探病 (visit someone, a patient), 探頭 (stick one's head out).

column3: It counts a trip there and back, and goes between the number and the verb or place: 去一趟, 白跑一趟 (make the trip for nothing). It also counts a train or bus on its run: 这趟车.
column6: Wǒ zuótiān qù le yī tàng Táizhōng.
column7: Yesterday I made a trip to Taichung.
column9: It counts a trip there and back, and goes between the number and the verb or place: 去一趟, 白跑一趟 (make the trip for nothing). It also counts a train or bus on its run: 這趟車.

column3: For something hot enough to hurt the touch: 好烫, 烫伤 (a scald or burn). It is also a verb for a hair perm (烫头发) and for ironing (烫衣服), both done with heat.
column6: Xiǎoxīn, tāng hěn tàng!
column7: Careful, the soup is scalding hot!
column9: For something hot enough to hurt the touch: 好燙, 燙傷 (a scald or burn). It is also a verb for a hair perm (燙頭髮) and for ironing (燙衣服), both done with heat.

column3: The round shape stands for family togetherness. Eating tangyuan at the winter solstice (冬至) is a custom of Taiwan and southern China; in the north people eat dumplings (饺子) then. They are usually in a sweet soup, and the verb is 吃汤圆.
column6: Dōngzhì nà tiān wǒmen chī tāngyuán.
column7: On the winter solstice we eat tangyuan.
column9: The round shape stands for family togetherness. Eating tangyuan at the winter solstice (冬至) is a custom of Taiwan and southern China; in the north people eat dumplings (餃子) then. They are usually in a sweet soup, and the verb is 吃湯圓.

column3: It is for someone who lives away from home and travels back to see family, often a long trip: 回家探亲. 探亲假 is the leave from work that is taken for it.
column6: Tā měi nián huíxiāng tànqīn yī cì.
column7: Once a year he goes back to his hometown to visit relatives.
column9: It is for someone who lives away from home and travels back to see family, often a long trip: 回家探親. 探親假 is the leave from work that is taken for it.

column3: A written, serious word for looking into a question in depth: 探讨问题, 探讨原因, 深入探讨. It turns up in papers, meetings and the news more than in casual talk.
column4: 这个问题值得我们深入探讨。
column5: 這個問題值得我們深入探討。
column6: Zhège wèntí zhíde wǒmen shēnrù tàntǎo.
column7: This question deserves deeper discussion.
column9: A written, serious word for looking into a question in depth: 探討問題, 探討原因, 深入探討. It turns up in papers, meetings and the news more than in casual talk.

column3: It stresses the space a seller holds at a market or fair: 摆摊位, 租摊位, 摊位费 (the rental fee). Night markets are full of them. 摊子 is the stall itself.
column4: 夜市里的摊位一个接一个。
column5: 夜市裡的攤位一個接一個。
column6: Yèshì lǐ de tānwèi yī ge jiē yī ge.
column7: The stalls at the night market go on one after another.
column9: It stresses the space a seller holds at a market or fair: 擺攤位, 租攤位, 攤位費 (the rental fee). Night markets are full of them. 攤子 is the stall itself.

column3: The measure word is 条: 一条毯子. The same 毯 is in 地毯 (a rug or carpet on the floor) and 毛毯 (a blanket).
column4: 天气冷，我盖了一条毯子。
column5: 天氣冷，我蓋了一條毯子。
column6: Tiānqì lěng, wǒ gài le yī tiáo tǎnzi.
column7: It was cold, so I covered myself with a blanket.
column9: The measure word is 條: 一條毯子. The same 毯 is in 地毯 (a rug or carpet on the floor) and 毛毯 (a blanket).

column3: Besides a stall (摆摊子, 小吃摊子), it means a whole setup or operation, in a figurative sense: 摊子铺得太大 is taking on too much, and 烂摊子 is a mess that someone leaves for others to clean up.
column4: 路边有一个卖水果的摊子。
column5: 路邊有一個賣水果的攤子。
column6: Lùbiān yǒu yī ge mài shuǐguǒ de tānzi.
column7: There is a fruit stall by the roadside.
column9: Besides a stall (擺攤子, 小吃攤子), it means a whole setup or operation, in a figurative sense: 攤子鋪得太大 is taking on too much, and 爛攤子 is a mess that someone leaves for others to clean up.

column3: Almost always part of a compound, so learn those: 讨厌 (to dislike, annoying), 讨论 (to discuss), 讨价还价 (to haggle), 讨饭 (to beg), 讨好 (to curry favor). 讨厌 is the first to know.
column6: Wǒ zuì tǎo yàn chī xiāngcài.
column7: I hate eating cilantro the most.
column9: Almost always part of a compound, so learn those: 討厭 (to dislike, annoying), 討論 (to discuss), 討價還價 (to haggle), 討飯 (to beg), 討好 (to curry favor). 討厭 is the first to know.

column3: A hand goes into a pocket, a bag or a hole and comes out with something: 掏口袋, 掏出钱包. 掏耳朵 is cleaning one's ears, and 掏钱 means to pay out of one's own pocket.
column6: Tā cóng kǒudài lǐ tāo chū shǒujī.
column7: He pulled his phone out of his pocket.
column9: A hand goes into a pocket, a bag or a hole and comes out with something: 掏口袋, 掏出錢包. 掏耳朵 is cleaning one's ears, and 掏錢 means to pay out of one's own pocket.

column3: It is for not facing something you should face: 逃避责任, 逃避现实, 逃避问题. The speaker often disapproves. For literally running away, the word is 逃跑.
column4: 不要逃避问题，要面对它。
column5: 不要逃避問題，要面對它。
column6: Bù yào táobì wèntí, yào miànduì tā.
column7: Don't run away from the problem, face it.
column9: It is for not facing something you should face: 逃避責任, 逃避現實, 逃避問題. The speaker often disapproves. For literally running away, the word is 逃跑.

column3: It names the material and the craft more than a single piece: 陶瓷杯, 陶瓷工艺. Single wares are 陶器 (earthenware) and 瓷器 (porcelain).
column4: 这个陶瓷杯是手工做的。
column5: 這個陶瓷杯是手工做的。
column6: Zhège táocí bēi shì shǒugōng zuò de.
column7: This ceramic cup was made by hand.
column9: It names the material and the craft more than a single piece: 陶瓷杯, 陶瓷工藝. Single wares are 陶器 (earthenware) and 瓷器 (porcelain).

column3: For a child who plays pranks and does not listen, said with a fond tone: 淘气的孩子, 淘气鬼 (little rascal). The child is not bad. 调皮 is a close word with the same feel.
column6: Zhège háizi hěn táoqì.
column7: This child is very naughty.
column9: For a child who plays pranks and does not listen, said with a fond tone: 淘氣的孩子, 淘氣鬼 (little rascal). The child is not bad. 調皮 is a close word with the same feel.

column3: Peaches stand for long life, so the birthday buns made for older people are shaped like them: 寿桃. A soft, juicy kind is 水蜜桃.
column6: Zhège táozi yòu dà yòu tián.
column7: This peach is big and sweet.
column9: Peaches stand for long life, so the birthday buns made for older people are shaped like them: 壽桃. A soft, juicy kind is 水蜜桃.

column3: It describes things as found in nature, not made or processed by people: 天然气, 天然资源, 天然食品. It is a favorite in ads for food and cosmetics. For manners that are unforced, 自然 is the word.
column6: Zhè jiā diàn zhǐ mài tiānrán shípǐn.
column7: This shop sells only natural foods.
column9: It describes things as found in nature, not made or processed by people: 天然氣, 天然資源, 天然食品. It is a favorite in ads for food and cosmetics. For manners that are unforced, 自然 is the word.

column3: A somewhat literary word for open countryside: 田野风光 is a view of fields. 田野调查 is fieldwork, the standard term among researchers such as anthropologists.
column6: Wǒmen zài tiányě lǐ sànbù.
column7: We take a walk in the fields.
column9: A somewhat literary word for open countryside: 田野風光 is a view of fields. 田野調查 is fieldwork, the standard term among researchers such as anthropologists.

column3: 天主 is the Catholic name for God and 教 means a religion. 天主教徒 is a Catholic and 天主教堂 a Catholic church. Protestant Christianity is usually 基督教.
column6: Tā jiā xìn Tiānzhǔjiào.
column7: Her family is Catholic.
column9: 天主 is the Catholic name for God and 教 means a religion. 天主教徒 is a Catholic and 天主教堂 a Catholic church. Protestant Christianity is usually 基督教.

column3: A word from history and the news: 签订条约, 和平条约, and 不平等条约 for the unequal treaties forced on China in the 1800s. The 条 is the one for clauses of a treaty, the same 条 that counts roads and pants.
column6: Liǎng guó qiāndìng le hépíng tiáoyuē.
column7: The two countries signed a peace treaty.
column9: A word from history and the news: 簽訂條約, 和平條約, and 不平等條約 for the unequal treaties forced on China in the 1800s. The 條 is the one for clauses of a treaty, the same 條 that counts roads and pants.

column3: A word of praise for someone or something that thinks ahead for you: 贴心的服务, 贴心的朋友. 真贴心 is the typical compliment for a kind gesture that you did not even ask for.
column4: 你想得真周到，太贴心了！
column5: 你想得真周到，太貼心了！
column6: Nǐ xiǎng de zhēn zhōudào, tài tiēxīn le!
column7: You thought of everything, that is so considerate!
column9: A word of praise for someone or something that thinks ahead for you: 貼心的服務, 貼心的朋友. 真貼心 is the typical compliment for a kind gesture that you did not even ask for.

column3: The verb is 量: 量体温 is taking someone's temperature, and 体温计 is the thermometer. You hear 正常体温 (normal) and 体温偏高 (a little high). A fever itself is 发烧.
column6: Nǐ de tǐwēn yǒudiǎn gāo.
column7: Your body temperature is a bit high.
column9: The verb is 量: 量體溫 is taking someone's temperature, and 體溫計 is the thermometer. You hear 正常體溫 (normal) and 體溫偏高 (a little high). A fever itself is 發燒.

column3: It moves something earlier than planned or scheduled, and works as a verb or an adverb: 提早出门, 提早到达, 提早一个小时. 提前 is much the same, a bit more written.
column4: 我们提早一个小时出发吧。
column5: 我們提早一個小時出發吧。
column6: Wǒmen tízǎo yī ge xiǎoshí chūfā ba.
column7: Let's set off an hour earlier.
column9: It moves something earlier than planned or scheduled, and works as a verb or an adverb: 提早出門, 提早到達, 提早一個小時. 提前 is much the same, a bit more written.

column3: It covers copper and its alloys, so 铜像 is a bronze statue and 铜牌 a bronze medal. Bronze the alloy is 青铜. In Taiwan 铜板 is the everyday word for any coin; the mainland says 硬币.
column6: Guǎngchǎng shàng yǒu yī zuò tóng xiàng.
column7: There is a bronze statue in the square.
column9: It covers copper and its alloys, so 銅像 is a bronze statue and 銅牌 a bronze medal. Bronze the alloy is 青銅. In Taiwan 銅板 is the everyday word for any coin; the mainland says 硬幣.

column3: Usually the last part of a word for a container: 水桶, 垃圾桶. It is also a measure word for what fills one: 一桶水, 一桶油.
column6: Qǐng bǎ lājī diū jìn lājī tǒng.
column7: Please throw the trash in the trash can.
column9: Usually the last part of a word for a container: 水桶, 垃圾桶. It is also a measure word for what fills one: 一桶水, 一桶油.

column3: A formal, warm word for the people of one's country, heard in speeches and the news: 亲爱的同胞们, 海外同胞 (compatriots abroad). It treats the nation as one family.
column4: 总统向全体同胞发表演说。
column5: 總統向全體同胞發表演說。
column6: Zǒngtǒng xiàng quántǐ tóngbāo fābiǎo yǎnshuō.
column7: The president gave a speech to all fellow citizens.
column9: A formal, warm word for the people of one's country, heard in speeches and the news: 親愛的同胞們, 海外同胞 (compatriots abroad). It treats the nation as one family.

column3: Mostly the field of communications: 通讯录 (a contacts list), 通讯地址 (mailing address), 通讯设备. A messaging app is 通讯软体 in Taiwan and 通讯软件 on the mainland. In a newspaper it can also be a news report.
column6: Qǐng tiánxiě nǐ de tōngxùn dìzhǐ.
column7: Please fill in your mailing address.
column9: Mostly the field of communications: 通訊錄 (a contacts list), 通訊地址 (mailing address), 通訊設備. A messaging app is 通訊軟體 in Taiwan and 通訊軟件 on the mainland. In a newspaper it can also be a news report.

column3: Originally a comrade, a form of address in the party, and still used that way in official mainland speech. Today it is also the usual word for gay people, especially in Taiwan, as in 同志大游行 and 同志婚姻.
column4: 台北每年都有同志大游行。
column5: 台北每年都有同志大遊行。
column6: Táiběi měi nián dōu yǒu tóngzhì dà yóuxíng.
column7: Taipei has a Pride parade every year.
column9: Originally a comrade, a form of address in the party, and still used that way in official mainland speech. Today it is also the usual word for gay people, especially in Taiwan, as in 同志大游行 and 同志婚姻.

column3: A word of history and politics that suggests power imposed from above: 统治者, 统治阶级, 长期统治. For a government's everyday running of things, 治理 or 管理 is the better word.
column4: 这个国家被一个政党统治了很多年。
column5: 這個國家被一個政黨統治了很多年。
column6: Zhège guójiā bèi yī ge zhèngdǎng tǒngzhì le hěn duō nián.
column7: This country was ruled by one party for many years.
column9: A word of history and politics that suggests power imposed from above: 統治者, 統治階級, 長期統治. For a government's everyday running of things, 治理 or 管理 is the better word.

column3: It marks the channel or means by which something happens: 透过朋友认识 (get to know through a friend), and literally 透过窗户 (through the window). In Taiwan it is the usual word for this "via"; the mainland says 通过 more often.
column4: 我是透过朋友认识他的。
column5: 我是透過朋友認識他的。
column6: Wǒ shì tòuguò péngyou rènshi tā de.
column7: I got to know him through a friend.
column9: It marks the channel or means by which something happens: 透過朋友認識 (get to know through a friend), and literally 透過窗戶 (through the window). In Taiwan it is the usual word for this "via"; the mainland says 通過 more often.

column3: A verb with its object built in, so other words go in the middle: 投了票, 投了一票, 投票给他. 投票日 is election day and 投票率 the turnout. A polling station is 投票所 in Taiwan and usually 投票站 on the mainland.
column4: 明天是投票日，你去投票了吗？
column5: 明天是投票日，你去投票了嗎？
column6: Míngtiān shì tóupiào rì, nǐ qù tóupiào le ma?
column7: Tomorrow is election day, have you voted?
column9: A verb with its object built in, so other words go in the middle: 投了票, 投了一票, 投票給他. 投票日 is election day and 投票率 the turnout. A polling station is 投票所 in Taiwan and usually 投票站 on the mainland.

column3: For war and for contests, and in speech as a joke: 我投降 means "I give up". 举手投降 is raising one's hands in surrender.
column6: Wǒ tóuxiáng, nǐ yíng le.
column7: I give up, you win.
column9: For war and for contests, and in speech as a joke: 我投降 means "I give up". 舉手投降 is raising one's hands in surrender.

column3: Also said of a tree with no leaves or a hill with no trees: 光秃秃 is completely bare. 秃头 is a bald head, and 秃子 a blunt word for a bald person. It was built as hair 毛 on a person 儿, and the hair part later changed into 禾.
column6: Dōngtiān de shù dōu tū le.
column7: The trees are all bare in winter.
column9: Also said of a tree with no leaves or a hill with no trees: 光禿禿 is completely bare. 禿頭 is a bald head, and 禿子 a blunt word for a bald person. It was built as hair 毛 on a person 兒, and the hair part later changed into 禾.

column3: What is overturned has been in force until now: a government, a theory, an earlier statement or a decision. 推翻政府, 推翻理论, 推翻原来的决定.
column4: 新的证据推翻了原来的说法。
column5: 新的證據推翻了原來的說法。
column6: Xīn de zhèngjù tuīfān le yuánlái de shuōfǎ.
column7: The new evidence overturned the earlier account.
column9: What is overturned has been in force until now: a government, a theory, an earlier statement or a decision. 推翻政府, 推翻理論, 推翻原來的決定.

column3: It is for an item that is rejected and sent back, by mail or to a shop: 退回商品, 被退回. A refund of money is 退款 or 退钱. 退回原位 is moving back to one's place. In oracle bone script 退 was a food vessel with a foot stepping down, meaning to leave the table after eating.
column6: Zhè jiàn shāngpǐn kěyǐ tuìhuí ma?
column7: Can this item be returned?
column9: It is for an item that is rejected and sent back, by mail or to a shop: 退回商品, 被退回. A refund of money is 退款 or 退錢. 退回原位 is moving back to one's place. In oracle bone script 退 was a food vessel with a foot stepping down, meaning to leave the table after eating.

column3: A formal word: the thing is a means or channel to a goal, never a literal road. 解决问题的途径, 合法途径, 各种途径. In plain speech, 办法 or 方法 is more natural for a way to do something.
column4: 这是了解中国文化的好途径。
column5: 這是了解中國文化的好途徑。
column6: Zhè shì liǎojiě Zhōngguó wénhuà de hǎo tújìng.
column7: This is a good way to learn about Chinese culture.
column9: A formal word: the thing is a means or channel to a goal, never a literal road. 解決問題的途徑, 合法途徑, 各種途徑. In plain speech, 辦法 or 方法 is more natural for a way to do something.

column3: For swallowing something whole without chewing: 吞药 (a pill), 吞口水 (saliva), 吞下去. 吞没 is to swallow up, or to embezzle. 狼吞虎咽 is wolfing down food.
column6: Tā bǎ yào tūn xià qù le.
column7: He swallowed the medicine.
column9: For swallowing something whole without chewing: 吞藥 (a pill), 吞口水 (saliva), 吞下去. 吞沒 is to swallow up, or to embezzle. 狼吞虎嚥 is wolfing down food.

column3: Things pulled along behind: 拖行李 (drag luggage), 拖车 (a tow truck), and 拖地 (mop the floor). 拖鞋 are the slippers or flip-flops worn at home. For delaying, there are 拖延 and 拖时间 (stall).
column6: Wǒ zhōumò yào zài jiā tuō dì.
column7: I will mop the floor at home this weekend.
column9: Things pulled along behind: 拖行李 (drag luggage), 拖車 (a tow truck), and 拖地 (mop the floor). 拖鞋 are the slippers or flip-flops worn at home. For delaying, there are 拖延 and 拖時間 (stall).

column3: It describes how something was handled, with no problem left: 处理得很妥当, 安排妥当 (all arranged). With 不太 it is a polite criticism: 不太妥当 is not quite proper.
column6: Zhè jiàn shì chǔlǐ de hěn tuǒdang.
column7: This matter was handled very properly.
column9: It describes how something was handled, with no problem left: 處理得很妥當, 安排妥當 (all arranged). With 不太 it is a polite criticism: 不太妥當 is not quite proper.

column3: Day care for babies and small children, before they go on to 幼儿园 (kindergarten): 送孩子去托儿所, 托儿所老师. It is the place working parents leave their children.
column4: 妈妈每天送弟弟去托儿所。
column5: 媽媽每天送弟弟去托兒所。
column6: Māma měitiān sòng dìdi qù tuō'érsuǒ.
column7: Mom takes my little brother to nursery every day.
column9: Day care for babies and small children, before they go on to 幼兒園 (kindergarten): 送孩子去托兒所, 托兒所老師. It is the place working parents leave their children.

column3: Mostly an adverb before a verb, for doing something fully and with care so that nothing goes wrong: 妥善处理, 妥善保管, 妥善安排. It sounds formal, as on notices and instructions.
column6: Qǐng tuǒshàn bǎoguǎn nǐ de zhèngjiàn.
column7: Please keep your documents safe.
column9: Mostly an adverb before a verb, for doing something fully and with care so that nothing goes wrong: 妥善處理, 妥善保管, 妥善安排. It sounds formal, as on notices and instructions.

column3: Each side gives up something to reach an agreement: 做出妥协, 达成妥协. It can sound like giving in, so it is often critical: 不要向压力妥协, 绝不妥协.
column4: 双方最后各让一步，达成妥协。
column5: 雙方最後各讓一步，達成妥協。
column6: Shuāngfāng zuìhòu gè ràng yī bù, dáchéng tuǒxié.
column7: In the end both sides gave way a little and reached a compromise.
column9: Each side gives up something to reach an agreement: 做出妥協, 達成妥協. It can sound like giving in, so it is often critical: 不要向壓力妥協, 絕不妥協.

column3: Books as a category or collection, not one particular book. It mostly modifies another noun: 图书馆, 图书证, 儿童图书. For a single book, say 一本书.
column4: 学校图书馆有很多图书。
column5: 學校圖書館有很多圖書。
column6: Xuéxiào túshūguǎn yǒu hěn duō túshū.
column7: The school library has many books.
column9: Books as a category or collection, not one particular book. It mostly modifies another noun: 圖書館, 圖書證, 兒童圖書. For a single book, say 一本書.

column3: A personal seal stamped on paperwork in place of a signature, as at a bank or post office: 盖图章. 印章 is the more general word for a seal, and an organization's official seal is 公章.
column6: Zhè fèn wénjiàn xūyào gài túzhāng.
column7: This document needs to be stamped with a seal.
column9: A personal seal stamped on paperwork in place of a signature, as at a bank or post office: 蓋圖章. 印章 is the more general word for a seal, and an organization's official seal is 公章.

column3: The object is what gets dug or scooped out: 挖洞, 挖井, 挖土. Figuratively, 挖人 is to poach an employee from another company, and 挖苦 is to make sarcastic fun of someone.
column4: 他在院子里挖了一个洞。
column5: 他在院子裡挖了一個洞。
column6: Tā zài yuànzi lǐ wā le yī ge dòng.
column7: He dug a hole in the yard.
column9: The object is what gets dug or scooped out: 挖洞, 挖井, 挖土. Figuratively, 挖人 is to poach an employee from another company, and 挖苦 is to make sarcastic fun of someone.

column3: For things that should be straight: 挂歪了 (hung crooked), 歪着头 (head tilted). For ideas and reasoning it means twisted or bad: 歪主意 is a scheme, 歪理 is faulty logic.
column6: Zhè zhāng huà guà wāi le.
column7: This picture is hanging crooked.
column9: For things that should be straight: 掛歪了 (hung crooked), 歪著頭 (head tilted). For ideas and reasoning it means twisted or bad: 歪主意 is a scheme, 歪理 is faulty logic.

column3: How a person or thing looks from the outside, often set against what is inside: 不要只看外表, 外表很漂亮. For the exterior design of an object or building, 外观 is the better word.
column6: Bù yào zhǐ kàn wàibiǎo.
column7: Don't judge only by appearances.
column9: How a person or thing looks from the outside, often set against what is inside: 不要只看外表, 外表很漂亮. For the exterior design of an object or building, 外觀 is the better word.

column3: A written, technical word for the outside of something, or "external": 外部因素, 外部环境. Its opposite is 内部. For the outside as a place in speech, say 外面.
column4: 这栋大楼的外部需要整修。
column5: 這棟大樓的外部需要整修。
column6: Zhè dòng dàlóu de wàibù xūyào zhěngxiū.
column7: The outside of this building needs repairs.
column9: A written, technical word for the outside of something, or "external": 外部因素, 外部環境. Its opposite is 內部. For the outside as a place in speech, say 外面.

column3: Rather formal, and typical on notices: 外出办事, 外出用餐. In everyday speech, "go out" is just 出去, and 他出去了 says he is out.
column4: 他今天外出了，不在办公室。
column5: 他今天外出了，不在辦公室。
column6: Tā jīntiān wàichū le, bù zài bàngōngshì.
column7: He is out today and is not in the office.
column9: Rather formal, and typical on notices: 外出辦事, 外出用餐. In everyday speech, "go out" is just 出去, and 他出去了 says he is out.

column3: The look of an object or building as a whole, its shape and finish: 外观设计, 外观很新. For a person's looks, 外表 is the usual word.
column6: Zhè liàng chē de wàiguān hěn shímáo.
column7: This car looks very stylish.
column9: The look of an object or building as a whole, its shape and finish: 外觀設計, 外觀很新. For a person's looks, 外表 is the usual word.

column3: Someone who is not in a trade and does not know its ways: 对电脑是外行. The opposite is 内行, an expert, and 外行话 is talk that shows you do not know the subject. Here 行 is read háng, and means a line of business.
column6: Wǒ duì diànnǎo shì wàiháng.
column7: I am a layman when it comes to computers.
column9: Someone who is not in a trade and does not know its ways: 對電腦是外行. The opposite is 內行, an expert, and 外行話 is talk that shows you do not know the subject. Here 行 is read háng, and means a line of business.

column3: 科 names a department or branch of medicine: 内科 (internal medicine), 儿科 (pediatrics), 眼科 (eye care). 外科医生 is a surgeon.
column6: Tā shì yīyuàn de wàikē yīshēng.
column7: He is a surgeon at the hospital.
column9: 科 names a department or branch of medicine: 內科 (internal medicine), 兒科 (pediatrics), 眼科 (eye care). 外科醫生 is a surgeon.

column3: Those a generation or more below you in a family or a field. Its opposite is 长辈, and a senior or predecessor is 前辈. Before an elder, a speaker may call himself 晚辈, which is humble and a little old-fashioned.
column6: Tā duì wǎnbèi zǒngshì hěn qīnqiè.
column7: He is always kind to the younger ones.
column9: Those a generation or more below you in a family or a field. Its opposite is 長輩, and a senior or predecessor is 前輩. Before an elder, a speaker may call himself 晚輩, which is humble and a little old-fashioned.

column3: A formal word for a procedure or task that is wholly done, typical of announcements and reports: 准备完毕, 检查完毕. In speech, say 好了 or 完了.
column6: Zhǔnbèi wánbì, kěyǐ chūfā le.
column7: Preparations are complete and we can set off.
column9: A formal word for a procedure or task that is wholly done, typical of announcements and reports: 準備完畢, 檢查完畢. In speech, say 好了 or 完了.

column3: A more literary word than 看 for looking into the distance or toward something: 望着远方, 望向窗外. It also means to hope, as in 希望 and 失望, and to visit, as in 看望老人. It began as a person standing up and looking off into the distance, with the moon 月 added later.
column4: 他望着远方，一句话也没说。
column5: 他望著遠方，一句話也沒說。
column6: Tā wàng zhe yuǎnfāng, yī jù huà yě méi shuō.
column7: He gazed into the distance and said not a word.
column9: A more literary word than 看 for looking into the distance or toward something: 望著遠方, 望向窗外. It also means to hope, as in 希望 and 失望, and to visit, as in 看望老人. It began as a person standing up and looking off into the distance, with the moon 月 added later.

column3: The verb is 开: 开玩笑 is to joke or to tease, and 开我的玩笑 is to make fun of me. 你开玩笑吧 is "you must be kidding", and 这不是玩笑 is "this is no joke".
column6: Nǐ bié kāi wánxiào le!
column7: Stop joking!
column9: The verb is 開: 開玩笑 is to joke or to tease, and 開我的玩笑 is to make fun of me. 你開玩笑吧 is "you must be kidding", and 這不是玩笑 is "this is no joke".

column3: A verb plus its object (bend + waist), so other words fit inside: 弯下腰, 弯了弯腰. It is also how you bow: 弯腰鞠躬.
column6: Tā wānyāo jiǎn qǐ le bǐ.
column7: He bent down and picked up the pen.
column9: A verb plus its object (bend + waist), so other words fit inside: 彎下腰, 彎了彎腰. It is also how you bow: 彎腰鞠躬.

column3: Taiwan's everyday word for cooking gas and the gas supply: 瓦斯炉, 瓦斯桶, 瓦斯费, 瓦斯漏气. On the mainland, say 煤气 or 天然气.
column6: Zhǔ wán fàn jìde guān wǎsī.
column7: After cooking, remember to turn off the gas.
column9: Taiwan's everyday word for cooking gas and the gas supply: 瓦斯爐, 瓦斯桶, 瓦斯費, 瓦斯漏氣. On the mainland, say 煤氣 or 天然氣.

column3: A written negative for "has not (yet)", at home in notices and set words: 尚未, 未必, 未婚, 未来. Before a verb it says something has not happened so far; in speech use 还没 or 没有.
column6: Tā dào xiànzài hái wèi huíxìn.
column7: He has not replied even now.
column9: A written negative for "has not (yet)", at home in notices and set words: 尚未, 未必, 未婚, 未來. Before a verb it says something has not happened so far; in speech use 還沒 or 沒有.

column3: Mostly part of other words: 尾巴 for an animal's tail, 结尾 for an ending, 年尾 for the end of the year. As a measure word it counts fish, though 条 is the usual one in speech: 一尾鱼.
column6: Nà zhī gǒu yīzhí yáo zhe wěi ba.
column7: That dog keeps wagging its tail.
column9: Mostly part of other words: 尾巴 for an animal's tail, 結尾 for an ending, 年尾 for the end of the year. As a measure word it counts fish, though 條 is the usual one in speech: 一尾魚.

column3: The written form of 为什么, put before the verb: 为何如此, 为何不. It sounds serious or literary, and fits speeches and formal questions better than a chat.
column6: Nǐ wèihé bù zǎodiǎn gàosù wǒ?
column7: Why didn't you tell me sooner?
column9: The written form of 為什麼, put before the verb: 為何如此, 為何不. It sounds serious or literary, and fits speeches and formal questions better than a chat.

column3: Marital status on forms and in description, set against 已婚. It means not yet married, not "never will". A man's 未婚妻 is his fiancée, and a woman's 未婚夫 her fiancé. For "single" in speech, 单身 is more usual.
column6: Tā hái wèihūn, yī ge rén zhù.
column7: She is still unmarried and lives alone.
column9: Marital status on forms and in description, set against 已婚. It means not yet married, not "never will". A man's 未婚妻 is his fiancée, and a woman's 未婚夫 her fiancé. For "single" in speech, 單身 is more usual.

column3: Goes with 经济 and 金融 in the news, and with verbs for facing or solving one: 面临危机, 化解危机, 危机处理.
column6: Gōngsī zhèng miànlín yī chǎng wēijī.
column7: The company is facing a crisis.
column9: Goes with 經濟 and 金融 in the news, and with verbs for facing or solving one: 面臨危機, 化解危機, 危機處理.

column3: A kitchen seasoning, white crystals added to savory dishes. Restaurants may advertise 不加味精, and 鸡精 is a similar chicken-flavored seasoning.
column4: 做菜时不一定要放味精。
column5: 做菜時不一定要放味精。
column6: Zuò cài shí bù yīdìng yào fàng wèijīng.
column7: You do not always have to add MSG when cooking.
column9: A kitchen seasoning, white crystals added to savory dishes. Restaurants may advertise 不加味精, and 雞精 is a similar chicken-flavored seasoning.

column3: It works as a feeling (觉得很委屈), a noun (受委屈, to be wronged) and a verb. 委屈你了 apologizes for putting someone to inconvenience, and 别委屈自己 means don't shortchange yourself.
column4: 他觉得很委屈，一句话也不想说。
column5: 他覺得很委屈，一句話也不想說。
column6: Tā juéde hěn wěiqu, yī jù huà yě bù xiǎng shuō.
column7: He felt wronged and did not want to say a word.
column9: It works as a feeling (覺得很委屈), a noun (受委屈, to be wronged) and a verb. 委屈你了 apologizes for putting someone to inconvenience, and 別委屈自己 means don't shortchange yourself.

column3: The standard, written name: 维生素C, 补充维生素. In Taiwan people also say 维他命 in speech, while on the mainland 维生素 is used in speech as well.
column4: 多吃水果可以补充维生素。
column5: 多吃水果可以補充維生素。
column6: Duō chī shuǐguǒ kěyǐ bǔchōng wéishēngsù.
column7: Eating more fruit helps you get your vitamins.
column9: The standard, written name: 維生素C, 補充維生素. In Taiwan people also say 維他命 in speech, while on the mainland 維生素 is used in speech as well.

column3: The spoken name for vitamins in Taiwan: 吃维他命, 维他命C. The characters only spell the sound of "vitamin", so 他 and 命 add no meaning. On the mainland the word is 维生素, also in speech.
column6: Wǒ měitiān chī yī kē wéitāmìng.
column7: I take one vitamin every day.
column9: The spoken name for vitamins in Taiwan: 吃維他命, 維他命C. The characters only spell the sound of "vitamin", so 他 and 命 add no meaning. On the mainland the word is 維生素, also in speech.

column3: Works as a verb with a person as object (威胁别人), in the passive (受到威胁), and as a noun (一种威胁). What is threatened can be a thing: 威胁健康, 威胁生命.
column4: 他威胁要把这件事说出去。
column5: 他威脅要把這件事說出去。
column6: Tā wēixié yào bǎ zhè jiàn shì shuō chūqù.
column7: He threatened to tell people about this.
column9: Works as a verb with a person as object (威脅別人), in the passive (受到威脅), and as a noun (一種威脅). What is threatened can be a thing: 威脅健康, 威脅生命.

column3: The person; the body a member sits on is the 委员会: 评审委员 is a member of a judging panel. In Taiwan 立法委员 is a legislator; on the mainland the legislature has 人大代表.
column4: 这位委员提出了不同的看法。
column5: 這位委員提出了不同的看法。
column6: Zhè wèi wěiyuán tíchū le bù tóng de kànfǎ.
column7: This committee member raised a different view.
column9: The person; the body a member sits on is the 委員會: 評審委員 is a member of a judging panel. In Taiwan 立法委員 is a legislator; on the mainland the legislature has 人大代表.

column3: More written and romantic than 亲, which is what people say in speech (亲一下). 吻 appears in 一个吻, 飞吻 (blow a kiss) and 吻别 (kiss goodbye).
column4: 他在她的脸上吻了一下。
column5: 他在她的臉上吻了一下。
column6: Tā zài tā de liǎn shàng wěn le yīxià.
column7: He gave her a kiss on the cheek.
column9: More written and romantic than 親, which is what people say in speech (親一下). 吻 appears in 一個吻, 飛吻 (blow a kiss) and 吻別 (kiss goodbye).

column3: As a verb it is to warm up gently, in the kitchen: 温一下, 温酒. As an adjective it is warm, not hot: 温水. It is also in 温度, 气温, 体温, 温柔, and means to review a lesson in 温习.
column6: Bǎ niúnǎi wēn yīxià zài hē.
column7: Warm the milk up a little before drinking it.
column9: As a verb it is to warm up gently, in the kitchen: 溫一下, 溫酒. As an adjective it is warm, not hot: 溫水. It is also in 溫度, 氣溫, 體溫, 溫柔, and means to review a lesson in 溫習.

column3: Stationery as a group: 文具店, 文具用品. The 具 is the same "tool" as in 工具 and 玩具.
column4: 开学前，我们去文具店买笔和本子。
column5: 開學前，我們去文具店買筆和本子。
column6: Kāixué qián, wǒmen qù wénjù diàn mǎi bǐ hé běnzi.
column7: Before school starts, we go to the stationery shop to buy pens and notebooks.
column9: Stationery as a group: 文具店, 文具用品. The 具 is the same "tool" as in 工具 and 玩具.

column3: The diploma as proof of schooling that employers look at: 大学文凭, 拿到文凭. The certificate itself is a 毕业证书, and 学历 is the level of education. Articles like to say 文凭不等于能力.
column4: 有了文凭，比较容易找工作。
column5: 有了文憑，比較容易找工作。
column6: Yǒu le wénpíng, bǐjiào róngyì zhǎo gōngzuò.
column7: With a diploma, it is easier to find work.
column9: The diploma as proof of schooling that employers look at: 大學文憑, 拿到文憑. The certificate itself is a 畢業證書, and 學歷 is the level of education. Articles like to say 文憑不等於能力.

column3: Objects from the past kept for their history, counted as a group: 出土文物, 保护文物, 博物馆里的文物. One item is 一件文物.
column4: 博物馆里有很多古代文物。
column5: 博物館裡有很多古代文物。
column6: Bówùguǎn lǐ yǒu hěn duō gǔdài wénwù.
column7: There are many ancient relics in the museum.
column9: Objects from the past kept for their history, counted as a group: 出土文物, 保護文物, 博物館裡的文物. One item is 一件文物.

column3: A written prohibition, put before the verb on signs and notices: 请勿吸烟, 请勿打扰, 切勿 (be sure not to). In conversation say 不要 or 别.
column6: Qǐng wù xīyān.
column7: No smoking, please.
column9: A written prohibition, put before the verb on signs and notices: 請勿吸煙, 請勿打擾, 切勿 (be sure not to). In conversation say 不要 or 別.

column3: Before a verb it means "by mistake": 误把盐当成糖, 误入, 误食. Otherwise it is met in compounds: 错误, 误会 (a misunderstanding), 耽误 (to delay), 误点.
column6: Tā wù bǎ yán dàngchéng le táng.
column7: He mistook the salt for sugar.
column9: Before a verb it means "by mistake": 誤把鹽當成糖, 誤入, 誤食. Otherwise it is met in compounds: 錯誤, 誤會 (a misunderstanding), 耽誤 (to delay), 誤點.

column3: Weather reports say 起雾 and 大雾; thick fog is 浓雾, light mist 雾气. 雾霾 is the smog heard about in air-quality news.
column4: 今天早上有大雾，路上要小心。
column5: 今天早上有大霧，路上要小心。
column6: Jīntiān zǎoshang yǒu dà wù, lùshàng yào xiǎoxīn.
column7: There is heavy fog this morning, so be careful on the road.
column9: Weather reports say 起霧 and 大霧; thick fog is 濃霧, light mist 霧氣. 霧霾 is the smog heard about in air-quality news.

column3: Dance as an art or a school subject: 学舞蹈, 舞蹈老师. The everyday verb for dancing is 跳舞.
column6: Tā cóngxiǎo jiù xué wǔdǎo.
column7: She has studied dance since she was little.
column9: Dance as an art or a school subject: 學舞蹈, 舞蹈老師. The everyday verb for dancing is 跳舞.

column3: The usual word in Taiwan for trains, flights and buses running late; on the mainland 晚点 is the standard word. Its opposite is 准点. For a person being late, say 迟到.
column6: Huǒchē yòu wùdiǎn le.
column7: The train is late again.
column9: The usual word in Taiwan for trains, flights and buses running late; on the mainland 晚點 is the standard word. Its opposite is 準點. For a person being late, say 遲到.

column3: Describes how someone does something, usually with 地: 无可奈何地说. It also modifies a noun: 无可奈何的事. The short form 无奈 can join clauses as "but unfortunately": 想去，无奈没时间.
column4: 他无可奈何地点了点头。
column5: 他無可奈何地點了點頭。
column6: Tā wúkěnàihé de diǎn le diǎntóu.
column7: He nodded, having no alternative.
column9: Describes how someone does something, usually with 地: 無可奈何地說. It also modifies a noun: 無可奈何的事. The short form 無奈 can join clauses as "but unfortunately": 想去，無奈沒時間.

column3: The school subject and science: 物理课, 物理老师. As "physical" it is set against chemical or mental: 物理现象, 物理变化, 物理治疗 (physical therapy).
column6: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan shàng wùlǐ kè.
column7: I like physics class best.
column9: The school subject and science: 物理課, 物理老師. As "physical" it is set against chemical or mental: 物理現象, 物理變化, 物理治療 (physical therapy).

column3: Said of people (无情的人) and of forces with no mercy: 无情的岁月, 无情的战争. The opposites are 多情 and 有情, and 无情无义 adds that there is no loyalty either.
column6: Tā duì wǒ hěn wúqíng.
column7: He is heartless toward me.
column9: Said of people (無情的人) and of forces with no mercy: 無情的歲月, 無情的戰爭. The opposites are 多情 and 有情, and 無情無義 adds that there is no loyalty either.

column3: A hall for social dancing, which sounds old-fashioned today; a modern club is 夜店. The 厅 is the same as in 客厅 and 餐厅.
column4: 他们周末常去舞厅跳舞。
column5: 他們週末常去舞廳跳舞。
column6: Tāmen zhōumò cháng qù wǔtīng tiàowǔ.
column7: They often go dancing at the dance hall on weekends.
column9: A hall for social dancing, which sounds old-fashioned today; a modern club is 夜店. The 廳 is the same as in 客廳 and 餐廳.

column3: Two uses: "accidentally", as in 无意中 and 无意间, and "have no wish to" before a verb: 我无意伤害你. It is more written than 不想 or 没打算.
column6: Wǒ wúyì shānghài nǐ.
column7: I had no intention of hurting you.
column9: Two uses: "accidentally", as in 無意中 and 無意間, and "have no wish to" before a verb: 我無意傷害你. It is more written than 不想 or 沒打算.

column3: In speech it also means doing something blindly, without a plan or point: 瞎说 (talk nonsense), 瞎忙 (busy for nothing), 瞎猜 (guess wildly). The physical sense is 瞎了一只眼.
column6: Tā de yī zhī yǎnjing xiā le.
column7: He is blind in one eye.
column9: In speech it also means doing something blindly, without a plan or point: 瞎說 (talk nonsense), 瞎忙 (busy for nothing), 瞎猜 (guess wildly). The physical sense is 瞎了一隻眼.

column3: Said alone (吃虾) or in compounds: 虾仁 (shelled shrimp), 虾饺 (shrimp dumpling), 大虾 (a big prawn), 龙虾 (lobster).
column6: Wǒ zuì ài chī xiā.
column7: I love eating shrimp most.
column9: Said alone (吃蝦) or in compounds: 蝦仁 (shelled shrimp), 蝦餃 (shrimp dumpling), 大蝦 (a big prawn), 龍蝦 (lobster).

column3: A spoken word for the animal in Taiwan, with 子 added as in 桌子 and 椅子; on the mainland 虾 alone is the usual form, as in 虾仁 and 虾饺.
column6: Xiāzi yào zhǔ shú le cái hǎochī.
column7: Shrimp are only tasty once they are well cooked.
column9: A spoken word for the animal in Taiwan, with 子 added as in 桌子 and 椅子; on the mainland 蝦 alone is the usual form, as in 蝦仁 and 蝦餃.

column3: Covers both the chin and the lower jaw: 摸下巴, 双下巴 (double chin), and 惊讶得下巴都掉了 (so shocked the jaw dropped).
column6: Tā de xiàba shàng yǒu yī kē zhì.
column7: He has a mole on his chin.
column9: Covers both the chin and the lower jaw: 摸下巴, 雙下巴 (double chin), and 驚訝得下巴都掉了 (so shocked the jaw dropped).

column3: Casual Taiwan slang for "what", from Taiwanese Hokkien, said where Mandarin has 什幺 (on the mainland 什幺 or 啥). The characters only spell the sound; the same word is also small dried shrimp. Keep it for friends, not formal speech.
column6: Nǐ gāngcái shuō xiāmǐ?
column7: What did you say just now?
column9: Casual Taiwan slang for "what", from Taiwanese Hokkien, said where Mandarin has 什么 (on the mainland 什么 or 啥). The characters only spell the sound; the same word is also small dried shrimp. Keep it for friends, not formal speech.

column3: The thing that bothers you follows directly, with no 很: 嫌贵, 嫌麻烦, 嫌小. 嫌弃 is to turn something or someone away with disdain, and 嫌疑 is suspicion, as in 嫌疑人.
column6: Tā xián zhège fángjiān tài xiǎo.
column7: He finds this room too small.
column9: The thing that bothers you follows directly, with no 很: 嫌貴, 嫌麻煩, 嫌小. 嫌棄 is to turn something or someone away with disdain, and 嫌疑 is suspicion, as in 嫌疑人.

column3: On its own it is written style: 现已退休, 现任 (the current holder). In words it means current: 现金 (cash), 现状, 现场, and appear in 出现 and 发现.
column6: Tā xiàn yǐ tuìxiū, zhù zài xiāngxià.
column7: He has now retired and lives in the countryside.
column9: On its own it is written style: 現已退休, 現任 (the current holder). In words it means current: 現金 (cash), 現狀, 現場, and appear in 出現 and 發現.

column3: Stresses that the work is already done or the thing is already on hand, so nothing more is needed. It usually follows 有 or takes 的: 现成的饭菜, 现成的办法.
column6: Bīngxiāng lǐ yǒu xiànchéng de fàncài.
column7: There is ready-made food in the fridge.
column9: Stresses that the work is already done or the thing is already on hand, so nothing more is needed. It usually follows 有 or takes 的: 現成的飯菜, 現成的辦法.

column3: Each other, before a verb, in words like 相信 "believe", 相爱 "love each other", 相同 "the same", 互相 "mutually". It is bound, so it is not used alone; it shows the action goes both ways. A different 相 is read xiàng "appearance" (相片, 照相). 木 "tree" and 目 "eye": an eye looking at a tree.
column6: Tāmen xiāng'ài le, juédìng jiéhūn.
column7: They fell in love and decided to marry.
column9: Each other, before a verb, in words like 相信 "believe", 相愛 "love each other", 相同 "the same", 互相 "mutually". It is bound, so it is not used alone; it shows the action goes both ways. A different 相 is read xiàng "appearance" (相片, 照相). 木 "tree" and 目 "eye": an eye looking at a tree.

column3: A lane or alley, the narrow street that runs off a larger one: 小巷 "small lane", 巷口 "the mouth of the lane". In Taiwan's addresses a 巷 comes after the road and before the 弄 and the number: 中山路二段十巷. 巷子 is the spoken word. In 巷, 共 gives the sound (xiàng, gòng).
column6: Wǒ jiā jiù zài zhè tiáo xiàng lǐ.
column7: My home is right in this lane.
column9: A lane or alley, the narrow street that runs off a larger one: 小巷 "small lane", 巷口 "the mouth of the lane". In Taiwan's addresses a 巷 comes after the road and before the 弄 and the number: 中山路二段十巷. 巷子 is the spoken word. In 巷, 共 gives the sound (xiàng, gòng).

column3: An alley or small lane, the spoken word for 巷: 小巷子 "a small alley", 巷子里的小吃店 "the snack shop in the alley". 巷 + 子, with 子 as the usual noun ending, neutral here. Classifier: 条.
column6: Nà jiā xiǎochīdiàn zài xiàngzi lǐ.
column7: That snack shop is in the alley.
column9: An alley or small lane, the spoken word for 巷: 小巷子 "a small alley", 巷子裡的小吃店 "the snack shop in the alley". 巷 + 子, with 子 as the usual noun ending, neutral here. Classifier: 條.

column3: Elephant: 大象 "elephant", 象鼻 "trunk", 象牙 "ivory". The character began as a picture of an elephant with its trunk and legs. The same 象 is in 印象 "impression", 现象 "phenomenon" and 形象 "image", where it means "appearance, shape". The animal itself is usually 大象.
column6: Dòngwùyuán lǐ yǒu yī tóu dàxiàng.
column7: There is an elephant in the zoo.
column9: Elephant: 大象 "elephant", 象鼻 "trunk", 象牙 "ivory". The character began as a picture of an elephant with its trunk and legs. The same 象 is in 印象 "impression", 現象 "phenomenon" and 形象 "image", where it means "appearance, shape". The animal itself is usually 大象.

column3: Unexpected, who would have thought: 想不到你也来了 "I never thought you would come too". It starts the sentence and shows surprise at something that has happened. 想 "think" + 不到 "not reach", so it is a thought that did not reach that result. The 不 in the middle is neutral in the dictionary's reading: xiǎngbudào. 没想到 means the same and is as common.
column6: Xiǎngbudào nǐ yě lái le!
column7: I never thought you would come too!
column9: Unexpected, who would have thought: 想不到你也來了 "I never thought you would come too". It starts the sentence and shows surprise at something that has happened. 想 "think" + 不到 "not reach", so it is a thought that did not reach that result. The 不 in the middle is neutral in the dictionary's reading: xiǎngbudào. 沒想到 means the same and is as common.

column3: Always, all along, about a habit or a past that goes on until now: 他向来很准时 "he is always punctual", 向来如此 "it has always been so". It goes before the verb and often comes with 都. It is a bit more written than 一直 and is used for a fixed trait, not for something that went on without a break.
column6: Tā xiànglái hěn zhǔnshí.
column7: He has always been punctual.
column9: Always, all along, about a habit or a past that goes on until now: 他向來很準時 "he is always punctual", 向來如此 "it has always been so". It goes before the verb and often comes with 都. It is a bit more written than 一直 and is used for a fixed trait, not for something that went on without a break.

column3: A meeting set up to see whether two people suit each other as marriage partners, a blind date arranged by family or friends: 去相亲 "go on a date to meet", 相亲对象 "the person one is introduced to". In Taiwan it is read xiàngqīn, the mainland xiāngqīn. 相 here means "to look at", as in 相片.
column6: Tā xià ge xīngqī yào qù xiāngqīn.
column7: She is going on a blind date next week.
column9: A meeting set up to see whether two people suit each other as marriage partners, a blind date arranged by family or friends: 去相親 "go on a date to meet", 相親對象 "the person one is introduced to". In Taiwan it is read xiàngqīn, the mainland xiāngqīn. 相 here means "to look at", as in 相片, and 親 includes 見 "see".

column3: An idiom for people who are close and warm toward one another: 相亲相爱的一家人 "a loving family", 兄弟姊妹要相亲相爱. It is used for family and friends, and puts 相 "each other" before both 亲 "be close" and 爱 "love". As a phrase it is warm and a little formal, often in wishes and in what a parent tells children.
column6: Xiōngdì jiěmèi yào xiāngqīnxiāng'ài.
column7: Brothers and sisters should love each other.
column9: An idiom for people who are close and warm toward one another: 相親相愛的一家人 "a loving family", 兄弟姊妹要相親相愛. It is used for family and friends, and puts 相 "each other" before both 親 "be close" and 愛 "love". As a phrase it is warm and a little formal, often in wishes and in what a parent tells children.

column3: To respond to a call or proposal by joining in: 响应号召 "answer the call", 响应环保 "support the environmental movement". It is a formal word often met in news about campaigns. 响 "echo, sound" + 应 "answer". 响 has 口 on its left and 向 for the sound; 应 is also the "answer" in 回应 and 反应.
column4: 很多人响应政府的号召。
column5: 很多人響應政府的號召。
column6: Hěn duō rén xiǎngyìng zhèngfǔ de hàozhào.
column7: Many people responded to the government's call.
column9: To respond to a call or proposal by joining in: 響應號召 "answer the call", 響應環保 "support the environmental movement". It is a formal word often met in news about campaigns. 響 "echo, sound" + 應 "answer". 響 has 音 "sound" below it and 鄉 for the sound; 應 is also the "answer" in 回應 and 反應.

column3: To enjoy a right, a benefit or a good thing, in a formal way: 享有权利 "enjoy rights", 享有盛名 "have a great reputation", 享有自由. It is used for things given or earned, such as rights, fame or a standard of living. Not for food or fun: that is 享受. 享 shows a shrine, a place of offerings.
column6: Gōngmín xiǎngyǒu yánlùn zìyóu.
column7: Citizens enjoy freedom of speech.
column9: To enjoy a right, a benefit or a good thing, in a formal way: 享有權利 "enjoy rights", 享有盛名 "have a great reputation", 享有自由. It is used for things given or earned, such as rights, fame or a standard of living. Not for food or fun: that is 享受. 享 shows a shrine, a place of offerings.

column3: To envy and admire someone for what they have or are: 我很羡慕你 "I really envy you", 令人羡慕 "enviable". It has no sense of hate, so it is gentler than 嫉妒. The object can be a person, a life or a talent. 羡 has 羊 "sheep" above and 慕 has 心 "heart" at its bottom: 慕 is a longing of the heart.
column4: 我很羡慕你可以去旅行。
column5: 我很羨慕你可以去旅行。
column6: Wǒ hěn xiànmù nǐ kěyǐ qù lǚxíng.
column7: I really envy you for being able to travel.
column9: To envy and admire someone for what they have or are: 我很羨慕你 "I really envy you", 令人羨慕 "enviable". It has no sense of hate, so it is gentler than 嫉妒. The object can be a person, a life or a talent. 羨 has 羊 "sheep" above and 慕 has 心 "heart" at its bottom: 慕 is a longing of the heart.

column3: Fresh milk, as sold in cartons and shops: 一瓶鲜奶 "a bottle of fresh milk", 鲜奶茶 "milk tea made with fresh milk", 鲜奶油 "cream". It sets fresh milk apart from milk powder; 牛奶 is the general word. 鲜 "fresh" has 鱼 "fish" as its meaning part.
column4: 我每天早上喝一杯鲜奶。
column5: 我每天早上喝一杯鮮奶。
column6: Wǒ měitiān zǎoshang hē yī bēi xiānnǎi.
column7: Every morning I drink a glass of fresh milk.
column9: Fresh milk, as sold in cartons and shops: 一瓶鮮奶 "a bottle of fresh milk", 鮮奶茶 "milk tea made with fresh milk", 鮮奶油 "cream". It sets fresh milk apart from milk powder; 牛奶 is the general word. 鮮 "fresh" has 魚 "fish" as its meaning part.

column3: Fresh, bright blood: 鲜血直流 "blood flowing", 鲜血淋漓 "dripping with blood". It is the word used in stories and news of injuries, where 血 alone would be plain. Not used for medicine: the words there are 血液 and 抽血. 鲜 "fresh" + 血 "blood". 血 has a dish 皿 with a drop in it.
column6: Tā de shǒu shàng liúzhe xiānxuè.
column7: Fresh blood is running from his hand.
column9: Fresh, bright blood: 鮮血直流 "blood flowing", 鮮血淋漓 "dripping with blood". It is the word used in stories and news of injuries, where 血 alone would be plain. Not used for medicine: the words there are 血液 and 抽血. 鮮 "fresh" + 血 "blood". 血 has a dish 皿 with a drop in it.

column3: To disappear, to fade, to remove: 消失 "vanish", 消除 "get rid of", 消化 "digest", 消费 "spend", 消息 "news". It is bound, as a base for many words with the sense of becoming less or vanishing. In 不消 it also means "need": 不消说 "it goes without saying". The 氵 "water" is the meaning part and 肖 gives the sound.
column6: Tòngkǔ huì mànmàn xiāoshī.
column7: The pain will slowly go away.
column9: To disappear, to fade, to remove: 消失 "vanish", 消除 "get rid of", 消化 "digest", 消費 "spend", 消息 "news". It is bound, as a base for many words with the sense of becoming less or vanishing. In 不消 it also means "need": 不消說 "it goes without saying". The 氵 "water" is the meaning part and 肖 gives the sound.

column3: Urine, and "to urinate": 小便 and 大便 are the two plain, family words; 验小便 "to test urine". It is the plain, neutral word that fits a clinic or a family talk; 尿 is the blunt word. 小 "small" + 便 "relief, convenience".
column6: Tā jízhe qù xiǎobiàn.
column7: He was in a hurry to go and pee.
column9: Urine, and "to urinate": 小便 and 大便 are the two plain, family words; 驗小便 "to test urine". It is the plain, neutral word that fits a clinic or a family talk; 尿 is the blunt word. 小 "small" + 便 "relief, convenience".

column3: A school bus: 搭校车上学 "take the school bus to school", 校车路线 "bus route". 校 "school" + 车 "vehicle". The 车 is a picture of a cart seen from above.
column4: 孩子们每天搭校车上学。
column5: 孩子們每天搭校車上學。
column6: Háizimen měitiān dā xiàochē shàngxué.
column7: The children take the school bus to school every day.
column9: A school bus: 搭校車上學 "take the school bus to school", 校車路線 "bus route". 校 "school" + 車 "vehicle". The 車 is a picture of a cart seen from above.

column3: To know, a spoken word: 我晓得 "I know", 谁晓得 "who knows", 不晓得 "do not know". It is used like 知道 and is rather colloquial or regional. 晓 means "dawn, to understand", with 日 "sun" beside 尧: the day dawning is understanding. The second syllable is neutral: xiǎode.
column6: Wǒ bù xiǎode tā zhù zài nǎlǐ.
column7: I do not know where he lives.
column9: To know, a spoken word: 我曉得 "I know", 誰曉得 "who knows", 不曉得 "do not know". It is used like 知道 and is rather colloquial or regional. 曉 means "dawn, to understand", with 日 "sun" beside 堯: the day dawning is understanding. The second syllable is neutral: xiǎode.

column3: A street peddler or small vendor: 路边的小贩 "a vendor by the road", 流动小贩 "a mobile vendor". It points to someone selling goods or snacks from a stall or a cart, with no shop. 小 "small" + 贩 "trade", where 贝 "shell, money" stands for goods and 反 gives the sound (fàn).
column6: Yèshì lǐ yǒu hěn duō xiǎofàn.
column7: There are many vendors in the night market.
column9: A street peddler or small vendor: 路邊的小販 "a vendor by the road", 流動小販 "a mobile vendor". It points to someone selling goods or snacks from a stall or a cart, with no shop. 小 "small" + 販 "trade", where 貝 "shell, money" stands for goods and 反 gives the sound (fàn).

column3: The market for a product, how well it sells: 销路很好 "sells well", 打开销路 "open up a market", 销路不佳. 销 "sell" + 路 "road, way", so it is the road along which goods travel to buyers. 销 has 钅 "metal" on the left from the older sense of melting metal. 路 has 足 "foot" for the meaning.
column6: Zhè zhǒng chǎnpǐn de xiāolù hěn hǎo.
column7: This product sells very well.
column9: The market for a product, how well it sells: 銷路很好 "sells well", 打開銷路 "open up a market", 銷路不佳. 銷 "sell" + 路 "road, way", so it is the road along which goods travel to buyers. 銷 has 釒 "metal" on the left from the older sense of melting metal. 路 has 足 "foot" for the meaning.

column3: Wheat: 小麦粉 "wheat flour", 小麦田 "wheat field". 大麦 is barley. Bread, noodles and dumpling wrappers are made from it. The character 麦 has 龶 above 夂.
column6: Miànbāo shì yòng xiǎomài zuò de.
column7: Bread is made from wheat.
column9: Wheat: 小麥粉 "wheat flour", 小麥田 "wheat field". 大麥 is barley. Bread, noodles and dumpling wrappers are made from it. The character 麥 has 來 above 夂, and 來 was once also a picture of wheat.

column3: To wipe out, to destroy completely: 消灭敌人 "wipe out the enemy", 消灭蚊子 "kill off the mosquitoes", 消灭贫穷. It is a strong word for doing away with something harmful, so that it no longer exists. 消 "melt away" + 灭 "extinguish". 灭 has 一 above 火 "fire".
column6: Wǒmen yào xiāomiè wénzi.
column7: We must wipe out the mosquitoes.
column9: To wipe out, to destroy completely: 消滅敵人 "wipe out the enemy", 消滅蚊子 "kill off the mosquitoes", 消滅貧窮. It is a strong word for doing away with something harmful, so that it no longer exists. 消 "melt away" + 滅 "extinguish". 滅 has 氵 "water" for putting out a fire, as its 烕 shows a flame.

column3: Stingy, petty, and "narrow-minded": 他很小气 "he is stingy", 小气鬼 "a miser". It may be about money, or about not letting things go. Its opposite is 大方 "generous". 小 "small" + 气 "spirit", so it is a small-spirited person.
column6: Tā hěn xiǎoqì, cónglái bù qǐngkè.
column7: He is stingy and never treats anyone.
column9: Stingy, petty, and "narrow-minded": 他很小氣 "he is stingy", 小氣鬼 "a miser". It may be about money, or about not letting things go. Its opposite is 大方 "generous". 小 "small" + 氣 "spirit", so it is a small-spirited person. 氣 has 米 "rice" inside it.

column3: A smile, an expression of smiling: 脸上带着笑容 "a smile on one's face", 露出笑容 "show a smile". The smile that is seen on a face, as against 笑 the act. 笑 "laugh" + 容 "appearance". 容 also means "hold" and shows up in 内容 and 容易.
column4: 她脸上带着温暖的笑容。
column5: 她臉上帶著溫暖的笑容。
column6: Tā liǎn shàng dàizhe wēnnuǎn de xiàoróng.
column7: She has a warm smile on her face.
column9: A smile, an expression of smiling: 臉上帶著笑容 "a smile on one's face", 露出笑容 "show a smile". The smile that is seen on a face, as against 笑 the act. 笑 "laugh" + 容 "appearance". 容 also means "hold" and shows up in 內容 and 容易.

column3: The lower leg, from knee to ankle, the calf and shin: 小腿很痠 "the calves ache", 小腿肌肉 "calf muscle". The thigh is 大腿. 腿 "leg" has ⺼ "flesh" on the left for a body part and 退 on the right for the sound, which sounds close (tuǐ, tuì).
column4: 走了一天的路，我的小腿很酸。
column5: 走了一天的路，我的小腿很痠。
column6: Zǒu le yī tiān de lù, wǒ de xiǎotuǐ hěn suān.
column7: After walking all day, my calves ache.
column9: The lower leg, from knee to ankle, the calf and shin: 小腿很痠 "the calves ache", 小腿肌肉 "calf muscle". The thigh is 大腿. 腿 "leg" has ⺼ "flesh" on the left for a body part and 退 on the right for the sound, which sounds close (tuǐ, tuì).

column3: A late-night snack, the meal eaten after dinner and before bed: 吃消夜 "have a late-night snack", 去吃消夜. It is written both 消夜 and 宵夜; they are the same word.
column4: 我们看完电影去吃消夜。
column5: 我們看完電影去吃消夜。
column6: Wǒmen kàn wán diànyǐng qù chī xiāoyè.
column7: After the movie we go for a late-night snack.
column9: A late-night snack, the meal eaten after dinner and before bed: 吃消夜 "have a late-night snack", 去吃消夜. It is written both 消夜 and 宵夜; they are the same word.

column3: A late-night snack: 吃宵夜 "have a snack late at night", 宵夜场. 宵 means "night" and has 宀 "roof" with 肖 as the sound, and 夜 is "night" too. It is the same word as 消夜, which is also seen. It is a meal taken after the evening meal.
column6: Yèshì lǐ de xiāoyè hěn hǎochī.
column7: The late-night snacks at the night market are delicious.
column9: A late-night snack: 吃宵夜 "have a snack late at night", 宵夜場. 宵 means "night" and has 宀 "roof" with 肖 as the sound, and 夜 is "night" too. It is the same word as 消夜, which is also seen. It is a meal taken after the evening meal.

column3: A schoolmate, someone from the same school: 校友会 "alumni association", 杰出校友 "an outstanding alumnus". It names a person who studied at the same school, usually after they have graduated. 校 "school" + 友 "friend". 友 is two hands 又, joined.
column4: 我们学校的校友遍布世界各地。
column5: 我們學校的校友遍布世界各地。
column6: Wǒmen xuéxiào de xiàoyǒu biànbù shìjiè gèdì.
column7: Our school's alumni are found all over the world.
column9: A schoolmate, someone from the same school: 校友會 "alumni association", 傑出校友 "an outstanding alumnus". It names a person who studied at the same school, usually after they have graduated. 校 "school" + 友 "friend". 友 is two hands 又, joined.

column3: A colloquial word for a boy or fellow, often playful or a bit disrespectful: 这小子 "this guy", 臭小子 "you little rascal", 小子 as how an older person addresses a youth. 子 is neutral in this word, xiǎozi. It is not used politely and not in writing; with strangers it could sound rude. 小 "small" + 子 "son, child".
column6: Zhè xiǎozi zhēn cōngmíng!
column7: This kid is really clever!
column9: A colloquial word for a boy or fellow, often playful or a bit disrespectful: 這小子 "this guy", 臭小子 "you little rascal", 小子 as how an older person addresses a youth. 子 is neutral in this word, xiǎozi. It is not used politely and not in writing; with strangers it could sound rude. 小 "small" + 子 "son, child".

column3: To play chess: 下象棋 "play Chinese chess", 下围棋 "play go", 下西洋棋 "play Western chess". The verb for board games is 下, not 玩 or 打: you "go down" a piece. Card games take 打 (打牌), and the board games here take 下. 棋 has 木 "wood" for the pieces, with 其 for the sound (qí, the same).
column4: 爷爷喜欢在公园里下棋。
column5: 爺爺喜歡在公園裡下棋。
column6: Yéye xǐhuān zài gōngyuán lǐ xiàqí.
column7: Grandpa likes playing chess in the park.
column9: To play chess: 下象棋 "play Chinese chess", 下圍棋 "play go", 下西洋棋 "play Western chess". The verb for board games is 下, not 玩 or 打: you "go down" a piece. Card games take 打 (打牌), and the board games here take 下. 棋 has 木 "wood" for the pieces, with 其 for the sound (qí, the same).

column3: Afternoon tea: 喝下午茶 "have afternoon tea", 下午茶时间, 下午茶套餐 "an afternoon tea set". It is a light meal of cakes, sandwiches and drinks in the afternoon, often at a cafe with friends. 下午 "afternoon" + 茶 "tea". 午 "noon" is an old picture of a pestle.
column4: 我们约好星期六一起喝下午茶。
column5: 我們約好星期六一起喝下午茶。
column6: Wǒmen yuē hǎo xīngqīliù yīqǐ hē xiàwǔchá.
column7: We have arranged to have afternoon tea together on Saturday.
column9: Afternoon tea: 喝下午茶 "have afternoon tea", 下午茶時間, 下午茶套餐 "an afternoon tea set". It is a light meal of cakes, sandwiches and drinks in the afternoon, often at a cafe with friends. 下午 "afternoon" + 茶 "tea". 午 "noon" is an old picture of a pestle.

column3: The lower reaches of a river, and in a business sense the later steps: 河的下游 "the lower part of the river", 下游厂商 "firms later in the supply chain", the reverse of 上游. 下 "down" + 游, here "reaches" of the stream. 游 has 氵 "water" and also means "swim", as in 游泳.
column4: 这条河的下游有很多村庄。
column5: 這條河的下游有很多村莊。
column6: Zhè tiáo hé de xiàyóu yǒu hěn duō cūnzhuāng.
column7: There are many villages on the lower reaches of this river.
column9: The lower reaches of a river, and in a business sense the later steps: 河的下游 "the lower part of the river", 下游廠商 "firms later in the supply chain", the reverse of 上游. 下 "down" + 游, here "reaches" of the stream. 游 has 氵 "water" and also means "swim", as in 游泳.

column3: A cell, in biology: 细胞分裂 "cell division", 脑细胞 "brain cell", 癌细胞 "cancer cell". 细 "fine, tiny" + 胞 "womb, sac". 胞 has ⺼ "flesh" and 包 "wrap" and appears in 同胞 "compatriot, born of the same mother". It is the basic unit living things are made of.
column4: 动物和植物都由细胞组成。
column5: 動物和植物都由細胞組成。
column6: Dòngwù hé zhíwù dōu yóu xìbāo zǔchéng.
column7: Animals and plants are all made of cells.
column9: A cell, in biology: 細胞分裂 "cell division", 腦細胞 "brain cell", 癌細胞 "cancer cell". 細 "fine, tiny" + 胞 "womb, sac". 胞 has ⺼ "flesh" and 包 "wrap" and appears in 同胞 "compatriot, born of the same mother". It is the basic unit living things are made of.

column3: A blood vessel, a vein or an artery: 血管破裂 "a vessel bursts", 心血管疾病 "cardiovascular disease", 血管很细. 血 "blood" + 管 "pipe". 管 has 竹 "bamboo" above it, for the pipe. Health words use it a lot: 心血管 "heart and blood vessels", 脑血管.
column6: Xuèguǎn lǐ liúdòngzhe xuèyè.
column7: Blood flows in the blood vessels.
column9: A blood vessel, a vein or an artery: 血管破裂 "a vessel bursts", 心血管疾病 "cardiovascular disease", 血管很細. 血 "blood" + 管 "pipe". 管 has 竹 "bamboo" above it, for the pipe. Health words use it a lot: 心血管 "heart and blood vessels", 腦血管.

column3: Blood type: 你是什么血型 "what is your blood type", A型, B型, O型, AB型. 血 "blood" + 型 "type, model". 型 has 土 "earth" below because it began as a mold made of clay.
column6: Nǐ shì shénme xuèxíng?
column7: What is your blood type?
column9: Blood type: 你是什麼血型 "what is your blood type", A型, B型, O型, AB型. 血 "blood" + 型 "type, model". 型 has 土 "earth" below because it began as a mold made of clay.

column3: Blood, as a bodily fluid, the technical and written word: 血液循环 "blood circulation", 血液检查 "blood test", 血液病. 血 is the plain word for blood; 血液 is used in medicine and in articles. It can also mean "lifeblood" of a business. 液 "liquid" has 氵 "water" and 夜 for the sound (yè, the same).
column6: Yīshēng yào jiǎnchá tā de xuèyè.
column7: The doctor is going to examine his blood.
column9: Blood, as a bodily fluid, the technical and written word: 血液循環 "blood circulation", 血液檢查 "blood test", 血液病. 血 is the plain word for blood; 血液 is used in medicine and in articles. It can also mean "lifeblood" of a business. 液 "liquid" has 氵 "water" and 夜 for the sound (yè, the same).

column3: A son's wife, a daughter-in-law: 娶媳妇 "take a wife for the son", 媳妇儿. The dictionary also lists "wife of a younger brother". Both characters are female 女: 妇 has 女 beside 彐, and 媳 has 息 for the sound (xī, the same). Your own 老婆 or 太太 is "wife"; this word is for your son's.
column6: Tā shì wǒ jiā de xífù.
column7: She is the wife of the son in our family.
column9: A son's wife, a daughter-in-law: 娶媳婦 "take a wife for the son", 媳婦兒. The dictionary also lists "wife of a younger brother". Both characters are female 女: 婦 has a woman with a broom 帚, and 媳 has 息 for the sound (xī, the same). Your own 老婆 or 太太 is "wife"; this word is for your son's.

column3: Wine at a wedding, and so the wedding feast: 吃喜酒 or 喝喜酒 "to go to a wedding banquet", 请你吃喜酒 "I am inviting you to my wedding". It is what you say when you tell friends of a marriage: they will be invited to drink the happy wine. 喜 "joy" + 酒 "alcohol". 酒 has the water 氵 and a jar 酉.
column4: 下个月我们请你吃喜酒。
column5: 下個月我們請你吃喜酒。
column6: Xià ge yuè wǒmen qǐng nǐ chī xǐjiǔ.
column7: Next month we will invite you to our wedding feast.
column9: Wine at a wedding, and so the wedding feast: 吃喜酒 or 喝喜酒 "to go to a wedding banquet", 請你吃喜酒 "I am inviting you to my wedding". It is what you say when you tell friends of a marriage: they will be invited to drink the happy wine. 喜 "joy" + 酒 "alcohol". 酒 has the water 氵 and a jar 酉.

column3: Bacteria, germs: 细菌感染 "bacterial infection", 杀死细菌 "kill bacteria", 有益的细菌. 细 "tiny" + 菌 "fungus, microbe". 菌 has 艹 "plant" above, and the word 菌 alone also means "mushroom, fungus". 病毒 is a virus, a different thing from 细菌.
column4: 手上有很多细菌，吃饭前要洗手。
column5: 手上有很多細菌，吃飯前要洗手。
column6: Shǒu shàng yǒu hěn duō xìjūn, chīfàn qián yào xǐshǒu.
column7: There are many germs on your hands, so wash them before eating.
column9: Bacteria, germs: 細菌感染 "bacterial infection", 殺死細菌 "kill bacteria", 有益的細菌. 細 "tiny" + 菌 "fungus, microbe". 菌 has 艹 "plant" above, and the word 菌 alone also means "mushroom, fungus". 病毒 is a virus, a different thing from 細菌.

column3: The itinerary or schedule of a trip, and the distance travelled: 行程表 "itinerary", 安排行程 "arrange the schedule", 今天的行程 "today's plans". It is about the plan for a trip and also for a busy day of a person. 行 is read xíng here, "to travel", and 程 "distance, course".
column4: 旅行社帮我们安排了行程。
column5: 旅行社幫我們安排了行程。
column6: Lǚxíngshè bāng wǒmen ānpái le xíngchéng.
column7: The travel agency has arranged the itinerary for us.
column9: The itinerary or schedule of a trip, and the distance travelled: 行程表 "itinerary", 安排行程 "arrange the schedule", 今天的行程 "today's plans". It is about the plan for a trip and also for a busy day of a person. 行 is read xíng here, "to travel", and 程 "distance, course".
